how do i do a 180 off a small jump? keep landing and catching my edge

Catching an edge on a 180 usually means you're landing on a tilted board, so focus on landing flat and centered with your weight stacked over both feet. Start the rotation with your shoulders before takeoff instead of throwing it in the air, and spot your landing over your lead shoulder. Practice ground 180s on a gentle green run until switch riding feels natural, because a shaky switch landing is often the real culprit.
I coughed up a little pink stuff after a deep dive. Normal?

No, that's a sign of lung squeeze, or pulmonary barotrauma, and you should stop diving. See a doctor promptly, especially if you have chest pain, shortness of breath or continued coughing up blood. Even if it settles, take a real break and don't dive back to that depth until you've been cleared. Work on flexibility and slower progression with an instructor.
Teenage son and his mates keep jumping off a pier into the sea. Should I be worried?

It's worth a calm conversation, because tombstoning causes serious spinal injuries and drownings every year. Water depth changes with the tide and hidden rocks or debris can sit just under the surface, while cold shock on impact can leave even strong swimmers gasping. If they love jumping, point them towards a coasteering company or a supervised venue, where guides check depths and conditions properly. That way they keep the thrill without the gamble.
worried about my 17 yo son going on a bungee trip with friends abroad. how do i check the place is legit

Ask him for the operator's name, then look at how long they've been running, check recent reviews that mention safety, and see whether they follow recognized standards. Many countries have a bungee code or adventure tourism certification. Since he's under 18, the operator will probably need your signed consent, which gives you a natural chance to vet them first. If they don't ask for parental consent at all, take that as a warning sign.
Crashed my paraglider on landing two days ago, neck stiff and I've got some tingling in my hand. Probably just whiplash right?

Maybe, but tingling in the hand after a crash means something may be irritating a nerve or there could be a neck injury. That needs medical assessment today, not self-diagnosis. Go to urgent care or the ER. Go immediately if you have weakness, worsening numbness, or trouble with balance or bladder. Don't fly until you're cleared, since you need full neck mobility and reliable hands on the brakes.
Going to Victoria Falls next month. Worth doing the bridge bungee?

It's one of the most spectacular jumps in the world, about 111 meters over the Zambezi gorge, and it's run by an experienced commercial operation. Expect a long, intense free fall followed by being winched back up. Check whether your visa lets you cross onto the bridge, and book through the established operator rather than an unofficial reseller.
can you kayak alone on class I if you're careful

Class I solo is a lot more reasonable than solo whitewater, but careful doesn't cover everything. Wear your PFD, dress for the water temperature, carry a whistle and a phone in a dry case, and tell someone your put-in, take-out and return time. Keep an eye out for strainers, which can show up even on gentle water.
What's the deal with diving after drinking? like a couple beers the night before?

A couple of beers the night before, followed by a good sleep and plenty of water, is usually fine. Drinking close to a dive, or a heavy night that leaves you hungover, is a different story, since dehydration and impaired judgment raise your risk of DCS and mistakes. Never drink between dives, and save the drinks for after your last dive of the day.
I'm 42 and want to learn to skate. Too old? Worried about breaking something since I don't bounce like I used to

42 is a perfectly good age to learn, and plenty of adults start in their 40s and 50s, but your instinct about recovery time is right, so build in some extra protection. Wear a helmet, wrist guards, and knee and elbow pads, and consider padded impact shorts, because hip and tailbone falls are common for adults. Start on a wider, stable board with softer wheels and learn pushing, turning and stopping before you try any tricks. An adult beginner lesson or session at a skate shop can save you a lot of trial-and-error falls.
I'm 14 and my parents don't know I've been riding my friend's bike in the woods without gear

The no-gear part is the real problem, because even a slow tip-over in the woods can mean a head injury, and trees don't forgive anything. At minimum you need a helmet, boots, goggles and gloves before you ride again. I'd tell your parents too. A lot of parents respond better than you'd expect when you show you're serious about doing it safely, and they might help you get proper gear or riding lessons. Riding behind their back with no gear is how a fun hobby turns into a hospital trip nobody saw coming.
Why are low head dams so dangerous? Look tiny.

Low head dams create a uniform hydraulic across the whole river, so there's no weak spot to escape from, and the backwash can hold boats and swimmers for a long time. Their small size fools people, which is why they've earned the nickname 'drowning machines.' Always portage them, and stay well back from the boil line below.
how do i get rid of speed wobbles on downhill

Speed wobbles usually come from tension and loose trucks, so start by tightening your trucks a bit and moving your weight more onto your front foot. Bend your knees, relax, and look ahead instead of down, because stiff legs make the wobble worse. Most importantly, stay at speeds you can control and practice slowing down by carving or sliding, and always wear a helmet and gloves on hills.
longboard or regular skateboard for getting to campus

For commuting, a cruiser or small longboard with soft wheels around 78a to 83a will be much smoother and faster over cracks than a standard popsicle deck. A full-size longboard is the most stable but annoying to carry into class, so something in the 30 to 36 inch range is a nice middle ground. Get comfortable footbraking before you ride in traffic or on campus hills.
how do I know how fast to go into a jump

Watch a few riders who seem in control and note where they start their run-in and whether they speed check. Your goal is to land on the downslope of the landing, not the flat knuckle and definitely not past the landing. Start with a few cautious hits where you deliberately come in slower and roll the knuckle, then add speed gradually. Overshooting is usually worse than undershooting on bigger jumps, so build up rather than guessing high.
Can I climb a frozen waterfall that I found on a hike? Never seen anyone on it.

Be very cautious with unclimbed or unknown ice. Without local knowledge you don't know how thick it is, whether water's flowing behind it, or how stable it is from season to season. You'd also need to check access rules and avalanche or rockfall hazards above. If you want to explore new routes, do it with an experienced partner or a guide who can judge the ice, rather than as your first adventure.
Dropzone says I need a coach for my first flight but I watched like 30 hours of tutorials. Fine to skip?

No, take the coached course. Videos can't watch your body position in the air, correct your exit, or tell you why your opening was off-heading. The First Flight Course also gets you briefed on the dropzone's specific flight patterns and jump-run, which you need to avoid colliding with other jumpers. Your study will still help you learn faster with a coach.
honestly what's the worst that happens if i dive a cenote cave without a light, the water is super clear

The worst case is that you die, and that has happened to plenty of people in exactly that crystal-clear water. Once you're past the daylight zone it's total darkness, and one silt-out or wrong turn leaves you blind with no way out. Stay in the cavern with a guide and lights, and leave the cave section for after real training.
how many skydives do i need before i can start wingsuit training?

The common baseline is 200 skydives within the last 18 months, and many drop zones and first flight courses won't budge on that. Those jumps build the canopy skills, altitude awareness and stability you need when a wingsuit adds a whole new layer of workload. Some places use slightly different rules, but treat 200 as a minimum and get there with solid, varied jumps rather than rushing the count.
Haven't dived in 4 years. Booking a liveaboard next month. Need a refresher?

Yes, do one before the trip. After four years, skills like buoyancy control, mask clearing and buddy air-sharing fade, and a liveaboard often means back-to-back days at deeper, current-prone sites. A half-day refresher at a local shop or in the pool is cheap insurance and will make the trip much more enjoyable.
First time leading WI3 tomorrow, any tips??

Place screws early and often, especially low down, because falling with crampons on is how ankles and legs get broken. The old rule that the leader must not fall still holds on ice, so climb well within your limits and back off if you feel pumped or shaky. Rest on good feet, get a screw in before the steep sections, and plan your rests rather than pushing through. Ideally you've already led a couple of easier WI2 pitches or done some mock leads on toprope, and if not, think about starting there instead.
Had a bad landing last jump and twisted my ankle. Kind of swollen but I wanna jump again this weekend.

Get it looked at before you go up, because landing on a weak or partly fractured ankle can turn a minor injury into a serious one. If a doctor clears it, wait until you can run and jump on it without pain, since landings load the ankle hard. Also ask a coach to review that landing so you fix the cause, not just the ankle.
is it really that bad to skip the partner check if i've been climbing for years

Yes, because experienced climbers have died from simple oversights like unfinished knots or unlocked belay devices, and familiarity is exactly what makes those mistakes easy to miss. A partner check takes about ten seconds and covers harness buckles, knot, belay device, carabiner lock, and the rope end knot. Make it automatic and it will never slow you down.
My girlfriend wants to try downhill but she's nervous. How do I help without pushing her?

The best move is often booking her a beginner lesson with a coach rather than teaching her yourself, because couples' coaching sessions tend to get tense. Let her pick the trails and the pace, start on green flow trails, and make sure her rental gear fits properly. Praise her progress and never suggest 'just one harder run'; she'll come back if the first day feels fun and in control.
Wet exit freaks me out, I hate being upside down. Can I skip learning it?

No. The wet exit is the one skill you have to have, because it's how you get out if you flip and can't roll. The fear is extremely common and fades fast with practice in a warm pool with an instructor standing beside you. Start without the sprayskirt, then with it loosely on, and you'll be surprised how quickly it becomes calm and automatic.
Worried about my first steep rock roll. Tips?

Before you ride it, walk it and pick your line plus a clear runout at the bottom. Drop your saddle, push your hips back, keep your arms long and stay off the front brake as the bike tips over the edge. Use steady, gentle braking rather than grabbing, and let the bike roll. If it still feels wrong after you've looked at it, skip it today, because hesitating halfway down is the worst outcome.
Do airbag packs actually make you safe enough to ski steeper stuff?

Airbags do improve survival odds by helping keep you near the surface, but they don't prevent trauma from rocks or trees or deep burial in a terrain trap. Studies also show people take more risk once they're wearing one, which cancels out the benefit. Think of it as a last-ditch backup that doesn't change which slopes you should be skiing.
what bearings are best for downhill skating

Downhill riders favor quality skate bearings rated ABEC 7 or higher, though the brand and materials matter more than the ABEC number. Ceramic or high-grade steel bearings with good shields resist heat and dirt at speed. Keep them clean and lubricated so they stay smooth and reliable.
My 17 year old son wants to go ski touring with his friends this weekend and none of them have taken an avalanche course. Should I be worried?

Yes, it's reasonable to be concerned, but you don't have to say a flat no. A good middle ground is to have them stick to low-angle terrain under 30 degrees with nothing steeper above or beside it, or to resort uphill routes that stay inside patrolled boundaries. Longer term, an AIARE 1 or equivalent course is the best gift you could give him, and many programs offer youth-specific versions. Also make sure each of them carries a beacon, shovel and probe and knows how to use them.
Just did my first jump and my eyes are bloodshot and I have a headache. Normal?

Minor red patches from tiny burst vessels in the eyes are a known side effect, especially after ankle-attached jumps, and they usually clear on their own within a week or two. A mild headache can also happen from the pressure change and adrenaline. But if you notice any change in vision, a severe or worsening headache, confusion, or neck pain, see a doctor promptly. Those aren't things to wait out.
Is it OK to drink a couple beers before a mellow river run?

I'd hold off until you're off the river. Even a couple of drinks slows reactions, impairs balance and judgment, and speeds up hypothermia, and alcohol plays a role in a lot of river drownings, even on easy water. Save the beers for the takeout, where they taste better anyway.
how much does a tandem jump cost roughly

In the US a tandem usually runs about $200 to $350, and Europe, the UK and Australia are in a similar range in local currency. Photos or video from a dedicated camera flyer typically add $100 to $150. Be wary of prices that seem much cheaper than everywhere else nearby, and check that the dropzone is affiliated with a national body like the USPA or British Skydiving.
What wind speed is too much for BASE?

There's no single number, but many jumpers set conservative limits of about 10 to 15 mph for an open landing area, and much lower for tight sites or anything near the object. Turbulence and direction matter as much as speed, because rotors near cliffs and buildings can collapse or turn a canopy. If you can't read the wind confidently, or it's gusting, don't jump. Walking away is a normal part of BASE.
how fast do you fall in freefall

In a stable belly-to-earth position you hit terminal velocity of about 120 mph, or 190 km/h, within roughly 10 to 12 seconds. Tandems fall at a similar speed because they use a drogue chute to slow the pair down. Head-down freeflyers can go 150 to 200 mph or more.
is it legal to downhill skate on public roads

It varies a lot by location. Some cities ban skateboarding on certain roads or at night, while others have specific rules about speed or helmets. Check your local laws, because even where it's technically legal, riding open roads with traffic is risky. Closed-road events or permitted sessions are the safest way to ride fast.
I want to hitch a ride up the hill holding onto a car bumper like in the old videos lol

Don't, because skitching is one of the ways riders actually die. The driver can brake, turn, or hit a pothole without warning, and you have no control or escape at that speed. Walk the hill, use a car shuttle with the board inside, or join a group session where people take turns driving. The walk up is part of the sport.
what's a pilot chute and what size should i use

The pilot chute is the small parachute you throw or that comes out of the container to pull your main canopy into the air. In BASE, the size depends on your delay length and airspeed, with larger pilot chutes for short delays to get a faster, cleaner opening. Your instructor will match the pilot chute to each jump, and you shouldn't guess, because the wrong size can cause a dangerous slow or hesitant deployment.
I'm a type 1 diabetic, 32, doing Annapurna Base Camp. What should I plan for?

ABC is very doable with type 1 diabetes, but see your endocrinologist before the trip, because altitude, cold, and long hiking days can all change your insulin needs. Carry double supplies of everything, split between two bags, and keep insulin close to your body so it doesn't freeze. Also bring extra glucose and test more often than usual. Make sure your trekking partner or guide knows how to spot and treat hypoglycemia, since its symptoms can look a lot like altitude sickness.
should my 6 year old wear wrist guards or is a helmet enough

Wear both. Little kids instinctively throw their hands out when they fall, so wrist guards prevent the most common injury, and the helmet protects against the most serious one. Knee and elbow pads are worth adding too, since they let a young kid fall without getting scared off skating altogether.
how do i check water depth before jumping

Swim the exact landing zone yourself, ideally with goggles, and dive down to touch bottom or confirm you can't reach it. A rough rule is depth of at least a third of the jump height, with a 4-meter minimum even for small jumps, and more for higher ones. Check a wide area too, because people rarely land exactly where they aim. Recheck every visit, since tides, floods and fallen rocks change things.
Is a samba normal? I had one after a dive and laughed it off but my friend freaked out.

Your friend was right to take it seriously. A samba is a loss of motor control from low oxygen, and it means you were right at the edge of blacking out. Stop diving for the rest of that day, then look honestly at what caused it, like a dive that was too deep or too long, too little surface recovery, or being tired or cold. Dial your dives back a level and make sure your buddy is always close for the last few meters and the first breaths at the surface.
Water temp is 12C, I've only got a 3mm. Will I be ok for a 40 minute dive?

Probably not comfortably. At 12°C, a 3mm suit will have you shivering well before 40 minutes, and cold hurts your judgment and air consumption. Rent a 7mm with a hood and gloves, or at least add a hooded vest. If you can't get warmer gear, plan a short, shallow dive and end it as soon as you start shivering.
do i actually need a reserve parachute or is it just extra weight

Fly with a reserve, every time. It's your last line of defence if your wing suffers a collapse you can't recover from, or a mid-air collision, and plenty of pilots are alive because they threw one. Make sure it's sized for your weight, properly connected to your harness, and repacked by a qualified packer roughly every six to twelve months. Practise the throw on the ground so the motion is automatic.
how do I know if a swell is too big for me

A good test is whether you'd be comfortable getting caught inside by the biggest set of the day, swimming without a board and taking a few on the head. If the answer is no, or you're not sure you could get back in from the impact zone, it's too big. Sit in the channel and watch a few sets before you paddle in, and trust that gut feeling when it says no.
my friend broke his wrist sliding, should i be wearing wrist guards for downhill

Slide gloves with hard pucks on the palms are the standard for downhill, since they let you put a hand down and slide instead of jamming your wrist. Some riders also wear low-profile wrist guards under the gloves for extra support, which is a smart idea if you're still learning slides. The bigger factor is technique, so practice hand-down slides at low speed until putting your hand on the pavement feels natural.
honestly scared of heights but my partner loves climbing. any tips?

Start with bouldering, where you're never far off the ground, and gradually work up to top-roping a few meters at a time while your partner belays. Practicing small, controlled falls on top rope can teach your body that the system catches you. Go at your own pace, celebrate small wins, and remember plenty of climbers started out afraid of heights.
What do I do if I start getting chills in the heat?

Treat chills or goosebumps in hot conditions as a serious warning sign of overheating, not as a cue to warm up. Stop, get into shade, cool yourself with ice and water, and see the medics at the next aid station. If you feel at all confused, don't keep moving; signal for help.
What's the weight limit for bungee jumping?

It depends on the operator, but most allow roughly 40 to 45 kilograms at the low end and 120 to 150 kilograms at the top. They weigh you on site so they can pick the right cord and settings, which is a big part of what keeps the jump safe. Be honest about your weight, because understating it can lead to the wrong cord being used.
can i swim at night if i have a light

It's doable, but it's riskier, because no one on a boat or the shore can see you well and it's hard to judge where you are. If you want to try, do it with an organized group or a kayaker escort, in a small area you know well, and attach a light to both your buoy and your cap. Swimming alone at night isn't worth the risk.
Can I put my 6 year old on the back of my motocross bike for a little ride around the field?

No. Motocross bikes aren't built for passengers, and there's no place for a small kid to sit or hold on safely. Even a slow ride can turn bad if you hit a rut or the bike bucks. If your kid wants to ride, get them their own small bike with a throttle limiter and full gear, and coach them on flat ground.
Can I skate in the rain?

You can, but it's sketchy and hard on your gear. Wet pavement cuts your grip a lot, especially on painted lines and metal covers, and water rusts bearings and makes decks go soggy and lose their pop. If you have to ride, go slow and avoid tricks, then dry your bearings afterward, or better yet keep an old beater board for wet days.
I threw up twice at mile 30 in the heat. Can I just keep going and eat later?

Slow way down or sit in shade, cool off and let your stomach settle before you try to move on, because vomiting in heat is often a sign of overheating. Sip small amounts of fluid with electrolytes and try something bland like ginger chews or broth once things calm down. If you can't keep anything down for an hour, get dizzy or feel confused, check in with medical and consider dropping. Going on empty and dehydrating in the heat is a fast way to end up on an IV.
quick: snow blindness at high altitude, real thing?

Very real. The UV light up high is intense and the snow reflects it, which can burn your corneas in just a few hours, causing severe pain and temporary blindness. Wear category 4 glacier glasses with side shields, even on cloudy days, and always carry a spare pair.
whats the deal with clipless vs flats for downhill

Flat pedals are best for learning downhill. You can put a foot down instantly, and they teach good technique, because sloppy form makes your feet bounce off. Clipless pedals give more control at race pace, but unclipping takes practice and can make crashes awkward. Most riders start on quality flats with grippy shoes, and many stay on them for good.
Any point in doing tunnel time for wingsuits?

Some wind tunnels now offer wingsuit-specific sessions, and they're useful for body position and feeling how the suit responds. It won't replace real flights for navigation, exits or deployments, but it can speed up your stability and control. If you have access and budget, a few coached sessions are a solid investment.
I'm 67 and have done ultras for 20 years but this is my first one in serious heat. Anything I should do differently at my age?

Twenty years in the sport means you have the base, but older runners do sweat less, feel thirst less, and take longer to acclimate, so give yourself a longer heat block, close to three weeks. Drink on a planned schedule instead of relying on thirst, and get your doctor to look over any medications that affect fluid or heart rate. Go out conservatively, because heat amplifies the cost of an early fast pace at any age.
I'm a teenager (16), already have junior advanced open water. Can I start cave training?

Most agencies require you to be 18 for full cave training, and some allow cavern training a bit earlier with parental consent. Use the next couple of years to rack up dives and master buoyancy, trim and frog kicking, since those skills make cave training far smoother. If you find a cavern instructor who accepts minors, talk with your parents and check the instructor's track record carefully.
I'm 52 and haven't ridden since my twenties. Want to get back into motocross. Am I nuts?

Not at all, plenty of riders come back in their fifties and have a blast, but your reflexes and recovery aren't what they were, so ease in. Start on trails or a beginner track, work on fitness and flexibility for a few weeks first, and consider a riding school day to update your technique for modern bikes. Invest in good modern gear, especially a quality helmet and knee braces, because healing takes longer now.
ok honest question. if I've done all the training, is BASE actually worth the risk?

Only you can answer that. Plenty of thoughtful people choose to jump for decades, and plenty of others decide the risk doesn't make sense with the kind of life they want. It's worth asking who depends on you, what level of risk you'd accept, and whether you can hold strict limits when the pressure to progress kicks in. If you jump, do it with clear eyes and a plan, not because of momentum or ego.
whats a v-thread

A V-thread, or Abalakov, is a rappel anchor made by drilling two angled holes with an ice screw so they meet inside the ice, forming a tunnel you thread cord or webbing through. You tie the cord into a loop and rappel off it, which lets you descend without leaving gear behind. It's very strong in good, solid ice, but only as good as the ice it's built in, so drill into dense ice away from fractures. Back it up with a screw while the heavier person rappels first, then let the last climber remove the backup and go.
quickest way to get good enough for class IV??

There isn't a safe shortcut. Most people spend a couple of seasons solid on class III before stepping up, and the ones who rush it are the ones who end up in bad swims. The fastest real path is lots of river days with stronger paddlers, coaching, and a swiftwater rescue course, plus a roll that holds up when you're tired and scared. Step up one rapid at a time with experienced people setting safety below.
best wheels for a beginner downhill board?

Go for medium-size wheels around 65 to 70mm in roughly 78a to 80a duro, ideally with rounded lips, because they grip enough to feel stable but break into slides predictably. Sharp-lipped grippy race wheels are hard to slide and punish mistakes, while tiny hard wheels slip out too easily. Pair them with decent bearings and well-tuned trucks. Once your sliding is solid, you can experiment.
What color urine is 'ok' during a race?

Pale yellow is the target. Dark, concentrated urine means you're behind on fluids, and if you see cola-colored or reddish urine, stop and get medical help, since that can signal rhabdomyolysis or kidney trouble. Clear and very frequent can actually mean you're overdrinking, especially if you're not taking in enough sodium.
Dumb question but can I scuba dive with a healing cut on my foot?

Not dumb at all. An open wound and seawater can lead to nasty infections, including some serious marine bacteria. If the cut is fully closed and scabbed over with no redness or discharge, you're usually fine with a waterproof dressing and a closed-heel boot. If it's still open or deep, wait until it's sealed. Watch it closely after diving, and get any spreading redness, warmth or swelling seen quickly.
Honestly do I even need a helmet top roping ice? It's just a little practice crag.

Yes, absolutely. Ice climbing sheds a constant stream of chunks from your tools, from other climbers and from the route itself, and even small pieces can cause serious injury. Belayers need them too, since they're standing right in the fall line. It's the cheapest, easiest protection in the sport, so wear one every time.
What's the minimum amount of flights before I can go cross-country?

There's no fixed number, but most pilots spend at least 50 to 100 hours and a year or two flying before attempting real cross-country flights. You need solid thermalling skills, confident handling of turbulence, the ability to choose safe landing fields from the air, and a good grasp of airspace and meteorology. Many clubs run XC clinics or mentoring days, so learn with an experienced pilot rather than figuring it out alone.
Is it safe to surf big waves alone if the conditions are perfect?

No, big waves should never be surfed alone, no matter how perfect it looks. A hold-down or a knock to the head can leave you unconscious in seconds, and without someone watching, nobody comes to get you. Always go with experienced partners, ideally with a ski on standby and someone on the beach watching the lineup.
Can you paraglide while pregnant? I'm 10 weeks.

Most instructors and doctors advise against it. A hard landing or launch fall carries real risk of abdominal impact, and harness straps press across the area too. Talk to your doctor, but the general consensus is to stay on the ground for the pregnancy and pick it back up afterwards.
how heavy can you be to bungee

Most operators cap jumpers somewhere between 100 and 150 kg (about 220 to 330 lbs), with a minimum usually around 40 to 45 kg. Limits vary by site and cord setup, so check with the specific operator before booking. They'll weigh you on the day regardless, and that number determines which cord they use.
can I build my own luge sled from a plank and some skate trucks

You can build one, and plenty of riders do, but a homemade sled needs to be strong, flex-free and properly fitted before you take it anywhere fast. Use quality trucks, a sturdy frame, and padding for your head and body, and test it at low speed first. If you plan to race, check your racing body's equipment specs before building. Talking to experienced builders at a local club will save you a lot of trial and error.
can i just tie a climbing rope to a bridge and jump

No, and please don't. Climbing rope is built to stretch only a little, so a long free fall onto it can produce forces that cause serious internal or spinal injury, and you'd also have to get the length exactly right to avoid the ground or water. Real bungee cords are engineered elastic, sized to your weight and the drop, and rigged by people who do it every day. If you want the jump, book it with an operator.
brakes feel spongy halfway down long runs, just pump them?

Pumping is a sign of a problem, not a fix. Spongy brakes on long descents usually mean overheating, air in the lines, or worn pads, and that can lead to brake fade when you need them most. Get them bled and check pads before your next lift day, and consider bigger rotors (200 or 220mm) for downhill. In the meantime, brake hard and short before corners rather than dragging them the whole way.
should I use a penny board as my first board

It's possible, but it's not ideal. Penny-style boards are small, twitchy and easy to over-steer, which makes learning balance harder. A regular popsicle deck or a cruiser around 8 inches wide is much more stable for a beginner. If you only want to cruise short distances a penny is fine, just keep the speed low.
Whats the youngest someone free soloed El Cap?

Hardly anyone has free soloed El Cap at all. Honnold was 31 when he soloed Freerider in 2017, after more than a decade of serious climbing. It's not a record anyone should chase. Celebrate young climbers who free climb El Cap on rope, which is already an elite achievement.
Is it normal for a skydiving landing ankle injury to still hurt after 6 weeks?

Lingering pain at six weeks isn't unusual for a significant sprain, but it's worth getting checked, especially after a hard landing. Ongoing pain can point to an undiagnosed fracture, a high ankle sprain, or a cartilage injury, which X-rays sometimes miss. Ask for a sports medicine assessment, and possibly an MRI if the pain is deep, sharp or comes with clicking. Hold off on jumping until it's sorted, since PLFs load the ankle hard.
can i skydive while pregnant? like 10 weeks, nobody knows yet

No, dropzones don't allow pregnant jumpers at any stage, and with good reason. The opening shock, the harness pressure and the landing impact all carry real risks, and even a gentle tandem landing can turn into a hard one. Take a rain check and go after the baby arrives, once your doctor has cleared you.
Group trip tomorrow, one guy says he can roll but I've never seen him paddle. How worried should I be?

Somewhat, because what people claim and how they paddle often differ. Put him in the middle of the group with a strong paddler nearby and plan rescue positions at the harder rapids. Watch him on the first easy stretch to gauge his skills, and if he's struggling, have the group help him portage or take a shorter section.
I'm 42, been trad climbing 15 years, and I'm considering soloing some easy alpine ridges I know well. Thoughts?

With 15 years of trad behind you, soloing easy alpine ridges is a well-trodden path, and plenty of experienced mountaineers move unroped on familiar low-angle terrain. The real dangers there are often rockfall, loose blocks, weather turning, and fatigue on the descent rather than hard moves, so pick stable conditions and stay honest about how you feel on the day. Carry a light rope and a small rack for any sections that feel off, and let someone know your plan and turnaround time. Downclimbing anything that feels sketchy is always the right call.
What's a good weight setup for a beginner in a 3mm suit?

Weight yourself so you're neutrally buoyant at around 10 meters, or roughly 5 to 7 meters for beginners staying shallow. That way you float at the surface, which is the safety point if you black out. In a 3mm suit in saltwater, that's often only 1 to 3 kg depending on your build, so start light and adjust in small steps. Never weight yourself so you sink at the surface.
how do i get out of a rip current

Don't fight it by swimming straight back to shore, because that's what exhausts people. Float, stay calm, and either swim parallel to the beach until you're out of the pull or let it carry you out until it weakens, then swim back at an angle. If you can't make progress, float on your back and raise an arm to signal for help. Learning to spot rips from the beach before you get in, where you see calmer, darker water breaking through the waves, is the best prevention.
Quick q: should my sag be 100mm or 105mm on a KX450

Kawasaki recommends about 100 to 105mm of race sag on the KX450, so start at 102 or 103 and fine-tune from there. If the front pushes in corners, go toward 105mm, and if it's unstable at speed or headshakes, go toward 100mm. Measure it with all your gear on, and check static sag too, because that tells you whether your spring rate is right for your weight.
quick: crampons for Kilimanjaro?

Usually not. The standard routes are walking trails and the summit is normally reachable in good boots, though microspikes can come in handy on icy sections near the crater rim after fresh snow. Check with your operator before you go, since conditions vary with the season.
Can I free dive and scuba on the same day?

Freediving before scuba is generally fine. Freediving after scuba is the risky order, because breath-hold descents and fast ascents on top of the nitrogen you're already carrying can raise your decompression sickness risk. If you want to do both, freedive first, or leave a long surface interval, ideally until the next day, before freediving after tank dives.
can I jump with glasses

Usually not loose, because they'll fly off. Some operators provide a strap and others make you remove them entirely, so ask on booking. Contacts are the easiest option if you can wear them, though be aware the rush of air can dry your eyes. Leaving your glasses with a friend is fine, since you won't need sharp vision to enjoy it.
is a cheap recreational kayak fine for rapids

No, recreational kayaks lack the rocker, outfitting, flotation and strength for whitewater, and they tend to fold or pin in rapids. They also don't let you brace your knees properly, so rolling and control are nearly impossible. If budget is tight, rent a whitewater boat or look for a used one with a reputable outfitter, so you have the right gear without buying new.
Concussion snowboarding 4 days ago, headache gone, feel fine. Pow day tomorrow. Helmet on, what's the harm?

The harm is that a second impact before your brain has healed can cause far worse damage than the first, and feeling fine at day four doesn't mean you've recovered. Your helmet reduces skull injury but doesn't stop your brain from rattling inside it. The standard is a graded return over at least a week or so after symptoms clear, ideally signed off by a doctor. Let this pow day go, because there will be plenty more if you protect your head now.
griptape bubbles, how fix

Poke each bubble with a pin or the tip of a craft knife to let the air out, then press it flat firmly with a screwdriver handle or the side of a wrench. For a large area, warm it briefly with a hair dryer first so the adhesive grips again. Next time, roll the tape down from the center outward as you apply it. Small leftover bubbles are only cosmetic and won't affect your grip.
my friend wants to rap off a single screw to save gear, fine?

No, that's a terrible trade for saving a screw. Build a V-thread instead, which costs you only some cord, or use a fixed anchor if the route has one. If you're nervous about the V-thread, back it up with a screw while the first person goes down, and have the last person pull the backup. Losing gear is cheap compared to an anchor failing.
Can I fly a wingsuit in cloud?

No, flying in cloud is unsafe and usually prohibited, since you lose visual reference, separation from other jumpers and orientation. Wingsuiters cover a lot of distance, which increases the risk of losing the landing area or colliding. Wait for clear conditions and follow dropzone rules.
My 9 year old wants to start motocross. Is a 50cc too small or should I just get him a 65 so he can grow into it?

Start him on the bike that fits him now, not the one he'll fit in two years, because a kid who can't flat-foot or comfortably reach the controls will struggle to stop and won't build good habits. A 50cc is perfect for a true beginner around that age, and many kids move to a 65 within a season or two once their throttle control and braking are solid. Buy used and you'll lose very little when it's time to step up.
Can I learn to roll in a weekend? I have a trip planned in 2 weeks.

Some people get a pool roll in a weekend with good coaching, but a reliable roll in moving water usually takes much longer, so don't plan your trip around having one. Take a rolling clinic or private lesson to give yourself the best shot, and practise as much as you can in the next two weeks. For the trip itself, pick water where a swim is safe and easy, and assume you'll be swimming if you flip. Lots of good paddlers swam for their first season, so you're in good company.
How do I know if a river level is too high for me? The gauge says 4.2 ft and I've only run it at 2.5.

Nearly doubling the level you know is a big jump, and on most rivers that changes everything: faster current, bigger holes, fewer eddies and longer swims. Check American Whitewater or a local guidebook for that river's recommended range, and ask paddlers who run it regularly what 4.2 feels like. A good rule is to step up gradually, maybe half a foot at a time, with experienced people who've run it at the higher flow. If you're asking whether it's too high, today's probably not the day to find out solo.
What's the deal with strainers, do I really need to worry about them on easy rivers?

Yes. Strainers like downed trees and logjams let water through but trap people and boats, and they kill paddlers on easy, slow-looking rivers precisely because people relax there. Scan ahead on outside bends where trees tend to fall, and if you can't see a clear path around one, get out and portage. If you're swimming toward one, get aggressive, swim hard away from it, and if you can't avoid it, go at it headfirst and try to climb over the top rather than getting pulled under.
How much weight should I wear? I want to sink easily

You want to be weighted so you're positively buoyant at the surface and neutral at around 10 meters, not so heavy that you sink easily from the top. Overweighting makes the ascent harder at exactly the point where you're running low on oxygen, which raises your blackout risk. Have an instructor check your weighting in the water, since the right amount changes with your wetsuit and the salinity.
I panicked on my AFF level 3 and didn't pull until my instructor did it. Am I just not cut out for this?

Not necessarily, because freezing up on an early AFF level is more common than you'd think, and it's exactly why instructors are there. Talk it through honestly with your instructor, repeat the level if they recommend it, and practice your pull sequence on the ground until it's automatic. Some time in a wind tunnel can also help a lot by making freefall feel familiar, though if the fear keeps overriding your actions, it's fine to step back and reconsider.
18 and just got my A license. want to do a wingsuit flight on my birthday next month, there's a tandem wingsuit option right?

True tandem wingsuit jumps are rare and not a standard offering, so be wary of anywhere advertising them casually. On your own license, you'll need around 200 jumps before a wingsuit first flight course. Instead, for your birthday, book some coaching jumps, try a tracking dive or do a canopy course. They all count toward the wingsuit path and are a lot of fun.
whats the safest way to get out through big surf to the lineup

Spend at least 15 minutes watching from shore, timing the sets and finding the channel. Most big-wave spots have a deeper channel where waves don't break as hard, so paddle out through it during a lull between sets. If a set catches you inside, ditch your board only if nobody is behind you, and dive deep to get under the whitewater.
I'm 34, never climbed before, and my friends want to take me outdoor climbing this weekend. Should I go to a gym first?

A gym session or two first is a smart move, because you'll learn to tie a figure-eight follow-through, how belaying works, and how your body moves on rock without the extra variables of weather and approach hikes. That said, going outside with experienced friends on easy top-rope routes is a classic way to start, as long as someone competent checks your knot and harness every single time. If your friends are solid climbers, go and have fun, but ask them to walk you through the basics before you leave the ground.
I'm 14, can I bungee jump?

Most operators set the minimum age somewhere between 12 and 16, and you'll almost always need a parent or guardian to sign the waiver. There's usually a minimum weight too, often around 40 to 45 kilograms, because the cords are matched to body weight. Check the specific site's rules before you go, and bring the adult who'll sign for you.
I keep landing hard on my heels after drops and my knees ache. What am I doing wrong?

Heel landings send the impact straight up into your knees and spine, so you'll want to land on the balls of your feet and let your ankles, knees and hips bend together to soak it up. Practice small drops of a foot or two, focusing on landing quietly, because a loud landing is a hard landing. Rest the knees for a while, and if the ache doesn't fade, have a physio take a look before you go back to bigger drops.
Twisted my knee hiking, now it locks up sometimes. Got a big backpacking trip in a month.

A knee that locks often has a meniscus tear or a loose fragment catching in the joint, and that needs a proper assessment before you go remote. Get it seen by a sports medicine doctor soon so there's time for imaging and a plan before the trip. If it locks on a trail days from help, that's a real problem. Depending on the diagnosis, poles, a brace and a lighter pack may make the trip possible, but get it diagnosed first.
Thinking about doing an overnight ski tour solo, but my wife is nervous. What would make her feel better?

Share a detailed itinerary with her, including your route, camp spot and expected return time, and agree on what she should do if you don't check in. Carry a satellite messenger so you can send updates and call for help if needed. Keep your terrain choices conservative and consider doing the trip with a partner or guide your first time.
is it true you can go blind from bungee jumping??

Not really. There are rare reports of temporary vision problems from small burst blood vessels in the eyes, caused by the pressure surge as the cord recoils. These almost always clear up on their own within weeks. If you have glaucoma, a recent eye surgery or a detached retina history, ask your eye doctor before jumping, because that's where the real risk sits.
My buddy says drinking as much water as possible is the safest move in heat races. True?

No, overdrinking plain water is how people get exercise-associated hyponatremia, which can cause seizures and has killed endurance athletes. The safer approach is drinking to thirst plus taking sodium, roughly matched to what you sweat out. Warning signs of overdrinking include gaining weight during the race, puffy hands, sloshing stomach, headache and nausea despite plenty of fluid.
Terse question: slider up or slider off for a 400ft building?

At around 400 feet most experienced jumpers go slider off for a fast opening, but the right setup depends on your delay, canopy, and the specific object. That's exactly the kind of call to make with a local mentor who knows that site, not from a one-line answer. Get it wrong and you either open too slow or get a hard, unpredictable snivel near the wall.
we're 4 friends, all with beacons, planning to skin up and ski a big open bowl. how should we do it?

Begin by reading the avalanche forecast and checking that the bowl's aspect and elevation aren't flagged as a problem. Do a group beacon check at the trailhead, then expose one person at a time on the descent, regrouping at safe spots that sit well off to the side of the runout rather than in the middle of it. Agree on bail-out options before you commit, and make sure everyone is comfortable saying no.
do i really need to stop wakeboarding with a sore lower back

If it's just mild stiffness, take a few days off and keep moving gently rather than going straight back to hard landings. Wakeboarding's compression and twisting can aggravate it, so ease back in with smaller jumps. See a doctor if the pain is severe, persists or shoots down your legs.
is a 30 min surface interval enough between dives

It can be, if your dive computer or tables say so for the next dive, but longer is better. An hour or more lets you off-gas, rewarm and rehydrate, and it gives you more bottom time on the second dive. Make the deeper dive first, and keep the second one shallower and within your computer's limits.
What's a good first spin to learn? Riding for 4 years, mostly groomers.

A frontside 180 off a small jump or a natural roller is the classic first spin, because you're turning toward the direction you're facing, so you can see your landing the whole time. Practice ground 180s on flat terrain first to get the wind-up and landing switch comfortable. Since you've been on groomers, make sure you can ride switch confidently, because landing backward is half the trick.
I'm 34 and have never kayaked. Can I just rent a whitewater kayak and figure it out on a class III run this weekend?

Skip the class III this weekend, because it has real consequences like pins, swims into rocks and long cold rescues, and first-timers lack the skills to handle them. Book a one- or two-day intro course with a certified outfitter instead, where you'll learn wet exits, edging and basic strokes on flatwater and easy class I-II. Most people who do that progress to class III within a season or two, and they enjoy it a lot more.
My heart rate stays super high even at walking pace in the heat late in the race. Do I just push through?

No, that's your body telling you you're overheating or dehydrated, a phenomenon called cardiac drift. Slow down, get into shade, cool off hard with ice, take fluids with sodium, and give it 15 to 20 minutes before you carry on. If your heart rate stays high, or you get dizzy, feel chest pain or become confused, stop and let the medics check you out.
My 12yo wants to join an open water race with me next month. She's a strong club swimmer. Good idea?

It can be a great idea, as long as she's done a few practice open-water swims before race day, because a strong pool swimmer can still panic in cold, murky water with people bumping into her. Check that the event allows her age group, since many races have junior distances with extra safety cover. Try to get her to two or three supervised lake or sea sessions where she practises sighting and swimming in a wetsuit. On the day, start her at the side or back of the pack so she avoids the scrum at the start.
My 9 year old son wants to start motocross. I'm terrified honestly. Is it insane to let him?

It's not insane. Lots of kids ride safely, and the sport teaches real discipline and mechanical sense. The keys are a bike sized to him, like a 50cc or a small 65cc with a throttle limiter, full proper gear, and starting with a certified youth coach or a kids' riding school instead of figuring it out alone. Keep him on flat, open ground until his control is genuinely solid, and stay close while he rides. Most kids who get hurt early were put on too much bike too soon, so let him earn each step up.
First time ever on a dirt bike this weekend at my cousin's farm. What gear do I actually need?

At minimum you want a DOT or ECE-rated full-face motocross helmet, goggles, gloves, over-the-ankle boots, long pants and a long-sleeve top. Proper motocross boots matter more than most beginners realize, because ankle and foot injuries are the most common first-day injuries. If you can borrow or rent a chest protector and knee guards too, do it. Spend your first hour riding slow circles in an open, flat area so you can learn the clutch and throttle before you go anywhere near hills.
fear of flying wingsuit after a buddy died, should I quit

I'm sorry about your friend. It's completely normal to feel this way, and you don't have to make a decision right now. Taking a break, talking it through with people you trust, and only returning when your head is clear is a sound choice. If you go back, start small and with people you trust, and if you decide to stop, that's not a failure.
I'm 45 and fit, been surfing since I was a kid. Is it too late to get into big-wave surfing?

It's not too late, and plenty of big-wave surfers keep charging well into their 40s and 50s with decades of ocean knowledge on their side. What matters is building up the size gradually, getting a sports physical to check your heart, and doing proper breath-hold and fitness training. Join a big-wave safety course and find a crew who surfs the spots you want, because good partners matter more than age.
Can I dive with contact lenses?

Yes, soft lenses are generally fine, and lots of divers wear them. If your mask floods, keep your eyes closed or squinted while clearing it so you don't lose a lens. Bring a spare pair, or for less hassle, get a prescription mask.
my rear shock is leaking oil, finish the season on it?

Get it serviced now. A leaking shock is losing damping and can fail, making the bike handle unpredictably at speed. It may also damage the shock further. Most shops or suspension services can turn it around quickly.
Do I need insurance for BASE?

It's a good idea, because many standard health and travel policies exclude BASE, and a rescue in the Alps or a serious injury can cost a fortune. Look for specialist adventure sports or rescue cover, and read the fine print to confirm BASE is included. In some places, like parts of Switzerland and Norway, mountain rescue memberships or specific policies are common among jumpers. Sort it out before you travel, not after something goes wrong.
My paddling buddy got pinned briefly last week and is now nervous. How can I help?

That's a scary experience, and it's completely normal for confidence to take a hit. Go back to easier water they enjoy, let them set the pace, and focus on fun runs to rebuild their trust in their skills. A swiftwater rescue course together can also help a lot, because knowing exactly how to respond to a pin makes it feel much less helpless. Just being patient and supportive is probably the most helpful thing you can do.
we forgot a second rope, can we just rap the route on a single 60 and figure it out

Only if you know for sure the rappel is 30 meters or less, or that there are fixed anchors at intervals that a single 60 can reach. Otherwise you risk rappelling off the ends of the rope or getting stuck hanging with no anchor in reach. Check the guidebook or ask others at the crag about descent options, and look for a walk-off. Always tie stopper knots in both ends of the rope before any rappel, especially when you're not certain about the length.
what's the fastest way to learn a backflip, i don't wanna waste weeks

The fastest safe route is a trampoline with a snowboard-style trainer board, then an airbag jump if your area has one. Trying backflips straight on snow is how people land on their heads, and an injury will cost you way more than a few weeks. Add a session or two with a freestyle coach and you'll progress quicker than you would by guessing.
I'm overweight (about 110kg) but want to try parkour. Will I hurt myself?

You can absolutely do parkour, but start lower and slower than lighter people, because every landing puts more force through your knees and ankles. Focus first on strength, crawling, balance, step vaults and tiny precision jumps, and leave drops and big jumps for later as you build up. A beginner class or coach is especially worth it so someone can adjust progressions for you. If you have joint issues or a heart condition, check with your doctor first, but don't let your size stop you.
Quick one: how long should my delay be on a 500 foot jump?

On a 500-foot object like Perrine, beginners typically use a short delay of around 1 to 2 seconds, or even a static line or PCA on their first jumps. The right delay depends on your gear, slider setup and the local landing area, so let your course instructor set it. Add delay slowly over many jumps, because the margin you lose is the one that saves you.
Is it fine to rent crampons that look a bit dull?

Dull front points slip on hard ice and make you work much harder, so ask the shop to sharpen them or swap for a sharper pair. Check that the straps or bails are intact and that they fit your boots snugly with no play. A good rental shop will be happy to sort that out, and it makes a noticeable difference to how secure you feel.
How did Honnold actually prepare for El Cap? I want to copy his method.

For Freerider, Honnold spent years climbing the route on rope, rehearsing the crux pitches dozens of times, writing detailed notes on every sequence, and even backing off one attempt partway through when it didn't feel right. That last part is just as important as the training: he gave himself complete freedom to bail. The method only makes sense on top of his foundation of roughly 20 years of climbing and thousands of roped and soloed pitches, so the honest way to copy him is to start with that slow apprenticeship. Read his book Alone on the Wall to see how much patience the process actually took.
Can I skip the mandatory medical check at an ultra if I'm feeling totally fine? Waiting is costing me minutes

Don't skip it, both because it can get you disqualified and because "feeling fine" is unreliable deep into a hot ultra. Heat illness and hyponatremia often cloud judgment before you notice anything wrong. Medical checks usually take a couple of minutes. Use the time to refill, ice down and eat, so the stop isn't wasted.
what wetsuit thickness for uk sea in may

Go for a proper swimming wetsuit of about 3 to 5 mm, since the UK sea in May is usually around 10 to 12°C. A surf suit will feel restrictive in your shoulders. Add a neoprene cap and maybe socks if you feel the cold. Even with the suit, keep your early-season swims short and build up gradually.
I froze at the exit point and walked down. Am I just not cut out for this?

Walking down is a sign of good judgment, not failure. Every experienced jumper has turned around at some point, and listening to your gut is one of the skills that keeps you alive. Talk it through with your instructor, figure out whether it was nerves, the conditions or the object, and come back when it feels right. Never let anyone pressure you into jumping.
is it really that dangerous to swim near boats? they can see me surely

Often they can't. A swimmer's head is tiny among waves and glare, and a boat driver may not be looking for one, especially at speed. Stay out of boat channels and mooring areas, wear a bright cap and tow float, and if you hear an engine nearby, stop and raise an arm so they can spot you. Assume you're invisible and swim accordingly.
We heard a big whumpf on the skin track this morning. Kinda cool honestly, should we keep going up?

That whumpf is the snowpack collapsing on a weak layer, and it's one of the clearest warning signs you can get that slopes are primed to slide. Back off from anything steep or connected to steep terrain and stick to low-angle slopes, or call it a day. Report it to your local avalanche center too, because other parties will benefit from the observation.
I fell hard on a jump yesterday and my wrist is swollen and hurts to bend. Can I still ride today if I tape it?

Skip today and get it looked at, ideally with an X-ray. Swelling and pain when you bend it after a fall can mean a scaphoid fracture, which is common in snowboarders and easily mistaken for a sprain, and riding on it can lead to bad complications. Ice and elevate it until you're seen. If it's just a sprain, wrist guards will help prevent it next time.
do wingsuits really let you glide like a bird or is that just hype

It's surprisingly real. A good wingsuit pilot can hit glide ratios around 2.5:1 or better, so you cover far more ground than you lose in altitude, and forward speeds can top 100 mph. You're still falling, just very efficiently, and you always need a parachute to land. Proximity flying near terrain is where things get dangerous, but basic wingsuit skydiving feels a lot like flying.
How bad is it to climb with a slight cold?

A mild cold makes altitude feel much harder, and respiratory infections may increase the risk of HAPE. It also makes it harder to tell whether a cough is just a cold or something more serious. If you're already on the mountain, slow down, get extra rest and descend if your breathing worsens. If you haven't left yet, wait a few days until you've recovered.
What's the actual difference between a shovel blade made of plastic vs metal?

Metal, usually aluminum, is the one you want, because avalanche debris sets up like concrete and plastic blades can crack, flex or just bounce off it. Most avalanche educators and gear guides recommend a metal blade, a sturdy shaft that extends, and a blade big enough to move real volume. Saving a few ounces with plastic isn't worth it when you're digging out a buried partner against the clock.
what height do people start getting badly hurt?

There's no clean cutoff, since people get badly hurt from 3 meters by hitting rocks or shallow bottoms, but forces rise quickly with height. Around 10 meters, a poor landing can cause real injuries, and above about 15 to 20 meters, even good entries carry serious risk without proper training. Treat anything above 10 meters as advanced territory and work up to it slowly.
reserve repack is due in like 2 weeks but there's a boogie this weekend. surely 2 weeks over is no big deal right

Two weeks over means you're jumping an out-of-date reserve, and in the US that's not legal, and your dropzone shouldn't let you on the plane. The repack interval exists because the reserve is your last chance, and a rigger's inspection catches problems you'd never see. Call your rigger now and ask for a quick turnaround before the boogie, because many will fit you in if you ask early.
Water's 45°F but air is 80. Shorts and a rash guard ok?

Dress for the water, not the air, because a swim in 45°F water can cause cold shock and incapacitation within minutes. A drysuit or at least a thick wetsuit with a paddle jacket is the right call, plus neoprene booties and a skullcap. You can roll or splash to stay cool if you overheat, but you can't warm up quickly after a long cold swim.
Had a herniated disc last year, physio says I'm mostly recovered. bungee?

Ask your physio or doctor specifically about bungee, because the sudden snap at the bottom and the rebounds put real force through the spine, and most operators exclude back injuries. "Mostly recovered" may not be enough for this kind of load. If they clear you, a body harness may distribute the force better, so ask the operator about that option.
is it fine to have a couple beers before a sunset swim? its super chill

I'd save the beers for after. Alcohol speeds up heat loss, slows your reactions and dulls your judgment of distance and fatigue, and it's a factor in a large share of adult drownings. A sunset swim also means fading light, which makes you harder to see. Swim sober, stay close to shore, and enjoy the drinks wrapped up in a towel afterward.
My computer says I'm in deco. I'm on a fun dive, not trained for it. What do I do right now hypothetically

Ascend slowly and follow the stops your computer shows. Don't skip them, and stay at each one until it clears, then do a longer safety stop at 5 meters if you have the air. Tell your guide or buddy right away with hand signals. Once you're out, skip diving for at least 24 hours and watch for decompression sickness symptoms. Next time, keep an eye on your no-deco limit and start ascending with a few minutes to spare.
Thinking of flying alone at a remote site no one uses. Fine as long as I'm careful?

Flying solo at an unused site removes the safety net you'd really want if anything goes wrong, including someone to call for help or note where you went down. Unused sites can also have unknown hazards like power lines, rotor or poor landing areas that local pilots would normally warn you about. If you go anyway, fly with a buddy or at least have someone tracking you via live tracking. Get site information from a local club first.
My boyfriend wants to jump tandem with me but I'm way lighter than him. Is that okay?

Tandem jumps are set up for the combined weight of both jumpers, and operators usually have a total limit plus rules about the weight difference between you. The staff will weigh you both and decide whether it's safe and how to rig it, so let them make that call. If the gap is too big, they'll suggest separate jumps, which are just as fun and often less awkward.
is it bad to swim right after eating? seems like a myth

The cramp-and-drown idea is mostly a myth, so a light snack is fine. A big heavy meal might make you sluggish or a bit queasy, though, which isn't ideal in open water. Give yourself an hour or so after a big meal. Swimming in your comfort zone and with a buddy matters far more for safety.
Painkillers before a big mountain bike day to get through a sore wrist — dumb or fine?

Dumb, honestly, because pain is the signal that stops you loading a damaged wrist, and masking it on technical terrain means you'll grip and brake on an injury you can't feel. If the wrist is sore enough that you need pills just to ride, it needs to be looked at, especially since some wrist fractures like the scaphoid look like sprains and heal badly if ignored. Take a mellow day or get it X-rayed first.
Want to wingsuit BASE next year. I have 30 BASE jumps and 400 skydives. Realistic?

Thirty BASE jumps is still early for wingsuit BASE, which is among the deadliest parts of the sport. Most experienced voices recommend at least 200 wingsuit skydives and a large number of BASE jumps first, plus coaching specific to wingsuit BASE. Spend the next year building wingsuit skydiving skills and BASE experience, and pick your first wingsuit objects with a mentor. There's no rush, and impatience is exactly what wingsuit BASE punishes.
Have high blood pressure, on meds, well controlled. Ok to jump?

Get your doctor's sign-off first, because most operators list high blood pressure on their medical form and the head-down rebound briefly spikes pressure in your head. Well-controlled hypertension may be fine in your doctor's judgment, but that call belongs to them, not the booking desk. Bring the clearance with you, since some sites will ask to see it.
do i need to tip my tandem instructor?

It isn't mandatory, but it's appreciated, especially if they took video or went out of their way to calm your nerves. Something like 10 to 20 percent or a flat 20 to 50 dollars is typical in the US, and norms vary by country. A good review mentioning them by name also means a lot.
how many days a week should I train?

Three or four days a week is ideal for most people, with rest days between high-impact sessions. Your joints and tendons need recovery time even when your muscles feel fine. On off days, light mobility or a walk is a good idea. Overtraining usually shows up as aching knees or shins, so ease off if that starts.
Is proximity flying something I can work up to in like a year?

Probably not safely. Most experienced pilots spend several years and hundreds of wingsuit jumps building skill before they fly anywhere near terrain, and even then they progress gradually, starting far from the slope and closing in only with experienced mentors. Proximity flying leaves almost no margin for error, which is why so many skilled people have died doing it. Treat a year as the time to get really good in open sky.
Wind's coming over the back of launch slightly but its light. Launch anyway?

Don't. Even light wind over the back means you'd be launching downwind, which makes takeoff faster and harder to abort, and it often signals rotor or turbulence on launch. Wait for the wind to come straight up the slope, or pack up if it doesn't change. Many serious launch accidents start with a pilot deciding the tailwind was light enough.
how far should I stand from the takeoff to watch for the right speed?

Stand well to the side of the jump with a clear view of both the takeoff and the landing, never in the landing zone or on the run-in. Watch a few riders who are about your size and ability and note where they start their approach. Then do a speed check by riding up to the lip without jumping to feel the takeoff. That's much safer than guessing.
Best way to stop fast if a car comes out of nowhere?

A standup or hands-down slide you've drilled to muscle memory is your fastest emergency stop, which is why practicing slides before riding fast matters so much. Foot braking is too slow at real speed. If you can't stop in time, bail toward grass or the shoulder rather than risk going under a vehicle. Honestly, the real answer is riding with spotters and never outrunning your sightlines.
what's a flapper and what do I do

A flapper is a chunk of skin, usually a callus, that tears loose and hangs off your finger or palm. Wash it, trim the loose skin with clean nail clippers or scissors, and cover it with tape or a bandage. That's usually the end of your session, because climbing on it slows healing. Once it closes, keep your calluses filed down so they don't catch and tear again.
What's 'swim failure' in cold water? Heard it mentioned.

Swim failure happens after you've been in cold water for 10 to 30 minutes, when your muscles, especially in your arms and hands, cool so much that you can't coordinate your strokes anymore. It catches out strong swimmers because it arrives gradually, and it often hits on the swim back. Plan shorter swims in cold water, stay close to an exit point, and turn back while you still feel strong.
What bearings should I get for downhill? Is ABEC 9 better?

ABEC ratings matter far less than you'd think for skateboarding, since they measure tolerances that don't really affect rolling speed under skate loads. Look for bearings with built-in spacers and solid shields from a reputable skate brand, and keep them clean and lubed. A decent mid-priced set will serve you just as well as anything marked ABEC 9.
ok but statistically is free soloing more dangerous than driving

Per hour of activity, yes, by a wide margin. Driving is dangerous mostly because people do so much of it, while soloing has an extraordinarily high fatality rate for the time spent. Many prominent free soloists have died climbing, which tells you how unforgiving it is even at the highest skill levels.
What's a samba?

A samba is a loss of motor control that happens just after a freediver surfaces. It shows up as shaking, twitching or jerky movements because the brain is short on oxygen, and the diver may or may not stay conscious. It's a warning sign that you came very close to a full blackout. Your buddy should support your airway, keep your face out of the water, and talk you through recovery breaths. After a samba you're done diving for the day.
How many skydives do I actually need before I can start BASE jumping?

Most reputable first jump courses want at least 200 skydives, and many mentors prefer you closer to 300 to 500 with solid canopy skills. The number matters less than what's behind it: consistent stable exits, accurate landings in tight areas, and handling of a high-performance canopy. Spend those jumps working on canopy control and spot landings, because that's what keeps BASE jumpers alive.
I'm cave certified. My buddy cancelled last minute. Solo cave dive tomorrow, thoughts?

Solo cave diving is a separate discipline with its own training, mindset and gear redundancy, and a full cave cert alone doesn't prepare you for it. With no one to share gas or help with an entanglement, small problems escalate fast. Either find another qualified buddy through your local cave community or reschedule, because the cave will still be there next weekend.
Quick q, cat leap vs precision jump, which should I learn first?

Learn the precision jump first, since it teaches distance judgment and controlled landings, which are the foundation for almost every other movement. The cat leap adds catching a wall with your hands and absorbing the impact with your feet, so it needs grip strength and hanging control as well. Get comfortable with precisions on lines and curbs, then start cat leaps onto low walls where your feet can reach the ground.
Does an airbag pack mean I can ski riskier stuff?

No, and thinking that way cancels out the benefit. Airbags improve your odds of staying near the surface, but they do nothing against trauma from trees, rocks or cliffs, and they don't help in terrain traps where debris piles deep. Treat it as a last line of defense and make the same conservative terrain choices you would without it.
how long should my surface interval be between dives?

A common rule of thumb is to rest at least twice as long as your dive time, and more for deeper dives. For example, a 1-minute dive needs a 2-minute rest. For dives past about 20 to 30 meters, many divers rest longer still, aiming for 5 or more minutes, or use time times depth divided by 5. If you feel tired, cold or short of breath, wait longer.
How do I know if a beach is safe to swim at?

Look for lifeguards and swim between their flags, and check the signs for warnings about rips, tides or water quality. Watch the water for a while before you get in, because calm-looking channels between breaking waves are often rips. If you're not sure, ask the lifeguards or locals. Staying in your depth on an unfamiliar beach is always the smart call.
what's a good warm up before a parkour session

Spend 10 to 15 minutes moving: start with easy jogging or skipping, then wrist circles and wrist pushups, because your wrists take a beating on vaults. Add deep squats, lunges, leg swings, and ankle circles, then finish with some quadrupedal crawling and a few small, soft jumps to wake up your landing mechanics. Before any big move, rehearse a smaller version of it a few times. Cold hamstrings and wrists are behind a lot of avoidable strains, so don't skip it even on short sessions.
my kid is 8 and wants to start bouldering, is that too young?

Eight is a great age to start, and lots of gyms run kids' clubs from five or six upward. Bouldering suits children because there are no ropes to manage, but they still need to learn to climb down when they can and to fall onto their feet and roll back. Sign them up for a youth intro session so a coach teaches those habits early. Keep the sessions playful rather than pushing grades.
Snapped a finger pulley (A2) climbing, small tear. Coach says I can tape and keep projecting. True?

A small A2 tear usually means a few weeks off hard crimping, not projecting through it with tape. The evidence that taping protects the pulley is pretty weak, and loading a damaged pulley risks a full rupture with months of recovery. A climbing-savvy physio can give you a structured return, usually starting with open-hand hangs and progressing over six to eight weeks. Easy climbing on big holds may be okay, but hold off on your project.
Is it okay to paddle at night if it's a river I know?
Generally no. Even on a familiar river, you can't see new wood, changing levels or other hazards, and rescues are far harder in the dark. Plan to be off the water before dusk.
planning to solo a WI4 next weekend, done it on lead a few times. tips?

Honestly my best tip is to keep leading it for now, because soloing ice gives you zero margin for a popped tool, a shattered placement or a dinner-plating smear, and a few leads of WI4 is not much buffer. Experienced soloers usually solo several grades below their lead limit after years of mileage, on ice they know well. If you want the feeling of moving fast and free, lead WI3 confidently with long runouts on solid ice and save soloing for much later, if ever.
what's hypothermia feel like when swimming? how do i know when to get out

The early signs are subtle: your strokes get clumsy, your fingers splay and won't stay together, and you start feeling oddly calm or confused. Being unable to touch your thumb to your little finger is a good test. Get out at the first of these, not when you're shaking violently, because your thinking is already going by then. Have warm layers ready on shore and expect to feel colder for 10 to 20 minutes after you get out, so don't drive straight away.
Is solo cave diving ever OK?

Some very experienced cave divers do dive solo, but it's an advanced choice made after years of cave diving, with full redundancy in gas, lights and cutting tools and specific solo training. It isn't for newer divers, and everyone should be clear that it removes the backup a buddy provides. If you're still building experience, stick with a trained team.
is it okay to hit the park with a slight concussion from last week? feel fine now

No, give it more time and get medical clearance first. Riding before a concussion fully heals raises the risk of a second, more serious injury, and feeling fine doesn't always mean your brain is recovered. Follow a gradual return-to-activity plan with a doctor. Also replace the helmet you crashed in.
butters

A butter is just pressing your weight onto the nose or tail so the other end lifts while you keep riding, and it's one of the most fun low-risk tricks out there. Start on a gentle groomer at slow speed, shift your hips over the nose, and flex that ankle and knee until the tail comes up off the snow. Once you can hold a nose press, add a little shoulder rotation to spin it into a 180 butter.
How do I start racing locally? Ive been riding about 2 yrs

Find your local motocross organization or the AMA-sanctioned tracks near you, get a membership, and look up their race schedule. Enter the beginner or novice class for your bike size, even if you think you're faster. Racing feels very different from practice, and the first-turn pileup is where a lot of crashes happen. Go to a race as a spectator first, walk the track, and learn the flag rules before you line up.
How hot is too hot to ride?

There's no single cutoff, but riding above about 90°F (32°C) with high humidity increases the risk of heat exhaustion and heat stroke because MX gear traps heat. Drink plenty of water and electrolytes before and during riding, take frequent breaks in the shade, and ride shorter sessions. Watch for dizziness, nausea, headache or confusion and stop immediately if they appear. Early morning or evening rides are much safer in summer.
what's the easiest way to start soloing without anyone at my gym knowing

Doing it in secret is the part that worries me most, because the climbers at your gym are exactly the people who could catch the gaps in your judgment before they cost you. Climbers who solo safely tend to build up in public, talking routes over with partners, rehearsing on rope and getting honest feedback about whether they're ready. If the desire is real, find an experienced outdoor mentor or hire a guide and tell them your long-term goal. They'll respect that far more than you'd expect.
pregnant, 10 weeks, booked a jump before I knew. can I still go?

No, you shouldn't jump while pregnant, and every legitimate operator prohibits it. The violent deceleration and abdominal pressure aren't safe for you or the pregnancy at any stage. Call the operator and explain, since most will refund or let you transfer or postpone the booking.
Just finished my FJC!! My friends want to take me to a 300ft antenna this weekend, is that ok?

Congrats on finishing, but I'd hold off on that one. A 300-foot antenna gives you very little time and tends to sit in tricky landing areas, and it's not where a brand-new jumper should be making their own decisions. Stick to the forgiving objects you trained on and build a good number of jumps with your mentor first. The low stuff will still be there once you've earned it.
do I need wrist guards or is that a beginner thing

They're not just for beginners. Wrist fractures are among the most common skateboarding injuries at every level, because falling and reaching out is pure instinct. Lots of experienced street skaters skip them, but plenty of people who ride ramps and hills keep wearing them. If you're learning anything new or skating fast, wear them.
best way to learn a 180

Start on flat ground and practice the rotation with ollies, popping off your tail and turning your shoulders first so your board follows.
