Then try it off a small roller or side hit, wind up slightly before takeoff, and look over your leading shoulder toward the landing. Frontside 180s usually feel more natural first because you can see where you're landing, so get those consistent before working on backside.
can i film it with my phone in my hand

Almost every operator bans handheld phones, and for good reason. A phone flying out of your hand at the bottom of the drop can hit someone below, and gripping it can mess up your body position. Most sites sell video packages or allow a properly strapped camera they've approved, so ask about those instead.
can i bring my gopro on my first solo jump?

No, and most dropzones ban cameras until around 200 jumps, which is the USPA recommendation. Cameras add snag hazards in a malfunction, and more importantly they divide your attention right when you need to focus on altitude and procedures. Pay for the instructor's video if you want footage, and save your own camera for later.
Is it okay to climb ice alone if I'm just doing a short top rope with a self belay device?

Self-belay top-roping on ice is something some experienced climbers do, but it adds risks you don't have with a partner, like a device that won't run well on an icy rope, an anchor you can't watch, and no one around if you get hit by ice. If you do it, use a device built for this with a backup, set an anchor you'd trust with a partner, and tell someone exactly where you are and when you'll be back. For most people, finding a partner or joining a club meetup is the much better option.
Is it worth buying a $40 complete from a big box store or should I spend more?

Spend a bit more if you can, because those cheap completes usually have slippery decks, hard plasticky wheels and bearings that make learning harder and less predictable. A complete from an actual skate shop or a known brand runs about $90 to $130 and will roll, turn and pop much more consistently. If money is tight, a used setup from a local skater is often a better deal than a new big box board.
is a full face helmet better for BASE or open face

Lots of jumpers prefer full-face helmets for face protection when they strike the object or have a hard landing, while others like open-face helmets for better hearing and peripheral vision. Either one is far better than going without, since object strikes and landing impacts are common causes of injury. Choose a helmet that fits snugly and has no snag points, and wear it on every jump.
how much does it cost to get into paragliding? broke student lol

Expect roughly 1000 to 2500 in USD or euros for a beginner course, depending on country, and new gear can run another 3000 to 5000. As a student you can save by renting school gear while learning, then buying a good used beginner wing that's been professionally inspected. Don't skimp on the reserve or helmet. Some clubs also offer student discounts, so it's worth asking around.
we've been drinking a bit but it's only a 6m ledge, it's fine right?

I'd skip it today. Alcohol throws off your judgment of distance and body position, slows your reaction if you surface disoriented, and is a factor in a big chunk of jumping and diving deaths. Six meters is plenty high to injure you with a sloppy entry. Swim, hang out, and save the jumps for a sober day.
Do i need a special board for park tricks?

You don't strictly need one, but a park or all-mountain twin board with a softer flex and true twin shape makes spins, switch riding and buttering much easier. A stiff freeride board is harder to press and less forgiving on landings. If you're renting, ask for a park setup, and avoid buying anything until you know what you like riding.
My 15 year old son wants to try ice climbing. Is that too young? I'm kind of nervous.

Fifteen is a perfectly reasonable age to start, and plenty of guide services run youth or family intro days on top-rope, where the risk is well controlled. The key is having him learn from a certified guide rather than from friends, and keeping it to top-rope at first. If he gets hooked, a structured course will teach him to judge ice quality and handle cold safely before he goes any further.
My 15-year-old wants to start paragliding. Is that too young?

Many countries allow training from around 14 to 16 with parental consent, so check the rules with your national association. Maturity matters more than age: the best young pilots are the ones who can say no to marginal conditions and listen to their instructor. Book a tandem together first, then talk to a reputable school about their junior programme and how closely they supervise younger students.
How bad is it to touch the cave walls or floor

It's a big deal, both for safety and conservation. Kicking up silt can wipe out visibility in seconds for you and everyone behind you, and decorations like stalactites take thousands of years to form and break instantly. Good trim and frog kick technique keep you off the bottom, and that's why instructors drill buoyancy so hard.
I'm 58 and out of shape, is ice climbing realistic for me?

Very realistic. Lots of people start in their fifties and sixties, and good technique matters far more than strength. Book a guided intro day on easy toprope ice, and the guide will teach you to climb with your legs and save your arms. A bit of leg and grip conditioning beforehand will make it more fun. If you have heart or joint concerns, a quick chat with your doctor about strenuous cold-weather activity is worth it.
I've got 140 jumps and I'm honestly better than most guys with 300. Can I just borrow a buddy's suit and go?

Don't do it. Skill in freefall doesn't cover the specific risks of wingsuiting, like getting a stable, clean deployment with your arms wrapped in fabric, or handling a tension knot or line twist while unzipping. Borrowing a suit sized for someone else adds another unknown on top of that. Use the next 60 jumps to tighten up your canopy work and tracking, then do a proper First Flight Course.
how high can I safely drop from as a beginner

Start with drops from roughly knee height and get comfortable there before moving up, focusing on landing silently on the balls of your feet with your knees bent and hips back. Most beginners should stay under head height for several months, and anything above that should be paired with a solid roll to spread out the impact. Your bones, cartilage, and tendons take a long time to adapt, and the damage from too-big drops often shows up years later as knee and heel problems. A good test is whether your landing is quiet and controlled; if it's loud or jarring, the drop is too big for now.
track has a big triple everyone's hitting, I've only done doubles, buddy says just pin it and commit

Don't take advice to just pin it on a triple you've never jumped. Coming up short on a triple means casing hard or landing on a face, and those crashes injure people badly. Watch where the fast riders shift and how much speed they carry, have someone experienced watch you hit the biggest doubles cleanly and consistently, and if the track has a smaller line or a tabletop version, work up through that first. The triple will still be there next month.
Is cliff diving after a few beers a big deal? Everyone does it

Yes, it's a big deal, and alcohol shows up in a large share of cliff jumping deaths and spinal injuries. Drinking slows your reaction time, weakens your coordination and makes you more willing to try heights and entries you'd normally skip. It also speeds up heat loss in cold water. Jump first and drink afterward.
Anxious parent here. My teen wants to skate at a DIY spot under a bridge. Is that a bad idea?

DIY spots aren't automatically dangerous, but they vary a lot, with crumbling concrete, exposed rebar and debris being common hazards. It's worth going with your teen once to check the condition of the ramps, the area's safety and whether people skate there regularly. If it looks solid and well used, make sure they go with friends, wear a helmet and have their phone charged, and steer them to a public skatepark if it looks sketchy.
is it legal to do parkour in public places?

Generally yes in public spaces like parks and plazas, but it depends on local rules, and private property including many malls, office buildings and parking garages is off-limits without permission. Be respectful: leave when asked, don't damage anything, and avoid crowded areas where you could crash into people. Many cities also have dedicated parkour parks, which are the easiest legal option.
short: how do I stop a speed wobble mid-run

Relax, bend your knees, and shift weight to your front foot, which usually damps the wobble. Don't stiffen up or try to stop hard on a shaking board. If it doesn't calm, slide out or bail into the grass while you still have control. Then tighten your trucks before the next run.
Booked a tandem flight in Turkey for my honeymoon, how do I know if the company is safe?

Ölüdeniz has loads of operators, so it pays to check. Ask whether their pilots hold a national tandem licence, whether the company carries insurance that covers you, and how old their wings and reserves are. Read recent reviews for any mention of rushed launches or flying in bad weather, and walk away from anyone who pushes you to fly when the wind looks strong or seems unusually cheap. A good operator will happily cancel when conditions are wrong.
My mate says you can avoid hypothermia by swimming harder. True?

Only partly. Swimming hard generates heat, but moving fast through cold water also strips heat away quicker, and you can't keep up a hard pace forever. Once you tire, you cool even faster. Time in the water, the temperature and your body composition matter far more, so manage your duration rather than trying to outswim the cold.
I'm 62 and had a stent put in two years ago. Is Everest Base Camp out of the question?

Not automatically. Plenty of people your age with stable heart disease have done the EBC trek, but you need a cardiologist's sign-off first, ideally after an exercise stress test. Altitude raises heart rate and blood pressure and lowers oxygen to the heart muscle, so your doctor should know you'll be sleeping above 5,000 m. Go with a reputable outfit that carries oxygen and a pulse oximeter, and buy travel insurance that explicitly covers helicopter evacuation.
Any tips for my first race day? Novice class, nervous as hell

Get there early so you can sign up, walk the track and get through practice without rushing. In practice, focus on learning the lines instead of setting fast laps, and remember the goal on your first race day is to finish all your motos cleanly, not to win. Off the start, it's fine to let the aggressive guys go and settle in, because most first-lap crashes happen in turn one. Hydrate, eat something light, and know that everyone at the gate is nervous.
How long should I stay at Everest Base Camp before climbing through the Khumbu Icefall the first time?

Most expeditions spend several days at base camp and do a puja ceremony before the first icefall rotation. They also do acclimatization hikes up nearby peaks like Lobuche East, so climbers are well adapted by the time they first enter the Icefall. Move through the Icefall early in the morning, when it's coldest and most stable, and follow your expedition leader's rotation plan rather than charging ahead to save time.
rain today, still want to train outdoors

You can, but change what you train. Wet concrete, metal rails and painted surfaces get very slippery, so skip precision jumps, rail balances and anything at height. Rainy days are good for conditioning, quadrupedal movement, flow on ground-level obstacles, and testing grip on surfaces you know well. Pay attention to how your shoes grip and stay conservative.
my husband is on kilimanjaro right now and texted that he has a pounding headache and threw up at barafu camp. should i be worried??

Yes, take it seriously, because headache plus vomiting at Barafu (about 4,600 m) is classic acute mountain sickness and can progress. Message him to tell his guide right away and not to push for the summit tonight if symptoms don't clearly improve with rest and fluids. Descending even a few hundred metres usually brings fast relief, and good guides make that call without hesitation. If he becomes confused, stumbles or gets very breathless at rest, that's an emergency and he needs to go down immediately.
Strong current pulled us way off the boat on a drift dive, we surfaced and nobody saw us for 20 mins. What should we carry?

That's scary, and it happens more often than people think. Each diver should carry a surface marker buoy (a sausage) that you inflate before or at the surface, plus a loud whistle or air horn, and ideally a signal mirror or light. For remote drift diving, a personal locator beacon like a Nautilus Lifeline is well worth the money. Also, make sure the boat knows your dive plan and how long you'll be down.
Getting arm burn on longer wingsuit flights. Should I just push through?

Don't push through to the point of fatigue, because tired arms make your flight sloppy and can affect your deployment. Build shoulder and core strength on the ground, shorten flights or slightly relax your arms. Get a coach to check your body position too, because extra tension is usually the real culprit.
should I buy a used downhill bike off marketplace

It can be great value, but downhill bikes take a beating, so inspect the frame closely for cracks around welds and the head tube. Check for worn pivot bearings and suspension that leaks oil or feels sticky. Ask for service records, and ideally have a shop look it over before you hand over the cash. Budget for a suspension service and new brake pads straight away.
I ran low on air last time in a cavern and it scared me. How do I stop that happening?

Good that it scared you, because that's a near miss worth learning from. Plan turn pressures before you descend using the rule of thirds or something stricter, check your gauge often, and turn the dive the moment you hit your number, even if you feel fine. It's also worth reviewing your trim and breathing with an instructor, since stress and poor buoyancy burn gas much faster than people expect.
Asthma as a kid, haven't used an inhaler in 15 years. Need to mention it?

Yes, mention it on the medical form. Childhood asthma you've outgrown often isn't a problem, but a doctor should confirm that, sometimes with a lung function test. Asthma can trap air in the lungs, which is a real risk on ascent. Leaving it off doesn't change the risk, and getting cleared means you can dive with confidence.
can you get really hurt by just a 10 ft wave or is it mostly the huge ones?

You can absolutely get seriously hurt in 10-foot surf, especially over shallow reef or rock where the lip can slam you into the bottom. Injuries like dislocated shoulders, broken bones and blackouts happen at that size all the time. The wave's shape and what's under it often matter more than height, so respect heavy reef breaks at any size.
is it ok to have a beer between runs

Hold off until you're done riding for the day. Even one drink slows your reaction time and dulls your judgment, and downhill gives you very little margin for either. Many parks also prohibit riding after drinking. Enjoy it at the end of the day when the bike is on the rack.
Fingers have gone white and numb on the descent. Should I rub them hard to warm them up?

No, because rubbing frostbitten tissue damages it further. Warm them gently against your armpit or stomach, or in a partner's armpit, and get out of the wind. Avoid rewarming them fully if there's a chance they'll refreeze, since freeze-thaw cycles do much worse damage. Once you're safely down, get medical attention.
Can I jump alone if nobody's around? I'm a strong swimmer.

Don't. Even strong swimmers get knocked out, winded, or hit by cold shock, and alone there's no one to pull you out or call for help. Always jump with at least one buddy, ideally one who stays in or near the water while you go.
do people really get scared in the plane or is that a movie thing

It's real, even for people who've done hundreds of jumps, though the feeling often turns into focused excitement once you have experience. For first-timers, the door opening is usually the peak. Then freefall hits so hard that the fear tends to give way to adrenaline almost instantly.
My knee has been aching for three weeks of trail running, mostly on downhills, pain on the outside. I don't want to lose my base before my ultra in two months. What should I do?

Pain on the outside of the knee that flares on descents is classic IT band syndrome, and it usually gets worse if you keep pounding downhills through it. Swap your running for cycling or pool running for a week or two to hold your aerobic base, and see a sports physio for a proper diagnosis and a hip and glute strengthening plan. Two months is enough time to fix this if you act now, but not if you keep grinding through it until race week.
I'm 16 and want to do a wreck penetration with my older cousin who's done a few. He says it's easy.

Going inside a wreck is overhead diving, and people get lost, silted out or snagged in there, including experienced divers without the right training. Enjoy swimming around the outside, which is often where the best marine life is, and if wrecks hook you, take a Wreck Diver specialty when you're eligible. Your cousin should do the course too before going inside.
What does 'considerable' danger actually mean on the avalanche forecast? Sounds pretty mild.

It sounds mild, but considerable (level 3 of 5) is where the most avalanche fatalities happen in North America. Human-triggered avalanches are likely, and natural ones are possible, so conditions are dangerous on specific slopes even if the day feels fine. On a considerable day, read the forecast closely for which aspects, elevations and problems are flagged. Then stick to lower-angle terrain or slopes that aren't flagged, and keep careful terrain management in mind.
honestly i just want someone to tell me it's ok to keep bouldering on my sprained thumb lol

Can't do it, sorry. A sprained thumb on the inner side of the joint can be a UCL injury, and pinches and slopers will load it constantly. Bad ones don't heal without treatment. Get it checked if pinching is weak or the joint feels loose. If it's a mild sprain, you can climb jugs and easy routes with the thumb taped and avoid pinching for a couple of weeks.
how do i fall safely when bouldering

Land on both feet with your knees bent, then roll back onto your bum and shoulders. Keep your arms in and don't reach back with your hands. Whenever you can, climb down partway instead of jumping from the top. Practice small falls on purpose at the gym so the motion becomes automatic.
what's a speed wobble and how do I not die from one lol

A speed wobble is when the board starts shaking side to side faster and faster at speed until it bucks you off, and it's caused by tension, loose trucks and going faster than you can handle. The fix is to bend your knees, keep your weight forward on the front foot, and look ahead, because stiffening up and leaning back makes it much worse. Tightening your trucks a bit, and getting a longer wheelbase for downhill, reduces wobble a lot. Most importantly, stay at speeds where you can still foot brake or slide, and wear a helmet and gloves whenever you're riding hills.
my mate wants to jump right after a skydive the same morning to save time. any issue?

It's doable if you both feel fine, but stacking two big adrenaline hits can leave you more drained and shaky than you expect. Leave time for food, water and a proper rest between them, and don't rush the bungee briefing. Remember that weather delays at the dropzone can easily eat into your bungee slot. If either of you feels off after the skydive, push the jump to another day.
Is it safe to freedive while on my period?

Yes, it's generally completely fine. Use whatever products you're comfortable with. Some women notice slightly lower energy or breath-hold performance, so ease off if you feel off and dive conservatively. If you have particularly heavy or painful cycles, plan lighter sessions on those days.
how do I do a wall run to get up higher walls

Run in at a moderate speed, plant one foot on the wall at roughly waist height, and drive your body upward, pushing through the ball of your foot rather than kicking into the wall. Reach for the top with both hands while your foot is still pushing, and then pull yourself into a cat hang or straight onto the top. Most beginners plant their foot too high or too close, which kills their momentum, so experiment with placement on a wall you can almost already reach. Make sure the top edge is solid and the ground underneath is clear before you try anything taller.
How do bungee cords not snap? Like what's actually stopping that

Commercial cords are made from bundles of hundreds or thousands of latex strands, so the load is spread out and there's huge redundancy built in. They're rated well above the forces a jumper generates, and operators log every jump and retire cords after a set number. That combination of overbuilt materials and strict retirement is why snapping is so rare at professional sites.
rails or boxes first

Boxes first. They're wider, flatter and much more forgiving if your board slips out. Start with a long, low ride-on box and focus on keeping your board flat and your weight centered. Move to rails once boxes feel boring.
Thinking of hiring the cheapest Everest operator I can find. 30k vs 70k, how much does it matter

It matters a lot, because the price gap usually reflects your oxygen supply, the Sherpa-to-client ratio, the quality of the weather forecasting and the rescue backup. Budget outfits have been tied to running out of oxygen and to poor decisions on summit day. Ask any operator about oxygen per client, their guide credentials and their safety record, and favour established companies with long track records, even if that means waiting a year to save.
board length for 15-25 ft waves?

For paddling waves that size, most people ride guns between 9'6" and 11', depending on your weight, the wave's speed and how early you need to get in. Heavier surfers and slabbier, faster waves usually call for the longer end. Talk to a shaper who builds big-wave guns, because a board dialed for the specific break makes a real difference in your safety.
do i need an avalanche course if i only ski trees

Yes, because trees don't make a slope safe. Avalanches can and do run through widely spaced trees, and getting swept into trunks is extremely dangerous. Only dense, tightly spaced timber anchors the snowpack meaningfully, and tree wells add their own suffocation risk. An avalanche course will help you tell which tree skiing is actually low-risk and which isn't.
how fast do wingsuiters fall?

With a good flare, experienced pilots can get vertical speeds down to around 25 to 40 mph, compared to about 120 mph for a belly-to-earth skydive. Horizontal speed is usually 60 to 100 mph or more. Beginners in smaller suits will fall faster until their technique improves.
I'm 16 and want to get into wingsuiting as fast as possible. Fastest route?

In the US you have to be 18 to skydive at most dropzones, so the clock really starts then. Until then, you could try indoor skydiving in a wind tunnel, which builds body flight skills that make your freefall progression faster and safer later. Once you're 18, do an AFF course, build to 200 jumps, then take a First Flight Course. Rushing is the one thing that reliably gets people hurt in this sport.
how do I stop skating downhill fast, no time for a long answer

Foot braking is the most reliable method at moderate speed. Keep your weight on your front foot and drag the sole of your back foot flat along the ground, pressing harder gradually. At higher speeds you'll need slides, which take real practice. Until you've learned them, only ride hills you could comfortably bail off on, and if a hill scares you, carve wide turns to scrub speed or walk it.
is it legal to free solo in national parks

In most US national parks, including Yosemite and Joshua Tree, free soloing isn't specifically banned, and climbing regulations focus on things like bolting, closures and wildlife protections. Rules vary between parks and change over time, so check the current park climbing regulations and any seasonal raptor closures before you go. Other countries and private land can be stricter, so look up the local rules for wherever you're headed.
Snorkeled down after a dive to grab something at 6m, a few times. Should I worry?

Repeated breath-hold dives soon after scuba diving is a known risk factor for decompression sickness, so it's worth paying attention. Watch for unusual fatigue, joint pain, tingling, rashes or dizziness over the next 24 hours, and call DAN or get medical help right away if anything shows up. Next time, leave a long surface interval before any freediving after scuba.
My buddy got his boat pinned yesterday, we couldn't get it off and left it. Can we go back and try ourselves?

You can, but only if the water has dropped and the recovery doesn't put anyone in the current near the pin site. Pinned boats are under huge pressure, and people get hurt wading in to free them. Use a mechanical advantage system from shore, like a Z-drag, if you've been trained on it. Otherwise ask an experienced local club or swiftwater rescue folks to help, because a boat is never worth an injury.
How high does a bridge need to be for a first BASE jump?

Most FJCs use bridges around 400 to 900 feet over water or a clear landing area, which gives you enough time for a stable exit and a static-line or PCA opening without much margin for error. The height matters less than the overall setup: a clean landing area, no obstacles under the bridge, and an instructor who has jumped that exact site many times. Let your course pick the object instead of choosing one yourself.
dropping from a 3 meter wall, how do I land?

At three meters, a straight landing puts a lot of force through your knees and spine, so practice on lower drops before you attempt it. Land on the balls of your feet with your knees bending to absorb the impact, then flow straight into a safety roll to spread out the force. Work up gradually from one meter, adding height only when your landings are quiet and controlled. If your joints hurt afterwards, the drop is too high for now.
my friend says you can swim through a jellyfish bloom if you go fast enough lol

Your friend is wrong. Speed won't stop the stings, and swimming faster just means hitting more tentacles. Some species, like box jellyfish or Portuguese man o' war, can cause serious reactions. If you see a bloom, stay out of the water or swim somewhere else, and check local beach warnings, which often report jellyfish.
I had a panic attack last time at the platform and didnt jump. Should I try again or is it a sign

It's not a sign of anything except that your body did what bodies do at a big drop, and lots of people jump on their second attempt. Try again when you feel ready, tell staff upfront about last time, and they'll often coach you through it. If you'd like a gentler build-up, a tandem or a lower jump can help, and it's also completely fine to decide it's not for you.
Is it cheating to get towed into big waves with a jet ski?

Not cheating, just a different discipline, because tow-in lets you catch waves that are too fast and big to paddle into. It also adds its own risks, so the driver needs real training in jet ski rescue, timing and reading sets, and the surfer needs to trust them completely. If you're curious, learn as part of an established tow team or course rather than borrowing a ski and figuring it out with a friend.
how long does a 2 stroke top end last?

It depends heavily on the bike and how you ride, but a common range for a 125 or 250 two-stroke is roughly 15 to 40 hours of riding time. Check your manufacturer's service manual for the recommended interval, and track your hours with an hour meter. Replace it on schedule instead of waiting for it to fail, because a seized piston can lock the rear wheel at speed. Use good premix at the correct ratio and clean your air filter often to help it last.
street luge with no helmet just for a short run, its fine right

No, put on a helmet even for a short run. On a luge your head is a few inches off the pavement, and even a small tip at 20 mph can mean a serious head injury. Short runs are where people get careless, and that's when accidents happen.
do i need a helmet for big wave surfing

Plenty of big-wave surfers wear one, and it's worth it if your spot has a shallow reef or rocks, or if you're surfing in a crowd where boards fly. It cuts down head injuries, which are what knock people out underwater. Get one designed for surfing that doesn't trap too much water when you go under.
My dad is 72 and wants to do a tandem for his bucket list. He has a mild heart condition. Should we let him?

Lots of people in their seventies and older do tandems, so his age alone isn't the issue, but the heart condition means his cardiologist needs to sign off first. Ask specifically about the adrenaline surge, the altitude and the landing impact, and get any medical clearance in writing, since many dropzones will require it. Also let the dropzone know so they can talk about landing technique, because some tandem landings put real strain on the hips and knees.
rope solo vs free solo whats the diff

Rope soloing means climbing alone but protected, with a self-belay device or system that catches you if you fall. Free soloing means no rope at all. Rope soloing has a real learning curve and its own failure modes, so learn it from a guide or a very experienced mentor and back it up properly. Done right, it's the sane way to get solitude on the wall.
can i skip the AFF ground school if i've watched a ton of youtube videos

No, and no reputable dropzone will let you. Ground school covers your specific gear, emergency procedures and malfunction drills that you practice physically until they're automatic, and videos can't build that muscle memory. Think of the videos as decent prep that'll make the course easier, not a replacement for it.
Can i skip carrying water between aid stations 9 miles apart in desert? want to go light

Nine miles in the desert could be two hours or more, so carry at least a liter, and more if it's hot. Going light isn't worth getting stranded halfway with nothing to drink. Soft flasks in a vest weigh very little.
How do I equalize my ears better? I get stuck around 8m.

Getting stuck around 8 to 10 meters usually means you're using the Valsalva technique, which stops working well as your lungs compress. Learn the Frenzel technique, where you use your tongue as a piston to push air into your ears, and practice it dry on land until it feels automatic. Equalize early and often, starting right at the surface, and go down feet-first on a line if it helps. Never force through pain, because that's how eardrums rupture.
Do noseclips actually help or is that a gimmick

They genuinely help for some styles, especially deep diving with a fluid goggle or freediving without a mask, and for static apnea where you don't want water up your nose. For recreational line diving most people just use a low-volume mask and pinch their nose through the pocket to equalize. Try both in a pool session and see what feels better for your equalizing technique.
My friend says the best way to learn jumps is just to go big and figure it out, is that right?

That's how people end up casing the knuckle or overshooting into flat ground, so no. Start on small jumps, find the right approach speed by watching others or doing a speed check run, and land consistently before moving up. Your body learns timing and balance at low risk this way. Going big comes naturally once the basics are automatic.
can I take my dog ice climbing

It's best to leave the dog home. Falling ice, sharp crampons, and dropped tools at the base make it a dangerous spot for a dog. A loose dog can also wander under the climbers or out onto frozen water that won't hold weight. If you really want company, pick a ski or snowshoe day for the dog and save the ice for a solo or human-only trip.
Is free soloing something you can work up to safely if you start really easy?

Not really, because in free soloing any slip, broken hold or sudden cramp is likely fatal no matter how easy the route is. The climbers who do it have spent decades climbing roped, and even among them it has killed many of the best. If what draws you is the flow and simplicity, highball bouldering over good pads or fast, light roped climbing on moderate routes gives you a lot of that feeling with an actual margin for error. I'd honestly steer you away from soloing anything consequential.
Butter 180s. I keep catching an edge halfway through. What am I doing wrong?

Usually you're spinning with your board on edge instead of flat, or you're leaning back. Press onto your nose or tail with the other end lifted, keep the base flat to the snow, and let your shoulders lead the rotation with your hips following. Slow down too, because a lot of edge catches come from carrying too much speed into a trick that wants to be lazy and controlled.
Can I do parkour with a recently healed broken wrist? Cast came off two weeks ago

Hold off on anything that loads the wrist, like vaults, rolls, or climb ups, until your doctor or physio gives you the all-clear. Two weeks out of a cast, the bone might be healed but your wrist will be stiff and weak, and putting a full vaulting load through it can cause re-injury. Ask for a physio program to rebuild your range of motion and grip strength, then work your way back from wrist pushups on your knees. In the meantime, you can train precisions, balance, and lower body stuff that doesn't involve your hands.
rappelling — do i really need a backup like a prusik? seems like extra fiddling

Yes, use it. A friction-hitch backup like an autoblock catches you if you let go of the brake strand because of rockfall, a bee sting, a stuck hair or losing focus, and rappelling accidents are a big share of serious climbing incidents. Also tie stopper knots in both rope ends every time, because rappelling off the end of the rope has killed experienced climbers. Rigging it takes about thirty seconds once you've practiced. Get someone experienced to watch your first few setups.
Is free soloing illegal?

In most places it isn't illegal, though some parks, gyms, and private crags ban it or restrict climbing generally. Your rescue costs might not be covered, and some insurance policies exclude it. Check local regulations and access rules before climbing anywhere. Legality is never really the limiting factor here, and the risk is.
I'm 58 and want to start kayaking whitewater. Too old?

Not at all, and plenty of people start in their fifties and sixties and paddle happily for decades. Begin with a multi-day beginner course from a certified instructor, who will teach you the wet exit, basic strokes and reading water on gentle class I–II. Work on shoulder mobility and core strength, and progress at your own pace rather than trying to keep up with younger paddlers.
is a lifejacket a good idea for jumping?

For weaker swimmers or anyone jumping into cold or rough water, a lifejacket can help, but jump from low heights only, because the jacket can ride up and hit your chin or neck on entry from higher up. Hold it down by crossing your arms over the front when you land. If you need a lifejacket to feel safe in the water, keep jumps small and stay close to the shore.
What's thermalling and should beginners try it?

Thermals are rising columns of warm air that let you climb and stay up longer, which is how pilots fly cross-country. Strong midday thermals can be turbulent and are risky for new pilots, so beginners should start in gentle morning or evening conditions. Learn to thermal under an instructor or mentor in mild thermals once your basic skills are solid. It's a fun skill, but don't rush it.
best time of day to skin up a south facing slope in spring

Early, often on the move before or at first light, while the overnight freeze holds the snowpack together. Time your descent for when the surface has softened to corn but before it goes isothermal and sloppy, which is often mid-morning on south aspects. If there wasn't a good overnight freeze, skip sunny steep slopes that day.
Forecast says gusts up to 30 km/h but the morning looks calm. Worth launching quick before it picks up?

I'd sit this one out. Forecast gusts that strong usually mean the calm won't last, and conditions tend to build fast and unevenly once the day heats up. Getting caught in strong, gusty air mid-flight is exactly how pilots end up in collapses or get blown behind the hill into rotor. Talk to local pilots or the site guide about whether that forecast is realistic for the site, and save the flight for a day with a stable outlook.
My buddy has his A license and says he can take me up as a tandem passenger. Good deal right?

Absolutely not, because an A license doesn't qualify anyone to take a passenger. Tandem instructors need hundreds of jumps, a specific tandem rating, and specialized gear built for two people, and an unqualified tandem is a genuinely deadly setup. Book with a certified tandem instructor at a real dropzone and let your buddy jump alongside you instead.
What safety gear do I need for street luge?

For street luge you need a full-face helmet, preferably motorcycle-rated, a leather suit or durable racing leathers, gloves with palm protection, and sturdy shoes with added rubber for braking. Back protectors and knee and elbow pads add more safety. Organized events usually have minimum gear rules, so check those before you show up.
I'm trying to send my project faster. Should I hangboard every day?

Daily hangboarding is a fast track to finger injuries, because tendons and pulleys adapt more slowly than muscles. Two or three short sessions per week, with rest days in between, is plenty, and you should only start hangboarding after you've been climbing consistently for at least a year. Combine it with technique practice on your project for the biggest gains.
Got a sharp ear pain descending at 6m, pushed through and it popped. Ear feels full now. Okay to dive tomorrow?

No, get that ear checked by a doctor before you dive again, because a pop with pain and fullness can mean a perforated eardrum or barotrauma. Diving on it risks water entering the middle ear, severe vertigo underwater and infection. In future, stop, ascend a little and equalize again rather than forcing through pain.
I'm planning to jump in Norway this summer, first time at Kjerag. Any tips?

Kjerag is a classic site, but it has a fatality history, so treat it seriously even if you've jumped elsewhere. Go to the local BASE club, pay for the briefing, jump with experienced locals the first time, and know the exits and landing area thoroughly before you leave the edge. Weather in the fjords turns quickly, so be ready to wait out bad conditions or hike back down.
precision jump tips?

Swing your arms back then drive them forward as you jump, and aim to land on the balls of your feet with your knees bent to absorb the impact. Start with jumps drawn in chalk on flat ground so missing costs you nothing, then move to low rails or curbs. Only increase distance in small steps once you're sticking landings without wobbling, and never practice new distances where a miss means a real fall.
best way to get stronger fingers fast

There's no fast way that's also safe, because tendons adapt over months. Climb consistently for at least a year before adding hangboarding, then start with low loads and short sessions twice a week. Rushing finger training is the most common route to pulley injuries.
Can I use a caffeine pill every hour to push through the heat?

Caffeine helps in moderation, but taking it every hour is too much. High doses can raise your heart rate, upset your stomach, and mask the warning signs of fatigue you actually need to notice when it's hot. Most runners do well with about 1 to 3 mg per kg of body weight spread out over a long race, saved mostly for the later hours or the night.
how long can i hold my breath while scuba diving

You shouldn't, and that's the most important rule in scuba. Holding your breath while ascending, even a meter or two, lets expanding air overinflate your lungs and can cause an air embolism. Breathe slowly and continuously the whole dive, and exhale gently if you ever have to ascend without your regulator.
how high can you jump without hitting bottom if water is 2m deep

Two meters is really only safe for stepping in from very low, like a meter or so off a dock, feet first. Even a 3-meter jump can drive you into the bottom hard enough to break ankles or worse. For real cliff jumping you want at least 4 meters of depth, and more as height goes up. Find a deeper spot.
Is cold water really a big deal if the air is warm?

Yes, it's a huge deal. Water temperature is what matters in a swim, and cold water can trigger gasping, sap your strength in minutes and make self-rescue much harder, even on a hot day. Dress for immersion with a drysuit or wetsuit and proper layers based on the water temperature, not the air.
What's the deal with ice vests, worth it?

For pre-cooling before a hot start, they genuinely help by lowering your core temperature and buying you time. During the race most runners find they're too heavy, so ice in your hat, sleeves, and a buff does a similar job. Try whichever you use in training first so nothing surprises you.
can i fly with a cold

If it's mild, you can maybe fly, but congestion can make it hard to equalise pressure in your ears and sinuses, which gets painful when you climb or descend. A cold also dulls your focus and energy, which matters more than people think. If you're blocked up or feeling foggy, rest until you're clear-headed and your ears pop easily.
I'm 52 and want to get into motocross, am I crazy?

Not crazy at all, and plenty of people start in their 40s and 50s and have a blast. Your recovery is slower than a 20-year-old's, so ride a forgiving bike like a 250F, buy full quality gear including knee braces, and work on your fitness off the bike too. Take a few lessons early so you build good habits instead of learning through crashes, and stick to vet or novice practice days where the pace matches yours.
how do i do my first ollie on a snowboard

Start on flat ground or a gentle green run. Shift your weight onto your back foot so the tail flexes like a spring, then lift your front foot, pop off the tail and pull both knees up. Land with your knees bent and your weight centered over the board. Practice it standing still a dozen times before trying it while riding.
ugh the forecast hasn't updated yet and we're at the trailhead. just send it?

Use yesterday's forecast as your baseline, and if there's been new snow, wind or warming since then, assume the danger has gone up. Stick to conservative, low-angle terrain until you can confirm conditions yourself with clear observations. A missing forecast is a reason to dial back, not to go bigger.
Me and my buddy want to ski a big couloir that slid last week. Since it already slid it should be safe now right?

Not necessarily, a past slide can leave a weak bed surface or remaining hang fire, and new snow or wind can reload it quickly. Check the current avalanche forecast and recent observations, and look carefully at what's left above and around the slide path. If you're unsure, pick a more conservative objective or go with a guide who can assess it properly.
I'm 58, a bit overweight, high blood pressure on meds. Want to learn to dive. Crazy?

Not crazy at all, plenty of people start diving at your age. Because of the blood pressure, you'll need a doctor to sign off on the medical questionnaire, ideally a doctor with dive medicine experience who can check your medication and heart health. Once you're cleared, take the course at an easy pace and work on fitness, since swimming against current takes real effort.
can you get a concussion from cliff diving?

Yes, from hitting the water at a bad angle, especially flat on your back or side from height, or from striking a rock on entry or while climbing out. If someone seems confused, has a headache, vomits or acts off after a jump, stop for the day and get them checked by a doctor. Don't let them jump again until they're cleared.
Can I use a regular dive light for caves or do I need special stuff

You'll need a powerful primary light plus at least two backup lights, all independently powered, because losing light in a cave is an emergency. Most cave divers use a canister or high-output handheld primary and two compact backups clipped where they're easy to reach. Your instructor will have specific requirements for the course, so check their gear list before buying anything.
Can I freedive the day after scuba diving?

Yes, but leave a proper gap. Freediving soon after scuba, especially deep or with long breath-holds, can raise your decompression sickness risk. DAN's general guidance is to avoid freediving after scuba on the same day, and waiting around 24 hours after repetitive or deep scuba days is a sensible margin. Freediving before scuba is generally less of a concern.
my friend died base jumping last year and now i want to try it, is that weird?

It isn't weird, because a lot of people feel drawn to understand something that mattered to someone they lost. It's still worth asking yourself whether you want the sport itself or a way to process grief, and talking that through with someone, maybe even a grief counselor, can help. If you do go ahead, take the slow, structured route of skydiving experience and a proper FJC, so you are making clear-headed choices each step of the way.
first time trying a real hill tomorrow, what's the one thing I should actually practice tonight?

Practice your stop until it's boring, because on a real hill your stop is your brakes and your survival plan in one. Go to a flat parking lot or a very gentle grade and drill foot braking at walking speed and then a bit faster, keeping your weight on the board and your braking foot flat. If you can, also get comfortable bailing into a run so you know how to step off at low speed. Tomorrow, start halfway down the hill, not at the top.
Ice climber, frostnip on 2 fingertips last weekend. They're tingly still. Climbing Saturday ok?

Tingling a week later suggests some lingering tissue damage, and fingers that have had cold injury are more vulnerable to it again. If there's no blistering or color change, a short day may be ok with very good glove management, warmers, and an early bail plan if they go numb. If you see blisters, discoloration or increasing pain, see a doctor and skip Saturday.
what should be in a downhill first aid kit

Pack lots of non-stick gauze, wound wash or saline, tape, nitrile gloves, an elastic bandage and a few large sterile pads, since road rash is the most common injury. Add some painkillers, an instant cold pack and a list of emergency contacts. Take any serious injury, head knock or deep road rash to a doctor; the kit is for patching up, not replacing proper care.
lol what happens if my main chute fails

You'll be trained to recognize a malfunction, cut away the main with one handle, and deploy your reserve with another. Reserves are packed by certified riggers and are extremely reliable. Most rigs also have an AAD that automatically fires the reserve if you're still falling fast at low altitude. On a tandem, your instructor handles all of that for you.
do i really need a helmet for top roping, it's kinda uncomfortable

Yes, wear it every time. Ice climbing constantly knocks loose chunks of ice from above, including ones you dislodge yourself, and people get hit even on easy top-rope days. Belayers need one too. If yours is uncomfortable, try fitting a different model or adjusting it over a thin hat, because a comfortable helmet is one you'll actually keep on.
can i belay with a grigri and take my brake hand off since it auto locks

Keep your brake hand on the rope at all times, even with a GriGri. Assisted braking devices can fail to lock if they're loaded unusually, threaded wrong, or held open by your own hand during a panic grab, and there are documented accidents from exactly that. The GriGri is a backup to good technique, not a replacement for it.
I'm 52 and finally have time and money for this. Am I too old to start wingsuiting?

Plenty of people start skydiving and wingsuiting in their fifties, so age itself isn't the barrier. What matters is decent fitness, flexibility for the arch and deployment, and getting a medical checkup if you have heart or joint issues. Start with AFF, build your 200 jumps patiently, and you'll be in good shape to fly a suit safely.
Lower back aches after deadlifts but I've got a big kayak trip in 10 days. Should I just stop training?

You don't need to stop moving, but drop the deadlifts and anything else that clearly aggravates it. Keep up gentle walking, mobility work and core activation, because total rest usually makes back pain stiffer. Kayaking itself relies a lot on trunk rotation, so do some short paddles or rotation drills before the trip to see how it responds. If you get pain shooting down a leg, numbness, or any bladder or bowel changes, see a doctor right away.
do i need insurance for base jumping

Yes, and check it carefully, because most standard health, travel and life policies exclude BASE. Look for specialist adventure sports insurance that names BASE explicitly, especially if you'll jump abroad, where rescue and evacuation can cost tens of thousands. Make sure the policy covers search and rescue, not just medical treatment.
is a 35 degree slope actually dangerous or is that just people being paranoid

It's not paranoia: most slab avalanches release on slopes between about 30 and 45 degrees, and 35 to 40 is the peak zone. A 35 degree slope can be perfectly fine on a stable day and deadly on a bad one, so the angle tells you where to pay attention, not whether you're safe. Check the avalanche forecast, look for recent slides and cracking, and carry an inclinometer or use a phone app, because people underestimate slope angle all the time.
I've had a few hard landings lately on my own canopy. Should I just push through?

Don't push through it, because repeated hard landings point to a technique problem, and that's how ankles, spines and worse get hurt. Talk to an instructor or coach and have someone video your landings to diagnose the issue, which is often flaring too high, too low, or unevenly. A canopy course is the best investment you can make right now, and it may also make sense to go up a canopy size temporarily.
Is it ok to fly alone at a remote site if I tell someone where I'm going?

Telling someone helps, but flying alone at a remote site is risky, because if you get hurt or land in rough terrain, help could be hours away. If you do it anyway, carry a satellite messenger or GPS tracker, a phone and first aid, and pick conservative conditions. Ideally, fly with at least one other pilot or a ground crew, especially at sites you don't know well.
how tight should my trucks be

It depends on what you ride, but beginners usually do best slightly tighter than medium. That gives you stability and fewer wobbles without making turning impossible. Adjust the kingpin nut in quarter turns and test after each one, keeping a few threads showing above the nut so it can't work loose. Looser trucks carve better, while tighter trucks are calmer at speed.
its windy af today but i drove 3 hours. should i push the dz to let me jump

Don't push them. Wind limits exist because gusty or strong winds make landings genuinely dangerous, especially for students and tandems, and staff call holds for good reasons. Ask if the forecast looks better later in the day or tomorrow, since waiting out a hold is a normal part of skydiving.
My fingers hurt after climbing, especially the middle finger at the base. Should I just tape it and push through?

Pain at the base of your finger, especially if it gets worse when crimping, can be an early sign of a pulley strain, and pushing through is a common way to turn a minor injury into a full rupture. Back off from hard crimping, stick to easy open-hand climbing or rest completely, and see a physiotherapist who knows climbing injuries if it doesn't improve within a week or two. Taping can offer a little support during recovery, but it isn't a substitute for rest.
I'm 7 months pregnant and used to climb a lot. Can I keep bouldering?

Most guidance says to stop bouldering by this stage, since falls and impacts are the main risk and your balance and center of gravity have changed a lot. Many climbers switch to top-rope with a full-body harness or a pregnancy harness so a fall never puts pressure on the belly, and climb easy terrain. Run it by your OB or midwife, and listen closely to your body, especially around loosened joints.
My kickflips keep landing primo and it hurts my ankles

Landing primo usually means you're flicking too hard or kicking off the side instead of out the front corner of the nose, so ease off the flick and aim it up and forward. Keep your shoulders square and your back foot over the tail so you can catch the board with both feet. If your ankles are getting tweaked, take a break, consider ankle support or high-tops, and practice stationary on grass until the rotation is clean.
I have a mild cold but I paid $200 for this boat dive tomorrow. Decongestant and go?

I'd skip it. Decongestants can wear off at depth, which can cause a reverse block on the way up, and that can damage your ears or sinuses. Call the operator tonight, since most will reschedule or give partial credit for illness. Losing the money stings less than a burst eardrum or weeks out of the water.
My buddy says salt tablets are pointless if you eat chips at aid stations. True?

He's partly right, because salty real food like chips, broth and pickles can cover your sodium needs if you eat them steadily. The trouble comes later in the race when your stomach turns and you stop eating, and that's when capsules are handy as a backup. Heavy sweaters in heat often need 300 to 600 mg of sodium per hour or more. Carry a few tablets even if you plan to rely on food.
I keep hearing about the Perrine Bridge. Why is it so popular for beginners?

It's legal all year, it's about 486 feet tall, and it has a fairly forgiving landing area beside the Snake River. Several reputable schools run first jump courses there, so beginners can train in a controlled setting with experienced instructors. Even so, beginners get hurt there, and the river and current are hazards, so arrive trained and respect the site.
I've been climbing in the gym for 8 months and I'm hooked on Alex Honnold videos. How long until I can start free soloing?

Honestly, the timeline isn't measured in months, it's measured in years and thousands of roped pitches outdoors. Honnold spent over a decade climbing obsessively before his big solos, and even he rehearsed Freerider dozens of times on rope first. For now, channel that energy into learning to lead outdoors with a mentor or guide, because gym climbing doesn't prepare you for loose rock, polish, or real exposure. Keep watching the videos for inspiration, but let your ambitions grow at the pace of your experience.
Tweaked my ankle bouldering yesterday, it's swollen but I can walk on it. Comp is Saturday. Can I just tape it and send?

Swelling the day after means real ligament damage, and taping it for a comp where you'll be falling onto mats at awkward angles is how a mild sprain turns into a bad one. Get it checked first, ideally by a physio who sees climbers, because if you can't hop on it pain-free you shouldn't be jumping off problems. Ice, compression and elevation for the next 48 hours give you the best shot at Saturday, but be ready to skip this one and climb the next comp properly.
best way to keep hands from freezing while belaying

Wear a thick insulated belay parka over everything when you stop, because trapping core heat keeps blood flowing to your hands. Swap your thin climbing gloves for warmer ones while belaying, and keep a spare pair inside your jacket so they're warm and dry when you need them. Do not stop paying attention to the belay to shake out your hands, but swinging your arms in big circles between rope movements can push blood back into your fingers. Eat and drink warm fluids too, since a cold, underfueled body sends less heat to your extremities.
How big of a deal is a reef cut?

Reef cuts look minor but infect easily, especially in tropical water, so take them seriously. Rinse the wound thoroughly with clean fresh water, scrub out any coral or debris, and apply an antiseptic and a clean dressing. If it gets red, hot, swollen or starts oozing, or you develop a fever, see a doctor quickly. Deep cuts or ones near joints should be checked by a professional right away.
lost my belay device at the crag, can I use a munter hitch?

Yes, a munter hitch on a locking HMS carabiner works well, but only if you've practiced it before. It twists the rope, and you need to brake with your hand in the correct position. If you're unsure about tying or managing it, climb on a partner's setup or call it a day rather than learning it live.
Is it dumb to go out alone on a big day if no one else is surfing?

Yes, that's one of the riskiest choices in big-wave surfing. If you get knocked out or held down, nobody will be there to help. An empty lineup on a big day can also be a sign the conditions are worse than they look. Wait for a crew, find a buddy, or enjoy the show from shore.
I'm a girl, 5'3, everyone says I need a lowered bike. True?

Plenty of shorter riders lower their bikes, especially when starting out, because being able to get a foot down gives a lot of confidence. Options include a lowering link, a lower seat, or adjusting the suspension sag, though too much lowering can affect handling and ground clearance. Many experienced short riders eventually ride stock heights by learning to slide off one side at stops, so lower it now if it helps and revisit later.
can I learn kickflips without learning ollies first

Not really, because a kickflip is basically an ollie with a flick. Without a solid pop you'll end up landing on a spinning board, and that's how you roll an ankle. Get your ollies consistent first, then practice kickflips standing still on grass or carpet. Only try them rolling once you're landing bolts more often than not.
What causes the most injuries in cliff diving?

Hitting the bottom or a submerged object is the big one, usually because nobody checked depth or conditions changed. Next come bad entries, like landing flat or tilted, which cause bruising, burst eardrums, compressed vertebrae and winded lungs. Slipping on takeoff and drowning after an impact stun round out the list, and almost all of these come down to scouting, sober judgment and someone watching.
how long do you have to dig someone out of an avalanche

Survival odds drop sharply after roughly 10 to 15 minutes, mostly from asphyxiation, so rescue has to come from the people already on scene. That's why everyone in the group needs a beacon, shovel and probe, and regular practice so you can search and dig fast. Outside help almost never arrives in time to make the difference.
First time touring next month. Do I need a guide or can I follow YouTube tutorials?

YouTube is great for learning skinning technique and kick turns, but it can't teach you to read a real snowpack or make decisions in the field. For your first few tours, hire a certified guide or go with a mentor who has avalanche training, and book an AIARE 1 or equivalent course. A guide day is also a fast way to learn transitions and efficient uphill travel without risking a bad decision.
tryin to save money. used kayak off craigslist ok?

Used boats are a great way to save money, but check it carefully before you buy. Look for cracks, soft spots, a damaged hull, missing float bags, and a secure seat and footbrace. Make sure it fits your weight and size and that it's actually a whitewater kayak rather than a recreational boat. Bring a more experienced friend to look it over if you can.
35, never mountain biked, my friends want me to come downhill riding. am I gonna die

No, but don't start on the hard runs. Book a beginner lesson at the bike park, rent a downhill bike with full-face and pads, and stick to green trails for the first day. Lots of people start in their thirties and progress quickly with coaching. Friends who ride well often forget how hard it is for beginners, so ride your pace.
big swell coming, what should I check on the forecast besides wave height

Check swell period, direction and wind as well as height. Longer periods, say 16 seconds or more, pack much more power than the face height suggests. Swell direction decides how the wave breaks at your spot, and wind can turn a clean day dangerous. Also look at tide, since some reefs get much shallower and more dangerous at low tide.
rolled ankle snowboarding, can still walk. keep riding?

If you can walk without much limp and there's little swelling, it's probably a mild sprain. Still, I'd call it for the day rather than ride on it, since a stiff boot and an unexpected catch edge can twist it further. Ice it, elevate it, and see how it looks in the morning. If you can't put weight on it, or there's tenderness on the bony knobs of the ankle, get an X-ray before you ride again.
Doing an ice mile attempt solo next month, I've done 1km in 5C. thoughts?

Please don't make it a solo attempt. Ice miles are done in water under 5°C, and even very experienced swimmers can become incapacitated with little warning. You need a dedicated support crew, a boat or kayak alongside, and a rewarming plan with medical knowledge on hand. Going from 1 km at 5°C to a mile in colder water is a big jump, so build up gradually under supervision and consider joining an organized event.
im 15 can i start paragliding?

In many countries, yes, but you'll need parental consent, and some schools set a minimum age of 14 to 16, so check with local schools. Training is the same as for adults: a proper course with a certified instructor. Ask your parents to visit the school with you so everyone's comfortable with the plan. Starting young is great, because you'll build good habits early.
my shins keep getting smashed by my board, any way to stop it

Shin bangs usually come from your board flipping back at you when you bail flip tricks, especially if you lean back or kick too hard. Commit more with your shoulders over the board and keep your flick smaller and more controlled. Until you get it dialed, soccer shin guards or skate-specific shin pads under your pants will save you a lot of misery.
found a spot online with no info on depth, guy in the video jumped fine so should be cool

One video tells you that one guy didn't get hurt that day, but water levels may have changed, and the video won't show near misses or the people who were injured. When you get there, swim the landing zone and check the depth yourself before anyone jumps. Look for warning signs or ask locals too, because they'll often know about hidden rocks or seasonal hazards.
how long should my surface interval be?

A common rule is to rest at least twice your dive time, and longer, up to three to five times, as you go deeper or longer. Relaxed recovery breathing matters more than counting seconds, so don't start your next dive until your breathing and heart rate feel calm. If you're getting tired, end the session rather than squeezing in another dive.
bro my friend says if you bomb a hill you just crouch low and you won't wobble, true?

Crouching helps, but it won't save you if you're going faster than you can control. Speed wobbles mostly come from tension and loose trucks, so tighten your trucks a bit, stay relaxed, and keep your weight over your front foot. The real fix is not exceeding a speed you can stop from. Learn to foot brake and slide before bombing anything, and skip hills that end in traffic or intersections entirely.
can kids under 10 do parkour

Absolutely, and many parkour gyms run classes for kids as young as five or six, which focus on playful movement, balance, crawling, and small jumps. At that age, coordination and confidence are the main goals, rather than big drops or heights, which put a lot of stress on growing bones and growth plates. A structured class with coaches is the best way in, since kids naturally want to copy what they've seen online. Encourage them to keep their parkour at ground level and away from roofs and walls they could fall from.
My knee is kinda sore from front-pointing, can I just push through?

Take it easy, because pushing through usually turns a minor irritation into a longer layoff. Front-pointing puts more strain on calves and knees, so rest it, try lower-angled ice where you can flat-foot more, and check your boot fit. If it's swollen or still sore after a week or two, see a physio or sports doctor before going back.
what's rotor

Rotor is turbulent, tumbling air that forms downwind of an obstacle like a hill, ridge, tree line or building when wind flows over it. For paragliders it's one of the most dangerous things you can fly into, because it can collapse the wing suddenly and repeatedly, often close to the ground. The basic rule is to never get behind a ridge or obstacle relative to the wind, and to give lee sides a very wide berth. Your instructor should show you where rotor forms at each site you fly.
how to get over fear of a jump I know I can make

Prove it to yourself at ground level first: mark out the same distance on flat ground and stick it ten times in a row, which gives your brain real evidence. Then try it in a progression, like a slightly shorter version of the jump, or the same jump at a lower height. Some fear is useful information, so if you still have a specific doubt, like a slippery takeoff or a wobbly landing surface, address that rather than forcing it. Never commit to a jump halfway, since hesitating mid-air is far more dangerous than walking away and coming back another day.
dislocated shoulder kayaking last month, it went back in on its own. back on whitewater this weekend fine?

Probably not yet. A shoulder that's dislocated once is much more likely to do it again, and the high brace and roll positions in whitewater are exactly how they come out. Re-dislocating in a rapid is a serious drowning risk, not just an injury. See a physio for a rotator cuff strengthening program, and get clearance before running moving water again. Low-brace on flat water is a sensible stepping stone in the meantime.
I'm 68, fit, do yoga. too old to bungee?

Lots of operators have no upper age limit, and plenty of people in their seventies and eighties have jumped. What matters is your health: heart conditions, high blood pressure, osteoporosis, recent surgery or joint problems are the things to check. A quick chat with your doctor beforehand is smart, and some operators may ask for a medical certificate over a certain age.
whats the weight limit for tandem

Most dropzones set the limit around 220 to 250 pounds, which is roughly 100 to 113 kg. It's a gear and safety limit, because the tandem system and canopy are rated for a combined weight that includes the instructor. If you're near the cutoff, call ahead, since some places allow it with an extra fee and a specific instructor, while others are strict.
What's the minimum water depth I need for a 10m jump?

A good rule is at least 4 to 5 meters of clear water for a 10 meter jump, and more is better because you can easily go 3 or 4 meters under on a feet-first entry. Check the depth yourself on the day, since tides, drought and shifting rocks can change a spot you've used before. If you can't verify the bottom, don't jump.
what does lmc mean in freediving

LMC stands for loss of motor control, sometimes called a samba. It's when hypoxia makes a diver twitch, shake or lose coordination after surfacing, and it's one step short of a full blackout. A buddy should support the diver's airway, keep their face out of the water and talk them through recovery breathing. It's a clear sign you pushed too far, so ease off your dives.
I'm 62, decent shape, never flown. Too old to start?

Not at all, plenty of people start paragliding in their sixties and fly happily for years. Launch running and landings put some load on your knees and ankles, so it's worth checking with your doctor if you have joint or heart issues. Look for a school that's comfortable with older students. You'll probably find tandem flights first and gentle training slopes very approachable.
lost altitude awareness on my last AFF jump and the instructor pulled for me. am i failing?

No, this happens to a lot of students, and it's exactly why AFF instructors are there. You'll probably repeat that level, which is normal and nothing to be ashamed of. Focus on checking your altimeter at a regular rhythm during freefall, and practice the dive flow on the ground with an altimeter until checking becomes a habit.
Is it smart to go ice climbing alone with a self-belay device?

Rope-soloing ice is an advanced technique with very little margin for error, and if something goes wrong there's nobody to help or call for rescue. It's not something to try until you've got a lot of partnered experience. If you can't find a partner, look into local climbing clubs, gym groups or guide-led meetups. That gets you climbing safely and with people to learn from.
Can I take my GoPro on my tandem?

Usually not. Most dropzones and the USPA require 200 jumps before you can jump with a camera, because snags and distractions can be dangerous. If you want footage, pay for the handcam or outside video package so a professional films it. You'll get much better video, and you can stay fully in the moment.
how long should my first ice screw be from the belay

Get a solid screw in as soon as you can after leaving the belay, ideally within a body length or two, so a fall doesn't load the anchor directly with a high fall factor. Some people clip a piece of the anchor as their first protection for the same reason. The first few metres are where a fall does the most damage, so don't run it out early.
im 15 and want to solo the boulder field cliff behind my school its like 40 feet

Please don't. Forty feet is high enough to kill you or leave you with serious injuries, especially onto boulders. If you love climbing, find a local gym or climbing club, since many have youth teams and will teach you to climb outside properly with ropes. You'll get stronger much faster that way, and you'll get to keep climbing for decades.
What's the deal with tree wells? I'm doing a cat skiing trip.

Tree wells are deep pockets of loose snow around the base of trees, especially conifers. If you fall in headfirst you can get trapped and suffocate within minutes, even without an avalanche. Ski with a partner who keeps you in sight, stay clear of tree bases when the snow is deep, and if you go in, protect your airway and avoid thrashing. Your cat ski operation will brief you on this, so pay close attention.
Why does my vision tunnel on long dives?

Tunnel vision is a hypoxia warning sign, meaning your oxygen is running low. Treat it as a signal to end your dive immediately and to back off on the next ones. It often comes right before LMC or blackout. Shorten your dives, lengthen your surface intervals and make sure your buddy is right there.
Riding sand for the first time next week. Tips?

Keep your weight back, stay on the gas, and keep your momentum, because sand rewards smooth, steady throttle and punishes chopping it. Hold the bars loosely so the front end can wander a little on its own, and stand up through the soft sections. Sand is exhausting, so bring plenty of water and plan for shorter sessions than usual. Lower your tire pressure a bit, or run a paddle or sand tire if you're riding dunes.
How cold is too cold to swim without a wetsuit?

There's no single cutoff, because it depends on your acclimatization, body fat and time in the water. Most unacclimatized swimmers start struggling below about 16°C (60°F), and below 10°C (50°F) even short dips need real care. Cold-water swimmers build tolerance gradually over weeks, keep early swims to just a few minutes, and never go alone. If you're new to it, a wetsuit is the smarter choice under about 16°C.
my boyfriend watched Free Solo and now wants to solo a 5.8 at the crag this weekend. he's only ever top-roped in a gym. how do i talk him out of it

Point out that top-roping in a gym gives him none of the skills that matter for soloing: reading real rock, spotting loose holds, and staying calm with nothing below him. Alex Honnold had over a decade of outdoor climbing before his big solos and rehearsed Freerider on rope for years, which is the part the movie makes clear and most viewers skip past. Suggest a compromise that scratches the itch, like booking a guided outdoor climbing day where he can lead or top-rope real rock this weekend. If he still insists, tell him plainly that you're scared, because sometimes that lands better than statistics.
felt dizzy and couldn't stop shivering after a cold dip, normal?

Some shivering is normal, but feeling dizzy means you got quite cold. Get dry, wrap up in warm layers, have a warm sweet drink and move gently. Don't drive until you're properly warmed up. Next time, stay in for a shorter time. If you get confused, start slurring, or the shivering gets worse or suddenly stops while you still feel cold, get medical help right away.
Our tour guide in SE Asia is offering a bungee for like $20, no paperwork, cords look kinda faded. Worth it for the story?

That's a pass. Faded cords suggest UV damage or overuse, and no paperwork usually means no inspection logs or retirement schedule for the equipment. Cords have a limited number of jumps before they must be replaced, and cheap outfits are exactly where that rule gets ignored. Find an operator with a visible safety record and certification, because the story isn't worth a cord failure.
I'm 16, can I sign up for a desert 50 miler with my dad?

Many ultras set their minimum age at 18, so check the race rules first. Even if you're allowed in, your body heats up and recovers differently while you're still growing, so starting with a shorter hot-weather trail race or a cooler 50K together is a smarter first step. Run it with your doctor's okay and build up over a couple of seasons.
Friend says I'm ready for class IV after one season of class III. Thoughts?

Maybe, but one season is fast, so it depends on how solid you truly are. Ask yourself whether your roll works reliably in pushy water, whether you can catch small eddies on demand, and whether you can swim and self-rescue in difficult rapids. If you're unsure on any of those, keep building on harder class III first. When you do step up, pick a well-known class IV run with experienced paddlers who've done it many times and will set safety. Moving up gradually lowers the odds of a bad swim scaring you off the sport.
Ears hurt for 3 days after diving and hearing is muffled. wait it out?

Get it checked by a doctor, ideally an ENT. Lasting pain and muffled hearing for several days can mean middle ear barotrauma or a perforated eardrum, and in rare cases inner ear damage, which needs prompt treatment. Don't dive or fly until you've been cleared. If you notice dizziness, ringing or sudden hearing loss, go right away.
Doing Everest next season with a budget operator for 30k. Red flags to look for?

At that price, look closely at guide-to-client ratios, how much bottled oxygen each climber gets, and whether the Sherpa staff are experienced and properly paid and insured. Ask for their summit and fatality record, references from past clients, and exactly what happens if you need a rescue or helicopter evacuation. Some cheap operators cut corners on exactly the things that keep you alive above 8,000 meters, so it can be worth paying more for a company with a strong safety record. Also make sure you've already climbed at least one 7,000- or 8,000-meter peak, because Everest is not the place to learn.
best way to practice sliding without wrecking my hands

Wear proper slide gloves with thick pucks, and start on a smooth, mellow hill or a flat parking lot with a slight slope. Learn the motions at walking speed until putting your hand down feels natural, then increase speed slowly. Mellower, harder-wheeled setups help slides break loose more predictably.
My 13 year old son wants to start downhill racing and honestly I'm terrified. How do I make this less scary?

The best thing you can do is get him into a coached youth program, because kids who learn body position and braking from a qualified coach crash far less than ones who just follow older riders. Make a certified full-face helmet, goggles, knee and elbow pads, and a back protector or body armor non-negotiable for every lap, not just race day. Local race series usually have age categories on easier tracks, so he can build up gradually, and you'll feel better watching him ride with real skills behind him.
how do I fall safely

Try to roll rather than land on one point. Tuck your chin, keep your arms bent rather than locked, and let your shoulder, back or kneepads absorb and slide out the impact. On ramps, drop to your knees and slide on your pads. Practice falling on grass so it becomes instinct before you need it.
Kid's bike fits but he cant reach the ground. Fine?

Not really. If he can't touch the ground with at least the balls of his feet while sitting, stopping and balancing at slow speeds becomes dangerous, and tip-overs are much more likely. A smaller bike or lowering the suspension and seat can help, which a dealer can advise on. Riding a bike that fits builds confidence and good habits faster than outgrowing it in advance.
What's the difference between AFF and static line training?

AFF, or Accelerated Freefall, starts you jumping from full altitude with two instructors holding onto you in freefall, and you deploy your own parachute. Static line uses a cord attached to the plane that opens your canopy automatically from a lower altitude, so you focus on canopy skills first and build up to freefall gradually. AFF is faster and more common in the US, while static line is cheaper per jump and still popular in the UK and elsewhere. Both are safe routes to a license, so choose based on what your local dropzone offers and your budget.
is mixed climbing just ice climbing with rock bits

Pretty much, it means climbing rock and ice together with tools and crampons, hooking edges and cracks instead of just swinging into ice. It's a lot more technical, since tool placements on rock can blow suddenly and sparks fly when your tools slip. Learn it on top rope at a dry tooling crag or with a guide before you try it on lead.
should I buy a used downhill bike? what to check

Used is a smart way to get into downhill, but these bikes take a beating, so inspect carefully. Check the frame closely for cracks, especially around welds, the head tube and the suspension pivots, and avoid any carbon frame with deep gouges unless it has been professionally inspected.
