On a considerable day, choose slopes under 30 degrees that aren't connected to anything steeper above or beside you, and save that line for a better forecast.
is wingsuiting more dangerous than regular skydiving?

Wingsuit skydiving adds some extra risk from more complex deployments and the potential for collisions in group flights, but done properly it isn't massively more dangerous than regular skydiving. Wingsuit BASE and proximity flying are a different story and are far more dangerous. With good training, solid gear and patient progression, wingsuit skydiving can be enjoyed with sensible risk management.
How far can you drift under canopy? Worried I'll land in a lake

Under canopy you can travel a mile or more depending on wind and opening altitude, which is why exit order and spotting matter so much. Your dropzone plans exits so everyone can make it back, and students usually get radio guidance. Many students also wear flotation gear if there's water nearby. Learn the water landing procedure in ground school, and if you're ever unsure you'll make it back, pick a clear open field early instead of stretching.
my wrist still hurts 3 weeks after a crash, rode through it. ok?

Wrist pain that lasts three weeks needs an X-ray, because scaphoid fractures often feel like a sprain and can heal badly if they're ignored. Stop riding until a doctor clears it. Missing a few more weeks now beats months of complications later.
wind is gusting 25 km/h at launch but everyone else is going. should i?

If you're questioning it, that's your answer, so stay on the ground. Gusty conditions in that range are manageable for experienced pilots on appropriate wings, but they can produce collapses and nasty launches for anyone less current. Other pilots launching tells you nothing about your own skill margin. Watch how they handle it, and fly another day if you're not sure.
can I dive the day after a long-haul flight?

Generally yes, flying before diving isn't a decompression issue. Long-haul flights do leave you dehydrated and jet-lagged, though, and both raise your risk. Drink plenty of water, get a proper night's sleep, and make your first dive an easy, shallow checkout dive.
can you bungee with glasses

You can't wear them loose during the jump, because they'll almost certainly fly off. Some operators provide a tight strap, but many will simply ask you to take them off. Contact lenses are the easiest option if you have them, or you can just jump without and enjoy the blurry view.
Worried question: what's an off-heading opening and how bad is it

An off-heading opening is when your canopy opens facing a direction you didn't intend, sometimes straight back toward the cliff or building you jumped from. It's one of the most dangerous things in BASE, because you might have only a few seconds to react before hitting the object. Training drills the response hard: fly away immediately with rear risers or toggles. Good body position, a symmetrical pack and the right delay greatly reduce the odds.
quick q: can I fly the same day after freediving?

There's generally no strict no-fly rule after recreational freediving the way there is for scuba, because you're not breathing compressed gas. If you did many repeated deep dives with short surface intervals, though, waiting a few hours to a day is a sensible precaution, since freedivers can still get decompression sickness under heavy loads. A shallow, relaxed session is usually fine for a flight later the same day.
I have about 40 jumps. When can I downsize my canopy? Want something faster.

Downsize slowly and only after a coach watches your landings, not because of your jump count alone. Look at your wing loading, which is your exit weight divided by canopy size, because at 40 jumps you should be staying conservative, usually around 1.0 or below. Take a canopy course first, since aggressive downsizing early is one of the biggest causes of serious injury in the sport.
How long after eating should I wait before swimming? Is the 30 min rule real?

The idea that eating will make you cramp up and drown is mostly a myth. Light snacks before swimming are fine. A big heavy meal might just make you feel sluggish or a bit queasy during a hard effort, so leave an hour or so after a large meal before a long or intense swim. For a casual dip, don't worry about it.
My stomach always shuts down in hot ultras. Any fix?

That's usually blood being pulled away from your gut to cool you, so the biggest fix is slowing down and cooling harder with ice so your gut gets blood back. Switch to easier calories like gels, sports drink, broth, flat soda or watermelon. Practice eating while running in the heat during training, since your gut adapts too. If you're vomiting repeatedly and can't keep fluids down, that's a stop-and-see-medical situation, not something to grind through.
Is Manaslu a good stepping stone before Everest?

Yes. Manaslu at 8,163 m is one of the most common 'training eight-thousanders' before Everest, because it gives you real experience with fixed lines, high camps and supplemental oxygen at extreme altitude. It does carry serious avalanche risk, and the 2012 avalanche killed 11 climbers, so go with an established operator that has strong route and weather planning. Many guides also recommend a 6,000 to 7,000 m peak like Ama Dablam or Himlung first.
What should I wear for my first paragliding lesson?

Wear sturdy ankle-supporting boots, long trousers and a long-sleeved top, since you'll be running on rough ground and getting dragged around a bit during ground handling. Bring a windproof layer and gloves, and sunscreen and water too. The school will usually supply the helmet, but confirm when you book.
whats the difference between a gri gri and an atc, which should a beginner get

An ATC is a tube device where your brake hand alone stops the rope. A GriGri adds assisted braking that cams the rope during a sudden load. Assisted braking adds a margin for error, which is why many gyms favor GriGris, but it is not hands-free, and you still keep your brake hand on the rope at all times. Plenty of people learn on an ATC first so the fundamentals become automatic, then add a GriGri. Either way, get taught in person by a gym instructor rather than from videos.
I'm 52 and fit. Too old to learn BASE?

Age alone doesn't rule you out, and plenty of people start later in life. What matters is your fitness, your reaction speed, how well your joints handle hard landings and whether you're willing to progress patiently. Build a strong skydiving record first, talk honestly with a first jump instructor about your health, and consider a medical check if you have any concerns. Being older often helps with the most important trait in BASE, which is good judgment.
Ran out of air at 15m on my last trip and shot straight up. I'm fine, so no harm done right?

Feeling fine afterward doesn't mean it was safe. A rapid ascent from 15 meters carries a real risk of lung overexpansion injury and decompression sickness, and some DCS symptoms show up hours later. Any joint pain, numbness, unusual fatigue, chest pain or breathing trouble needs urgent medical attention and a call to DAN. More importantly, work out why you ran out of air, and build habits of checking your gauge often and ending dives with a reserve.
We found an unexplored underwater cave on our property in Florida!! Want to explore it this weekend, we're advanced open water certified

That's exciting, but please don't dive it yourselves, because unexplored caves are the most dangerous kind and advanced open water training doesn't cover overhead environments at all. Unknown flow, silt, restrictions and no existing line make it the type of site that only highly experienced exploration divers attempt. Contact a local cave diving organization or experienced cave instructor in Florida, since many would be thrilled to assess it properly and might even let you be involved from the surface.
Best way to train for altitude if I live at sea level in Florida?

Focus on long aerobic endurance work, like hiking with a loaded pack, stair climbing, and steady cardio sessions of an hour or more, since a strong aerobic base helps you cope with the work up high. You can't truly pre-acclimatize at sea level, and altitude tents help some people, but they're expensive and the results vary. A smart ascent schedule on the mountain itself matters more than anything you do in Florida, so build extra acclimatization days into your trip.
What's the right way to swim if I come out of my boat in a rapid?

Use the defensive position: on your back, feet up and pointing downstream at the surface, so they bounce off rocks instead of getting caught. Never try to stand in fast water, because foot entrapment can be fatal. In deep, calmer stretches or when you need to reach an eddy or avoid a strainer, flip over and swim aggressively. Hang onto your paddle if you can, but let your boat go if it's dragging you into danger.
Is there a minimum age for big wave surfing competitions?

Most major big-wave events don't set a strict age cutoff. In practice, though, they only invite surfers with years of proven experience at heavy spots, so competitors are usually adults. Younger surfers can get there by building their skills, getting safety-certified and making a name at smaller big-wave venues first.
We're on vacation and the shop says I can do a 'discover scuba' to 18m. Sound right?

That's deeper than it should be. Discover Scuba experiences are normally capped at 12 meters, and a shop offering 18 meters to untrained divers is a red flag about how they operate. Ask them to keep you at 12 meters or less, or find another operator with better standards.
Is cave diving that much harder than wreck penetration? I've done a few swim-throughs.

Swim-throughs are a world away from real cave diving, which kills untrained divers more reliably than almost any other kind of diving. Silt-outs, getting lost and running out of gas in an overhead environment leave no direct path to the surface. You need full cave training from a specialized instructor, usually after cavern and intro courses, before going past the daylight zone. Cavern dives with a guide are a great way to see what it's like safely.
quick q, should I jump or step off

Take a small, controlled step or hop outward rather than a big running jump. You want enough forward momentum to clear the cliff face and any ledges below, but too much makes it harder to keep your body vertical. Before you go, look at exactly where you need to land and make sure you'll clear the rock.
How steep should my first downhill hill be?

Start with a gentle slope where you can comfortably stop with a footbrake, around 5 to 8 percent grade. The hill should have a long flat runout and little or no traffic. Once you can slide and stop confidently there, move to slightly steeper hills step by step.
Ultrarunner here, 100 miler in 6 weeks. Got pinpoint pain on my shin that hurts even walking now. Taper early and run through it?

Pinpoint shin pain that now hurts when you walk is a classic stress fracture warning, and running a 100 on it could turn a crack into a full break. Stop running and see a doctor for imaging, ideally an MRI, since early stress fractures often don't show on X-ray. If it's a stress reaction, you may be able to keep fitness with pool running or cycling. Be ready to accept that this race might not happen.
Do I need a spray skirt for class I?

For flatwater or very easy class I in summer, some people skip it, but even small waves can swamp a whitewater kayak quickly. A skirt keeps you dry, warm and in control, and it's necessary for rolling. Wear one and practice the wet exit so you're comfortable with it before graduating to bigger water.
What's a low head dam and why does everyone freak out about them?

A low head dam is a small weir or ledge spanning the river, often just a few feet tall, and it creates a hydraulic that recirculates water back toward the face of the dam almost endlessly. People caught in it often can't escape, and rescuers frequently drown too, which is why they're called drowning machines. They look harmless from upstream, which is what makes them so deadly. Know where they are on your river and always portage around them, with no exceptions.
what height is safe to drop from as a beginner

Start around knee to waist height and only go higher once your landings are soft, quiet and controlled every single time. Add height in small steps and use a roll to spread out the impact on anything above roughly head height. Drops are where joint damage creeps up over time, so being patient here pays off for years.
tools keep bouncing off the ice when I swing, what am I doing wrong

Usually it's a weak or stiff swing, aiming at bulges or hard brittle spots, or dull picks. Use a relaxed, flicking motion from the elbow, aim for small concave dips where the ice is softer, and let the tool's weight do the work. Check your picks are sharp and well profiled. A session with a coach can fix bad habits quickly.
Is it worth buying supplemental oxygen for Island Peak?

Generally no, because Island Peak at 6189 m is climbed without bottled oxygen by almost everyone. What matters far more is solid acclimatization, ideally trekking through the Khumbu or doing Lobuche East beforehand, and knowing how to handle jumars and fixed lines. Some operators do carry emergency oxygen, and that's worth confirming when you book.
what does WI mean in grades

WI stands for water ice, meaning ice formed from flowing or seeping water, as opposed to AI, alpine ice, which forms from compacted snow. The number usually ranges from WI1 for low-angle walking terrain to WI6 and above for long vertical or overhanging pitches with tricky, poorly bonded ice. Ice grades describe the route under average conditions, so the same climb can feel easier or harder depending on how fat, brittle, or wet the ice is. Treat the grade as a guideline and judge the actual ice in front of you.
thinking of buying an old 2005 glider cheap to save money, flies fine according to seller

A 20-year-old wing is a gamble, even if it looks fine. Line strength and fabric porosity both degrade over time, which can change how the glider handles and how it recovers from collapses. If you're tempted, insist on a recent professional check that includes a porosity test, line strength test and trim measurement, and walk away if the seller can't provide one. A newer used wing a few years old is usually a much safer buy.
Got a cheap rec kayak, can I take it down some rapids?

I wouldn't. Recreational kayaks usually lack flotation, have big cockpits that can't hold a spray skirt well and fill with water fast, and can fold around rocks in a pin. Stick to flat water with it, and rent or borrow a proper whitewater boat through a class when you want to try rapids.
found a used wing on marketplace for $400, 12 years old. good deal?

Probably not, because a 12-year-old wing is often near or past the end of its safe life no matter how clean it looks. Before you even consider it, ask for a recent porosity and line strength check from a certified inspector. If the seller can't provide one, walk away. A wing that's aged out can lose its shape or collapse more easily, and $400 won't feel cheap after that.
electric skateboard 25mph worth it for a beginner?

Not as your first board. At 25 mph, a crack or sudden throttle cut can throw you harder than most beginners can handle, and many riders get hurt before they learn to control speed and braking. If you go electric, choose a slower model or use a beginner speed mode, wear a full-face helmet plus wrist guards and pads, and spend time on a regular board learning balance and how to bail.
I have a mild cold, just a bit stuffy. Fine to dive tomorrow if I take a decongestant?

I'd sit it out. Congestion makes equalizing hard, and if the decongestant wears off at depth you can get a reverse block on the ascent, which can rupture an eardrum or cause vertigo underwater. Rescheduling one day is a lot better than losing a whole trip to an ear injury.
I keep scraping my hands. tips?

Scraped palms are a normal part of parkour, and over time your skin toughens up. You can reduce the damage by planting your hands flat instead of sliding them, checking surfaces for grit, and keeping your nails short. Clean any scrapes properly afterwards, since urban grime can cause infections. Gloves usually aren't recommended because they reduce grip and feel.
60 yo, torn rotator cuff (partial) per MRI. Still want to ski this winter. Realistic?

Often, yes, because skiing puts less demand on the shoulder than people expect, as long as you don't fall on it or plant a pole hard. The key is doing the physio rehab program faithfully over the next few months and getting your surgeon or physio to sign off on your range and strength before the season. Stick to groomers you're comfortable on, consider shorter pole straps or none, and avoid lift lines where you'd brace a fall with that arm.
Is speedflying basically the same as paragliding? Thinking about skipping straight to it.

No, and skipping straight to it is a bad idea. Speedflying uses small, fast wings close to the terrain, so mistakes happen much faster and there's far less margin for recovery, which is why accident rates are much higher. Most reputable schools require a paragliding licence and a solid amount of airtime first. Get your paragliding foundation and then add speedflying with a specialist school.
Pulled a muscle in my side paddleboarding. Rest or keep going?

Take a few days off or keep things very light. Side and oblique strains get aggravated by the twisting and reaching that paddling involves. Gentle walking and mobility are fine, then come back with short easy paddles once you can twist and cough without pain. If the pain is sharp with breathing or doesn't improve within a couple of weeks, get it checked, since rib injuries can feel similar.
is top roping ice actually safe or am i gonna die lol

Top roping is the safest way to ice climb, and it's how pretty much everyone starts. The rope is anchored above you, so a slip usually means a short drop onto the rope rather than a real fall. The bigger risks are ice falling from above and sharp tools or crampons near your belayer, so wear a helmet, keep your belayer off to the side, and learn from someone experienced. Do that and you're in good shape.
ok so my buddy says you should never jump alone. is that actually true or just overcautious

It's true, and it's one of the most important rules in the sport. A bad entry can knock you unconscious or wind you badly enough that you can't swim, and without someone watching you can drown in under a minute. Have at least one person on shore or in the water who can see the landing zone and knows how to get you out.
Can I use a regular skateboard for downhill?

A regular street skateboard can work on very gentle hills, but it's not built for downhill speed and stability. Downhill boards are longer, lower and use bigger, softer wheels for grip and control. If you plan to ride faster, get a board designed for downhill to stay safer.
Throw bag worth carrying for a beginner?

Yes. A throw bag is the most useful rescue tool on the river, and every paddler in the group should carry one. Practice throwing it on land and in moving water so you can hit a swimmer quickly and accurately, and learn to belay from a solid stance so you don't get pulled in. Carry a river knife too, in case the rope ever wraps someone.
Is scouting rapids really necessary or can I just follow the guy ahead of me?

Following a trusted, experienced leader on a run they know well is a normal way to learn, but blind-following on unfamiliar water is how people end up in trouble. Scout anything you can't see the bottom of, anything rated as a significant drop, and any rapid where wood may have shifted. If you're ever unsure, getting out to look or portaging is never the wrong call.
i have 140 jumps, my buddy says he'll lend me his suit and talk me through it. thats fine right?

I'd hold off. At 140 jumps you're under the usual 200-jump minimum, and a friend coaching you informally isn't the same as a First Flight Course with a rated instructor and a beginner-friendly suit. Your buddy's suit may also be too advanced for a first flight, which makes exits and deployment much harder. Spend the next 60 jumps tightening up your canopy and tracking skills, then do it properly.
Teen here, 16. What can I do now to get into wingsuit flying later?

Great time to start building the base: look into indoor skydiving tunnels, which many accept young flyers, and develop body awareness and fitness. In most places you'll need to be 18 to skydive, and then log 200 jumps before wingsuiting. Build good habits in the tunnel and you'll progress faster and safer when you're old enough.
Buddy and I both want to train deep. Can we take turns diving at the same time to save time?

No, never dive at the same time. Your buddy's whole job is to watch you from the surface and be ready to reach you. Stick to one-up, one-down: one person dives while the other watches, then meets them partway up on deeper dives and stays close for 30 seconds after they surface. It takes longer, but it's the system that actually saves lives.
is it bad to train parkour every day

Training every single day at full intensity is a common way to get overuse injuries, especially in your knees, shins, and wrists, which adapt much more slowly than muscles. Three to four hard sessions a week, with lighter days of mobility, balance, or technique work in between, is a better long-term setup. If you really want to move every day, just make some of those days low impact. Persistent soreness that doesn't go away overnight is a sign to scale back.
is dehydration really a big deal in motocross or is that overhyped

It's a real deal. Motocross is brutally physical, and you sweat a lot in full gear, especially in heat. Even moderate dehydration slows your reactions and leads to arm pump and mistakes. Drink water or electrolytes before, during and after riding, and take breaks between motos. If you get dizzy, get a headache or stop sweating, stop riding immediately.
can i freedive the day after scuba diving

Yes, but leave a real gap first. After scuba you still have extra nitrogen in your body, and deep freediving on top of that can raise your risk of decompression sickness. Most guidance says to wait at least 12 to 24 hours after scuba before doing any serious freediving. Freediving before scuba is generally the safer order if you're doing both on the same trip.
Is it fine if I stop sweating late in the race? Seems efficient lol

No, stopping sweating in the heat is a serious warning sign, not efficiency, because it can mean you're severely dehydrated or heading toward heat stroke. Stop, get into shade, cool down aggressively, drink with electrolytes and get to medical staff. Don't try to push through to the next aid station if you're also feeling confused, dizzy or chilled.
my instructor wants to fail me on the lost line drill even though i found the line eventually. thats ridiculous right

I'd trust your instructor here. In a real lost line situation, time, gas and calm searching technique are what get you out, not just eventually finding the line. Ask them exactly where it fell apart, like your search pattern, tie-off or gas use, and repeat the drill until it's clean. Better to struggle in training than in a real cave.
can a jet ski driver learn rescue on youtube?

Videos help with concepts, but rescue driving in big surf is a skill you have to practice hands-on with instruction. Take a PWC rescue course with in-water drills, since timing pickups in the impact zone is hard to judge without real experience. Practice first on smaller days with experienced drivers.
my friend says drink a gallon of water the morning of the race to pre-hydrate

Don't do that. Chugging a gallon won't store extra water; it just sends you to the bathroom and can start you off with diluted sodium. Drink normally the day before, have about 500 ml with some salt a couple of hours before the start, and go to the line with pale-yellow urine.
how fast do street lugers actually go

Top racers on steep, closed courses can hit 60 to 70 mph, and record attempts have gone past 90. Most recreational and beginner riders are well below that, often in the 20 to 40 mph range while learning. Those big numbers come with full leathers, purpose-built sleds and fully closed roads with safety crews.
Can I use a pool noodle for open water swims instead of buying a swim buoy?

Not really. A noodle doesn't make you visible to boats, it can drift away in wind, and it's awkward to drag along while swimming. A proper tow float is cheap, clips to your waist, is bright orange so boats and spotters can see you, and gives you something solid to rest on if you get tired. It's one of the best-value bits of safety gear you can buy.
Pregnant (20 weeks), used to sea swim a lot. Can I keep going?

Many people carry on swimming through pregnancy, but check with your midwife or doctor, especially about cold water, because your circulation and core temperature behave differently now. Choose calmer, warmer days, keep your swims shorter, and always go with someone rather than solo. Get out as soon as you feel too cold, too tired or unwell in any way.
How windy is too windy to jump?

For students, most dropzones stop jumps when ground winds pass about 14 to 18 mph, and they also watch for gusts, because turbulence near landing is the real danger. Licensed jumpers have more leeway, but gusty, turbulent conditions catch experienced people out too. If the dropzone holds the load for weather, trust their call rather than pushing to go.
best shoes for free soloing?

Soloists usually pick a comfortable, all-day shoe they can trust on long routes, something like a La Sportiva TC Pro or Katana, sized for comfort rather than painful precision. Honestly, though, gear barely matters next to experience and judgment, so I'd put that money toward guided days or a trad rack. Those will move your climbing forward with the rope still on.
Bought a used wing online for cheap, never taken a lesson. How hard can it be to just run off a hill near my house?

Harder and more dangerous than it looks, because launching is the easy part and reading the air, handling a collapse and landing safely are what actually keep you alive. Self-taught pilots get hurt at a far higher rate, often on their first few flights when a gust lifts them before they know how to control the wing. Book a course with a certified school, which usually takes 8 to 12 days for a novice rating, and have them inspect that used wing too, since old or porous fabric can behave badly even for experienced pilots.
how long do i need to wait to dive after getting a tattoo

Wait until it's fully healed, which is usually two to four weeks, before getting it in the ocean or a pool. A fresh tattoo is an open wound, and seawater can bring in bacteria and infection, besides wrecking the ink. Follow your artist's healing timeline, and plan the tattoo for after your trip if you can.
honestly how bad is it to dive with a head cold if I take sudafed first

Pretty bad, and the decongestant is what makes it sneaky. Sudafed can wear off mid-dive, which leaves you with a reverse block on ascent, and that can mean a ruptured eardrum or sinus squeeze. If you can't equalize comfortably without medication, sit the dive out and wait until you're clear.
Can I do parkour in regular running shoes or do I need special ones?

Running shoes work fine to start, but look for a pair with a flat, grippy sole and not too much cushioning, because thick heels make it harder to feel walls and edges. Dedicated parkour shoes or minimal trainers give better grip and ground feel as you progress. Just avoid smooth soles or worn-out tread, since slipping off a wall or rail is a common way people get hurt.
can i skate downhill in the rain

You can, but it's a different sport. Grip drops sharply, slides become unpredictable, and painted lines and metal covers get super slick. If you want to try it, go much slower than normal on a hill you know well. Better yet, wait until the road dries.
can you bungee after drinking a couple beers to calm nerves

No, and any decent operator will turn you away if they smell it. Alcohol affects your blood pressure and coordination and makes nausea and blackouts more likely when you're hanging upside down. It also impairs your ability to follow instructions at the edge. Use breathing to calm your nerves and save the beers for the celebration afterward.
how do you tell if a frozen waterfall is safe to climb

Look for ice that's bonded to the rock, solid blue or white rather than gray and slushy, and thick enough to take full-length screws without hitting rock. Hollow booming sounds, running water behind the ice, cracks along the base, or detached pillars are all red flags. Watch the temperatures too, because a big warm spell or bright sun on south-facing ice can turn a solid route into a falling hazard by mid-afternoon. If you're new to judging conditions, check local reports and go with someone who knows that specific area, since reading ice takes real experience.
My buddy bailed. Ocean is perfectly calm today and I'm experienced. Going out solo just for some easy dives, it's fine right?

Experience doesn't protect you from blackout, and calm water doesn't either. Some of the most experienced freedivers in the world have died diving alone on easy days. If you black out with nobody there, it's almost always fatal. Snorkel at the surface today if you want to be in the water, but save the dives for when you have a buddy.
There's a flooded mine near my house. Same as a cave right? I'm cave certified.

Not quite; flooded mines bring their own hazards, like unstable ceilings, rotting timbers, old machinery, sharp debris and sometimes poor water quality. Cave certification gives you the core skills, but you should get local knowledge or a mine-specific orientation before diving one, and make sure you have legal permission from the owner. Many abandoned mines are off-limits for good reason, so check before you plan anything.
Is it OK to boulder outdoors without a crash pad if the landing looks flat?

Bring a pad anyway, because even a flat dirt landing hits much harder than you'd expect from a few meters up, and ankles, wrists and tailbones take the impact. Hidden rocks, roots and uneven ground make it worse. If you don't own one yet, borrow or rent one, or go with a group that pads up, and have a spotter guide your fall onto it. Without a pad, keep it to very low traversing.
Are there medical conditions that would stop someone from surfing big waves?

Yes. Heart conditions, epilepsy and anything that could cause a blackout are serious concerns, and so are recent concussions or lung problems. Big-wave wipeouts push your body and breath to the limit, so check in with a doctor, ideally one familiar with diving or extreme sports, before you commit.
I found an underwater cave entrance while snorkeling in Croatia. I've got my scuba gear. Worth a quick peek inside solo?

Don't do it, because a solo, unplanned entry into an unknown cave with open water gear and no guideline is exactly how strong divers die. You have no idea about the flow, the silt or the restrictions, and nobody would know where to look for you. Mark the spot and ask local dive centers whether it's a known site, since a trained cave diver might take you to explore the cavern zone safely.
Can I learn BASE from YouTube videos and just figure it out?

No. Videos skip the object assessment, packing details and malfunction responses that actually keep people alive, and they mostly show successful jumps. Packing mistakes or a misjudged landing area kill self-taught jumpers. Take a First Jump Course and find a mentor who will watch you pack and critique your decisions.
can i use my hiking boots with strap-on crampons for a WI3 route

Not a good idea. Flexible hiking boots let strap-on crampons twist and pop off when you front-point, and on steep water ice that can mean a fall. For WI3 you want stiff, insulated boots rated for semi-automatic or automatic crampons. Rent a proper pair before you try it, because the right boots make the climbing safer and a lot easier.
Salt tabs, how many per hour?

There's no universal number, because sweat sodium varies a lot from person to person. A common starting range is 300 to 600 mg of sodium per hour in hot conditions, counting what's in your drinks and food, not just the tabs. Practice it in hot training runs, and if you're a heavy, salty sweater (white crust on your hat), a sweat test can help you dial it in.
can i just watch youtube videos and do a solo jump without the course? i learn fast

No, and no legitimate dropzone will let you, because solo jumping without training is one of the quickest ways to get killed in this sport. The first jump course teaches emergency procedures, canopy control and landing, and you need to practice them physically, not just watch them. If you learn fast, an AFF program will move you along quickly anyway, and you could be jumping solo within a week or two of good weather.
I panicked in the water last time and felt like I couldn't breathe. Do I give up?

Not at all; that's really common, especially in cold or open water, and it's very fixable. Next time, start in shallow water where you can stand, and focus on long, slow exhales before you even start swimming. If panic hits, roll onto your back, float and breathe until it passes. A coached open-water session or a beginner group can help a lot, because having someone experienced beside you rebuilds confidence fast.
Lost my line in a silt out during training today and panicked. Instructor got me but I'm shaken. Should I quit?

Being shaken is normal, and it's exactly why these scenarios are practiced in training with an instructor right there. Talk it through honestly with your instructor, because they can tell you whether this is a skill gap to drill or a sign to slow down. Lots of excellent cave divers had a rough moment early on and came back stronger after more no-visibility line drills in controlled conditions, but it's also completely fine to decide cavern diving is your limit.
Can I wingsuit off the cliffs in Lauterbrunnen on vacation? I've done 50 wingsuit skydives.

With 50 wingsuit skydives and no BASE background, that's not a good idea. Lauterbrunnen has claimed many experienced jumpers, and wingsuit BASE requires its own training and progression on top of significant BASE experience. If you want to work toward it, take a proper BASE course, build object experience, and come back years later with local guidance.
Is it okay to do a cave dive when I'm a bit hungover?

Skip it. Even a mild hangover slows reaction time, dehydrates you and raises your risk of narcosis and decompression stress, and cave diving gives you no quick escape to the surface. Rest, hydrate and dive tomorrow; the cave will still be there.
First triathlon next month, never swum in open water. Is a month enough to prepare?

A month can work if you get in open water several times before race day, not just the pool. Practice sighting, swimming in a wetsuit, and handling a crowded start, ideally at an organized open water session with lifeguards. On race day, start at the back or the side to avoid the washing machine. It's fine to breaststroke or rest on a kayak if you need to, because race safety crews are there exactly for that.
I'm an open water certified diver with about 40 dives. Can I just follow my buddy into a cenote cave if he's cave certified?

No, and his certification doesn't extend to you, because cave training exists precisely so each diver can handle their own emergency when there's no surface to bolt for. Open water divers who follow experienced friends into overhead environments make up a grim share of cave fatalities. If you want to see the cenotes, book a guided cavern tour that stays within the daylight zone, or start a cavern course, which is the proper first step toward full cave certification.
first tandem jump next saturday and i'm honestly terrified. is it normal to feel this sick about it?

Completely normal, and most tandem students say the dread beforehand was worse than the jump itself. Your instructor has usually done hundreds or thousands of jumps and handles the parachute, so your job is mainly to arch, breathe and enjoy the view. Eat a light breakfast, skip the alcohol the night before, and tell your instructor you're nervous, because they're very good at talking people through it.
35, out of shape, want to try downhill. too old?

Not at all; lots of people start downhill in their thirties and forties and do great. Your body just heals slower, so prioritize gear, mellow hills, and building skills step by step instead of chasing speed early. Some leg and core strength work and a bit of stretching will help a lot with balance and tucking. Find a local crew or a learn-to-slide session, and older beginners often progress faster than kids because they're patient.
how do i do a wet exit

Tuck forward toward the deck to protect your face, find the spray skirt grab loop, then pull it forward and up to pop the skirt. Push off the boat with your hands at your hips as if taking off pants, and roll out forward, keeping hold of the boat and paddle if you can. Practice it in a calm pool or lake with someone standing by until it feels automatic.
I've done like 40 skydives. Can I just start BASE jumping now or do I need more?

Forty jumps isn't close to enough. Most reputable first jump courses want at least 200 skydives, and many experienced jumpers say 250 to 300 is better, because you need solid canopy skills and calm, automatic emergency responses before you try something with no reserve and very little altitude. Use the next couple hundred jumps to focus on accurate landings, canopy courses and tracking, then sign up for a proper FJC with an established instructor.
My reserve was last repacked like 3 years ago. It's probably fine right?

Get it repacked before your next flight. Most manufacturers recommend a repack every 6 to 12 months, because fabric that sits folded can stick together, take on moisture and open slower when you need it most. A reserve is the one piece of gear you can't test in the moment, so it has to be right. A rigger or your school can usually do it quickly, and many will let you watch or try a supervised throw at a repack clinic.
can I put my phone on a selfie stick while luging to film

Skip the selfie stick, because holding anything takes away your hands for steering and catching a fall, and the stick can snag or hit you in a crash. Use a small action camera mounted securely to your helmet with a breakaway mount or to the sled frame. Check it's tight before every run. Your hands should stay free for riding.
got a cramp in my calf like 300m out and panicked. how do i handle that next time

Roll onto your back, take slow breaths, and flex your foot by pulling your toes toward your shin to stretch the calf. Rest on your tow float if you have one, then swim back gently, mostly using your arms. Cramps are often linked to cold, fatigue or dehydration, so warm up, hydrate and build distance gradually. Swimming with a buddy or near a support kayak makes that moment far less scary.
is bungee jumping actually safe or am i gonna die lol

At a reputable, licensed operator it's statistically very safe, with fatalities extremely rare and almost always traced to human error like miscalculated cord length or a bad harness connection. The risk lives mostly in who you jump with, not the activity itself. Pick an established company with a long track record and visible certifications and you're in good hands.
Is speedflying basically the same as paragliding?

Same family, very different game. Speedwings are small and fast, and they fly close to the terrain at speeds where mistakes give you almost no time to react, which is why speedflying has a much higher accident rate. Most reputable schools want you to have a solid paragliding background, often 50 hours or more, before starting. Get your paragliding fundamentals first and then do a dedicated speedflying course.
Training for a 10k swim. Do I really need to eat during it or can I just push through?

You really need to fuel. A 10k takes most people two and a half to four hours, and if you run out of energy in cold water, you'll slow down, get colder and start making bad decisions. Plan feeds of carbs and fluids every 20 to 30 minutes, and practice them in training so your stomach is used to it. Have your support kayaker or boat handle the bottles.
Weight question: how much lead should I wear?

Set your weight so you're neutrally buoyant at around 10 meters, or roughly a third of your target depth if diving shallower. That way you float at the surface, which matters a lot if you black out. Being overweighted is a common and dangerous mistake. The exact amount depends on your body, wetsuit thickness and salt versus fresh water, so test it in calm conditions with your buddy.
how cold is too cold to go whitewater kayaking

There isn't a hard cutoff, but once the water drops below about 60°F (15°C), cold shock and hypothermia become real risks in a swim, and below 50°F (10°C) a long swim can incapacitate you fast. Dress for immersion, not for the air temperature, which means a drysuit for cold water, warm layers underneath, and pogies or gloves and a skull cap. Paddle with others, keep runs shorter, and keep dry clothes and a hot drink in the car. Cold-water swims are where gear really earns its keep.
quick q how deep should the water be for a 10m jump

Aim for at least 5 meters of clear depth, and more is better. Competition high-diving pools use about 5 to 6 meters for jumps from 20 meters or more, so don't cut it close at 10. Swim down and confirm the depth yourself across the whole landing area, not just one spot.
What's a silt out and how do I handle one?

A silt out is when fine sediment stirs up and drops visibility to near zero, usually because of fins, hands or bubbles. Prevention is everything: precise buoyancy, frog or modified flutter kicks, and staying off the floor. If it happens, keep or regain contact with the line, put a hand loosely around it in an 'OK' grip, and exit calmly by touch while signaling your buddy. Your cave course will make you practice this blind until it's second nature.
I'm 14, how do I convince my parents to let me bungee jump on our vacation?

Start by finding the exact operator and checking their age rule. Many set a minimum around 14 to 16, and anyone under 18 usually needs a parent's signed consent. Then show your parents the company's safety record, how they weigh you, and what harness system they use, so they can see it's a professional setup and not a random stunt. Offering to have one of them come watch, or jump with you, usually helps more than begging.
can I skip the basics? I'm already pretty athletic

Being athletic gives you a head start, but skipping basics is how athletic people get hurt in parkour. Your strength might let you reach jumps and vaults before your landing technique and joint conditioning can handle them. Spend a few weeks drilling fundamentals like precisions, rolls and vaults. You'll probably progress faster than most, just on a solid base.
I keep floating up at the end of dives. How do I fix it?

That's very common and usually comes down to two things. As your tank empties it gets more buoyant, so you may need slightly more weight. Also, people often forget to vent their BCD as they ascend. Do a proper weight check with a near-empty tank at the end of a dive, and practice slow ascents while dumping air in small bursts. A buoyancy specialty course with an instructor speeds this up a lot.
I'm diabetic (type 1) and want to do a hot ultra. Is that crazy?

Not crazy, because type 1 athletes finish ultras all the time, but heat makes insulin absorb faster and makes glucose swings harder to read, so it needs real planning. Work with your endocrinologist on basal adjustments and practice the full plan in long hot training runs with a CGM. Make sure your crew or race medical staff know your condition and how to treat a low. Carry fast carbs everywhere and check often, since heat symptoms and lows can feel similar.
My 15 year old son keeps talking about wanting to free solo like Honnold. Should I be panicking?

Not panicking, but paying attention is smart, since lots of teen climbers idolize Honnold without ever soloing. The best move is usually to channel the passion rather than forbid it, by getting him into a good youth climbing team or outdoor program where coaches teach real risk management and he earns respect for skill rather than daring. Talk openly with him about how much rope climbing and preparation Honnold did, and agree on a clear family rule about no ropeless climbing above bouldering height while he's a minor. Kids who feel heard tend to be more honest about what they're actually doing.
arm pump kills me every moto. fix?

Most arm pump comes from death-gripping the bars, so grip the bike with your knees and keep your arms loose, holding the bars just firmly enough to control them. Warm up properly with a few easy laps or some cardio before your first moto, stay well hydrated, and build your endurance with regular riding and cardio rather than just grip work. If it's still severe and it persists with good technique and conditioning, see a sports medicine doctor, because a small number of riders have chronic compartment syndrome.
hands get torn up on rails and walls. normal?

Some calluses and scrapes are normal, especially early on, but deep tears or blisters mean you're doing too much too fast. Let your skin adapt gradually, file down thick calluses so they don't rip off, and keep cuts clean so they don't get infected. Rough walls get easier as your hands toughen, but wash and moisturize them after training. If you get a deep cut with dirt or rust in it, check your tetanus status.
my ice screw went in and the ice cracked all around it, keep going?

Don't trust that screw. Back it out and place a new one in a fresh spot, ideally after clearing away the brittle surface layer. Dinner-plating and radiating cracks mean the ice around the screw can't hold a real load. Look for concave or more solid areas, and if the whole route is fracturing like that, it's too brittle to lead safely today and backing off is the smart call.
pregnant, 10 weeks. friend booked us a bungee jump as a surprise. can i still do it

No, skip this one. Operators universally exclude pregnant jumpers because the forces and jolt pose real risks, and it's a firm rule at reputable sites. Tell your friend thanks and see if you can swap to watching, filming, or rescheduling for after the baby. Most operators will transfer a booking if you ask.
how do I tuck properly

Put your front foot pointing forward and your back knee tucked behind your front calf, then fold your chest down over your front knee with your back straight and arms behind you. Keep your head up so you can still see the road well ahead. Practice it on a mellow hill until you can hold it relaxed, because a tense tuck makes wobbles worse.
what's the fastest way to cool down mid race

Ice is your best friend: stuff it in a bandana around your neck, under your hat, and in arm sleeves, and dump cold water over your head and torso at every aid station. Wetting your skin so evaporation does the work is far more effective than just drinking cold fluids. If you're overheating, also slow down or walk, because no cooling trick beats lowering how much heat your muscles are producing.
what's a good first spot type to learn on

A supervised venue is ideal, like a pool with 3 to 5 meter platforms, or a guided coasteering trip where instructors already know the depths and exits. If you're going natural, pick a calm, popular spot with clear deep water, an easy climb out and a low ledge. Skip anything remote, murky or with surf.
My son just told me he wants to get into wingsuit BASE jumping. He's 24. I'm terrified. What should I know?

Your fear makes sense, because wingsuit BASE has a much higher fatality rate than skydiving and most deaths come from flying too close to terrain. The responsible path takes years: hundreds of skydives, extensive wingsuit skydiving experience, a proper BASE first jump course, and then a long, slow progression on established exits with experienced mentors. If he's willing to follow that kind of patient progression, that's a good sign, and it's worth asking him calmly what his plan looks like.
Detailed question: my son is 14 and keeps getting kicked out of the local plaza by security. He says there's no skatepark nearby. What can we actually do about this?

The plaza is private or managed property, so the real fix is getting him somewhere legal rather than fighting security. Look for DIY spots, indoor parks, or school and church lots where you can get explicit permission. Many cities have built skateparks because parents and kids showed up to council meetings with petitions, and groups like the Skatepark Project offer free resources for that kind of campaign. Meanwhile a couple of portable ramps and a rail in your driveway can keep him progressing without trouble.
Is skydiving actually dangerous or is that overblown?

It's riskier than everyday activities but safer than most people assume, since US fatality rates have dropped to roughly one in several hundred thousand jumps in recent years. Tandems have an especially good record because of experienced instructors and automatic activation devices. Most serious injuries among licensed jumpers come from canopy errors near the ground, not parachute failures, which is why training and good judgment matter so much.
best way to learn drops

Start with small drops no higher than a curb, where the landing is smooth and clear. Roll toward the edge at moderate speed, stay centered and relaxed, and push the bike forward slightly as the front wheel leaves the lip so you land both wheels together or rear wheel first. Never brake at the lip, because that pitches you forward. Increase height gradually, and a skills coach can fix bad habits before they cost you on a bigger drop.
Just got off my first flight course and I tumbled on exit. Embarrassed. Normal?

Completely normal, and nothing to be embarrassed about. A huge share of first-flight students get unstable on exit, usually from flaring the wings too early or not presenting the hips to the relative wind. Debrief the video with your instructor, focus on a clean, symmetrical exit and the habit of de-arming before you pull, and do a few more coached jumps. You'll likely see big improvement within a handful of flights.
ok so how do I do a palm spin over a wall

Place both hands on the top of the wall with one hand turned slightly outward, kick your legs up and to the side, and let your body spin around your planted hand as you rotate your hips. Start on a low wall or box at waist height and go slowly, focusing on leading with your hips rather than your feet. Practice both directions and land facing forward with soft knees. Make sure the wall is solid and the top is not crumbling.
can I sharpen my crampons with a bench grinder

It's better to sharpen them by hand with a file. A grinder can overheat the steel and ruin its temper, making the points soft or brittle. File in the direction the points were originally ground, keep the bevels the same, and don't overdo it, because points that are too sharp and thin break more easily. A shop can do it for you if you're unsure.
Wear contacts. Will they fly out?

Contacts usually stay put, especially soft ones, but there's a small chance one shifts or pops out from the airflow and pressure. Many jumpers just blink a lot or keep their eyes shut at the bottom. If losing one would ruin your trip, bring spares. Glasses should come off unless the operator provides a strap, and even then most recommend leaving them behind.
What do I do if I get a cramp way out in the lake?

Roll onto your back and float, which keeps your airway clear while you deal with it. Try to stretch the muscle, for example by pulling your toes toward your shin for a calf cramp, and wave or shout to your buddy or kayaker. A tow buoy really earns its keep here, because you can rest on it while the cramp eases. Staying hydrated and fueled and warming up before you swim makes cramps less likely in the first place.
There's a cliff near my house that looks perfect for launching. No one flies there. Should I try it?

I wouldn't, at least not on your own. Sites no one flies often have hidden problems like rotor, bad landing options, power lines or access and legal restrictions. Get in touch with a local club or experienced pilots, who will usually know why it isn't used or can help you assess it properly. Plenty of good sites were opened by careful scouting, but that's a group effort, not a solo experiment.
Is it ok to dive a cave right after heavy rain?

Often it's not a good idea, because heavy rain can turn springs into siphons, increase flow, drop visibility and send tannic water into the system. Some caves, especially in Florida, can reverse or become dangerous for days after storms. Check local conditions with the dive shop or site staff, and if they say flow or visibility is off, wait.
Is it safe to fly wingsuit formations with strangers at a boogie?

It can be, if everyone attends the briefing and the organizers group people by experience level. Make sure you know the flight plan, breakoff altitude, and your spot in the formation before you board. If you feel like you're getting pushed into a bigger formation or larger suit than you're comfortable with, say so and fly a smaller group.
What happens if I black out during freefall??

Fainting during a tandem is rare, but the instructor deploys the canopy and lands for you whatever happens. Student and sport rigs carry an automatic activation device that fires the reserve at low altitude if you're still falling fast. If you have a history of fainting or seizures, tell the dropzone and your doctor before jumping, because that can change what's safe for you.
Someone in our group got stuck in a hole for like 10 sec and was fine. How do we prep for next time?

Good on you for treating it as a warning sign rather than a funny story. Get everyone into a swiftwater rescue course, since throw bag skills, positioning safety below features and knowing how to swim out of a hydraulic are learned skills. Before each rapid, agree on who sets safety and where, and portage holes that look sticky or have bad consequences.
quick one: helmet or no helmet in big surf

Helmet, especially at reef or rocky breaks. A board or reef impact to the head can knock you unconscious, and that's what turns a wipeout into a drowning. A lot of serious big-wave surfers wear them now, and it's a cheap insurance policy.
is it fine to skate without a helmet if I'm just cruising around my neighborhood?

Cruising is actually when a lot of serious head injuries happen. A pebble or crack stops your wheels and you get pitched forward with no time to react, and the pavement doesn't care how chill your ride was. A lightweight certified skate helmet costs about as much as a set of wheels, so just wear it. Your brain doesn't heal the way a scraped elbow does.
My 12 year old wants to start doing parkour after watching YouTube videos and I'm terrified he's going to jump off roofs. What should I do?

Your instinct to get ahead of this is right. The best move is to sign him up at a parkour gym or a class with certified coaches, where he'll learn landings, rolls and progressions on mats instead of copying stunts from videos. Good coaches also teach the culture of the sport, which actually discourages rooftop stuff and emphasizes training low and controlled. Have a clear family rule that roofs and heights are off-limits, and kids usually find the gym challenges plenty exciting.
what to bring for a cliff diving day trip

Bring water shoes, a wetsuit if the water is cold, goggles for checking depth, water and snacks, sun protection, and a charged phone in a dry bag. A small first aid kit and a buddy who stays on shore to watch are worth a lot. Know where the nearest road access is in case you need help.
I felt dizzy after a jump yesterday and still have a headache. Is that normal?

No, a lingering headache and dizziness after a jump can be a sign of a concussion or an ear injury, especially if you hit the water hard or at an angle. See a doctor today, and go to the emergency room if you notice confusion, vomiting, blurred vision or worsening symptoms. Skip jumping until you've been checked and your symptoms are completely gone.
how do i ollie higher, mine are like 2 inches off the ground

Height comes from snapping the tail hard and then sliding your front foot up toward the nose while pulling your knees up to your chest. Most people stuck at a couple inches either don't crouch low enough before popping or leave their front foot flat instead of dragging it. Practice on grass or carpet first so the board doesn't roll away, then take it to smooth pavement once the timing clicks.
What's a 'restriction' and should I be worried about them?

A restriction is a tight spot where you can't pass side by side with your buddy, or sometimes can barely fit with your gear. They're manageable with training but much riskier, because sharing air through them is hard and silt-outs there are common. Many agencies limit restrictions until you hold full cave certification, so stick to your training level and turn around if a passage looks tighter than you're trained for.
We found a river spot with a 12m ledge, the water looks dark and deep. Good enough?

Dark water tells you nothing about depth, it just means you can't see what's down there. Rivers move logs, boulders and debris after every storm, so someone needs to swim down and check the exact landing zone that day, ideally with a mask. Also look at the current, since even a modest flow can pull a winded jumper under. If you can't verify it, find a lower, known spot instead.
first time at a bike park next weekend, rented a full sus downhill bike. what should I actually wear?

Wear a full-face helmet, knee pads at minimum, and gloves. Most parks rent full-face helmets and body armor if you don't own them, and it's worth it. Add long sleeves or elbow pads and flat-soled shoes with grippy soles if you're on flat pedals. Eye protection like goggles or glasses keeps dust and roost out, which matters more than people expect on dry days.
whats the deal with wingsuit BASE, how long till i can do that

Plan on years, not months. The usual path is around 200 or more skydiving wingsuit flights, a solid BASE background with somewhere near 200 jumps, and then starting on established exits with big clearance and a mentor who knows the line. Proximity flying is where most wingsuit deaths happen, and it should only come after a lot of experience, if ever. Anyone telling you to shortcut that timeline is not someone to fly with.
what does PCA mean in base

PCA stands for Pilot Chute Assist. A ground crew member holds your pilot chute or bridle as you exit, so the canopy deploys almost immediately with no freefall. Instructors often use it on early jumps or low objects to take timing and throw errors out of the picture. It's a good training tool, but your helper has to know exactly what they're doing.
can i surf with a broken pinky finger

If it's a simple, stable fracture and your doctor has buddy-taped or splinted it, some people do paddle gently. The real risks are popping up off a bent finger, getting rag-dolled by a wave, and soaking the splint so it stops doing its job. Ask whoever set it whether it's stable, and use a waterproof splint if they give you the okay. Expect two to three weeks of patience before you're hitting real surf again.
Ankle harness or body harness for a first-timer?

Either is fine at a good operator, and many first-timers use a full-body harness because it feels more secure and is gentler on joints with a more upright rebound. Ankle attachment gives the classic swan-dive feel and is usually backed up with a body harness anyway. If you have ankle, knee or hip issues, go full-body.
Do I really need knee pads? They're hot and I ride slow anyway

Yes, wear them, because even slow-speed downhill crashes land on rocks and roots and knees take the hit almost every time. Modern lightweight pads with breathable sleeves are barely noticeable once you're moving, so if your current ones are miserable, try a different model rather than ditching them. A gashed or cracked kneecap ends your season; a sweaty leg doesn't.
Terse question: shovel. Plastic or metal blade?
Metal, always. Avalanche debris sets up like concrete and plastic blades bounce off or crack, which costs you minutes you don't have. Get one with an extendable shaft and a decent-sized blade.
is a neck brace worth it or just marketing

The evidence isn't conclusive, but a lot of pros and doctors use them, and they're designed to limit extreme head movement in crashes that can injure the neck. A properly fitted one from Leatt, Atlas or Alpinestars is a reasonable investment if you jump or race. Fit matters a lot, so try it on with your helmet and chest protector before you buy. It's not magic, though, and riding within your limits still does more for your safety than any single piece of gear.
Can I just wear my regular life jacket from the lake for kayaking rivers?

Your lake jacket is better than nothing, but a proper whitewater PFD is worth it. They fit snugly so they don't ride up over your face in a swim, have more buoyancy for aerated water, and are cut for paddling movement. Many also have a rescue harness, though you should only use that after training. Get one fitted in a shop and do the shoulder-pull test to make sure it stays put.
is it fine to freedive alone if I stay shallow, like 5 meters max?

No, shallow water blackout happens most often in exactly that range, because the pressure drop on the last few meters of ascent is what makes you lose consciousness, and it gives no warning. A diver who blacks out at 5 meters alone drowns in a couple of minutes. Always dive with a trained buddy who watches you from the surface and stays with you for at least 30 seconds after you surface.
can i wear a wingsuit with my student rig

Generally no, because large student mains and some student containers aren't suited to wingsuit deployments and can be unpleasant or dangerous to open with a suit. Your instructor will want a well-maintained container that deploys cleanly with a wingsuit and a canopy you can comfortably land. Talk with your rigger and First Flight Course instructor before buying gear so it actually works together.
how do you read a river from the boat

Look for downstream Vs, which mark the main channel. Upstream Vs point to rocks or obstacles, and a smooth horizon line means a drop you can't see over. Eddies behind rocks are your parking spots, and boils or pillows show water hitting something underneath. If you see a horizon line or can't see the line clearly, eddy out and scout from shore.
ok so how cold is too cold to paddle without a drysuit

A common rule is that if air and water temperature add up to under about 120°F, you need a drysuit or at least a proper wetsuit, and many paddlers want a drysuit any time the water is below roughly 60°F. Cold-water shock can make you gasp and lose control in the first minute of a swim, well before hypothermia sets in. Dress for the swim, not the air temperature.
how high should i pull on a wingsuit skydive

Most drop zones set wingsuit deployment around 4,000 to 5,000 feet, and beginners should be on the higher end. Wingsuit pulls take a bit more time because you have to stabilize and get your arms clear. Follow your drop zone's rules and your instructor's recommendation, and never stretch a flight past your planned break-off altitude to chase more distance.
Do you need a license to wingsuit?

There isn't a separate government license in most places, but dropzones control who flies, usually requiring a skydiving license, around 200 jumps and a First Flight Course with a qualified instructor. Some countries and organizations also have wingsuit ratings or endorsements. Check with your local dropzone for the exact requirements.
My shoulder pops sometimes when I brace hard. Push through it?

Don't push through it. Shoulder dislocations are a classic whitewater injury, and a joint that already pops is at higher risk, especially on high braces with your arm extended. See a sports physio or orthopedist before paddling hard again, and in the meantime work on low braces with your elbows tucked close to your body, which protects the shoulder.
Pacing tips for my first hot ultra? I'm a strong road marathoner.

Throw out your road pace and run by effort and heart rate instead, because heat can add a lot to the cost of every mile. Start much slower than feels necessary, walk the hills early, and expect your pace to drop 10 to 20 percent or more in real heat. The runners who finish strong in hot ultras are almost always the ones who started embarrassingly easy.
whats a good first downhill setup

Look for a stable drop-through or top-mount deck with medium flex, reverse-kingpin trucks with moderately tight bushings, and 70mm to 75mm wheels in the 78a to 80a range. That combination is easy to control, forgiving on wobbles, and good for learning slides. Add a certified full-face helmet, slide gloves and pads before you put money into upgrades.
What's the difference between HAPE and HACE in plain English?

HAPE is fluid building up in the lungs, so you'll see breathlessness even at rest, a persistent cough that sometimes brings up frothy or pink sputum, and a performance drop that's way beyond normal tiredness. HACE is swelling of the brain, and it shows up as confusion, odd behavior, severe headache, and loss of coordination, such as being unable to walk heel-to-toe in a straight line. Both can kill within hours, and the most important treatment for either one is immediate descent, ideally with oxygen and medical help.
Me and my wife are in our 50s, fit, want to start ski touring. Where do we even begin?

Start with a guided intro tour or a hut trip with a certified guide, which lets you learn skinning, kick turns and transitions while someone experienced handles terrain decisions. Then take an AIARE 1 or similar avalanche course together and practice beacon searches. Plenty of people take this up in their 50s, and building skills step by step is how you keep it fun and safe.
Can I set up a top rope anchor around one tree? It's a huge tree

A big, healthy, living, well-rooted tree is widely accepted as a solid single natural anchor, so yes, that can be fine. Check that it isn't dead or loose at the roots, use a sling or static line around the base rather than high up the trunk, and keep the setup redundant with locking carabiners at the master point. Have your edge protection sorted where the rope runs over rock. If you haven't built anchors before, learn this hands-on from a guide or instructor first, because anchor mistakes are rarely survivable.
Is paragliding more dangerous than skydiving?

Statistics vary, but recreational paragliding is generally considered riskier per hour than skydiving, mostly because pilots fly longer and in more variable weather and terrain. Most accidents are tied to pilot decisions, like flying in strong or turbulent conditions or flying beyond their skill. Good training, conservative weather choices and staying on a suitable wing drop your risk significantly.
I'm 58, a bit overweight, and on blood pressure meds. Can I still learn to dive?

Plenty of people your age learn to dive and love it, but you'll need a doctor to sign off first. The standard diver medical questionnaire flags blood pressure medication for review. Try to see a physician familiar with dive medicine, since some meds affect exercise tolerance or heat regulation. Once you're cleared, a good instructor will let you take things at a comfortable pace.
I keep casing the big double at my local track. Should I just hit it faster?

Adding speed without fixing your technique usually turns a case into an overshoot or a crash, so don't just pin it. Casing often comes from rolling off the throttle on the face, sitting down too early, or a bad drive out of the previous corner, so work on a smooth, consistent run-up and staying on the gas through the lip. Watch where faster riders start their approach and copy their line and gear. Building up in small increments over several sessions is much safer than one big send.
Worried mom here. My daughter (24) is an experienced climber and just told me she's started soloing. I'm terrified. What do I say?

As an adult and experienced climber, she'll make her own choice, so the most useful thing is usually to stay close rather than push her away with ultimatums. Tell her honestly that you're scared and you love her, then ask questions that get her thinking, like how she picks routes, what her margin is, and what makes her back off. Many climbers soften their approach when they feel respected rather than judged. It's also fair to ask her to always tell someone where she's going, and to agree on a check-in plan.
how fast do street luge riders actually go? like real numbers

Competitive street luge riders regularly hit 60 to 80 mph on race courses, and the fastest recorded runs have gone past 90 mph on purpose-built steep roads. Most recreational riders on closed hills sit somewhere between 30 and 50 mph, which is already plenty when your body is inches off the asphalt. Those top speeds only happen on closed, swept courses with hay bales and corner marshals, never on open roads.
I keep going over the bars on drops. what am i doing wrong

That's almost always from rolling off the drop with your weight forward, or nose-diving because you grabbed the front brake. Approach with a little more speed than feels comfortable. Shift your hips back as the front wheel leaves, then pull the bike up slightly so both wheels land together or the rear lands first. Go back to drops of a foot or two until it's automatic, and get a coach to film you if you can.
Can I learn cave diving from YouTube and practice with my buddy who's done it before?

No, this is one area where informal training gets people killed. Videos can't teach you to run a line, handle a silt-out, share air in zero visibility or keep your trim tight enough to avoid stirring up the floor, and those skills need drilling under an instructor's watch. Watch videos for background, but take a proper cavern and cave course with a certified instructor before you go anywhere beyond daylight.
best spots in Europe to solo?

I'd steer you toward great places to climb rather than to solo, because the right solo terrain depends entirely on routes you already know deeply. Kalymnos, Siurana, Arco and the Frankenjura are fantastic for roped sport climbing. Mallorca is world-famous for deep water soloing over the sea, which is the safer way to climb ropeless, but go with local knowledge of tides and depths.
how should i hit berms faster without washing out

Look through the berm to the exit, get your braking done before you enter, and then let off completely so the tires can grip. Drop your outside foot slightly, keep your hips low, and push the bike into the berm wall rather than leaning your body over. Speed comes from carrying momentum through the turn, so build it up gradually lap by lap instead of charging in and grabbing the brakes mid-corner.
What's the deal with the rule about flying perpendicular to jump run?

Wingsuiters usually fly a pattern that takes them away from where other jumpers are falling and opening, often flying out perpendicular or offset to the line of flight and then back. Because you travel horizontally much farther than regular skydivers, flying the wrong direction can put you right in the path of opening canopies. Every dropzone has its own flight plan, so always get it briefed before you jump.
I'm claustrophobic but cave diving looks amazing. Should I try?

Try a guided cavern dive first, where you stay within sight of daylight and the passages are large. That's a low-stakes way to learn how your mind reacts under an overhead. If you feel calm and curious, a cavern course is a good next step. If you feel panic creeping in, take that seriously, because panic underground is genuinely dangerous.
My friend says you should never swim in the sea when there's a red flag but surely if you stay close to shore it's fine?

A red flag means conditions are dangerous for everyone, and that includes the shallows, where powerful shore breaks and rips often do their worst damage. Plenty of people get into trouble in water only waist deep when a wave knocks them off their feet and the backwash drags them out. Your friend is right, so stay out of the water and enjoy the beach until the flags change.
what does pee color tell me during a race

Pale yellow means you're in good shape. Dark amber means you need more fluid. Peeing nothing for hours is a warning sign. Brown, cola-colored urine can mean rhabdomyolysis or kidney trouble, so stop and get to the medics immediately.
i'm pregnant (about 10 weeks) and booked a tandem for a bday trip before I knew. still okay?

You should cancel or reschedule. Dropzones won't take pregnant jumpers because opening shock, harness pressure and hard landings pose real risks at any stage of pregnancy. Most places will happily move your booking or refund you, so explain the situation, and congratulations.
my instructor said I'm not ready for high flights yet but my buddy who flies says I am. who's right

Go with your instructor. They've watched every one of your launches and landings and know your weak spots, while your buddy is going on enthusiasm and a few shared sessions. Ask your instructor exactly what you need to improve to move up, and focus on that. A few extra training days now cost much less than learning a lesson the hard way.
my friend says hyperventilating before a dive lets you stay down way longer. true?

It does let you stay down longer, and that's exactly the danger. Hyperventilating blows off CO2, which is what triggers your urge to breathe, so your oxygen can drop to blackout levels before your body warns you. Use a calm, relaxed breathe-up instead, and keep the final breath full but not forced. That's what every reputable freediving course teaches.
how do i get over my fear of heights so i can solo stuff

Fear on a climb is useful information, so the aim is to make it accurate rather than to get rid of it. Work through it on a rope with lots of practice falls in a gym, guided by a coach, until your nervous system learns which situations are actually dangerous. That process takes months or years, and it makes you a much better roped climber. If you're still fighting serious fear, you're not ready to solo, and that's simply honest feedback.
How dangerous is a canopy collision with other wingsuiters?

Freefall collisions are a real risk in group flying, which is why every formation needs a clear plan, defined break-off, and pilots spread out before deploying. Wingsuiters cover a lot of ground horizontally, so jump run order and flight pattern matter to keep you away from other groups. Brief every jump, stick to the plan, and if you lose sight of someone, assume they're close and move away.
My 16 year old daughter wants to run a 50 mile race in Arizona this summer. She's been running cross country for 3 years. Is that OK?

Most ultras require racers to be 18 or older, and some extreme heat events have even stricter entry rules. A 50 miler in Arizona summer heat is a big jump from cross country for anyone. A better path is building up through shorter trail races in milder weather over a couple of years, with a coach who understands long-distance training for teenagers. Her endurance base is a great start, but the heat and distance combination carries real risk.
Is it worth getting a certification or can I just watch YouTube videos?

Get the certification. Videos are fine for learning theory, but a course teaches you how to rescue someone, recognize blackout and sambas, and get feedback on your technique in the water, and you can't learn any of that from a screen. A Level 1 or equivalent course only takes a couple of days, and it's the best thing you can do for your safety in this sport.
How do I deal with an off-heading opening off a cliff??

Your first job is to fly away from the wall, right away. Look toward open air, grab the rear riser on the side away from the wall, and pull hard to turn, then go to toggles once you're clear. Practice this as a reflex in skydives and on easy objects, because the time between opening and impact can be about a second. A First Jump Course will drill this with you, and that's the right way to learn it.
Kids ages 10 and 12, want to trek to EBC as a family. Too young?

Families with kids that age do trek to Everest Base Camp, but children may be less able to describe altitude symptoms, so parents need to watch closely for changes in mood, appetite, sleep and energy. Choose a longer itinerary with extra rest days and be ready to turn back without pressure if anyone gets sick. Talk to a pediatrician before the trip, and consider a lower trek like Annapurna Poon Hill as a safer, still amazing alternative.
terse q: how long is freefall on a tandem
Usually about 45 to 60 seconds from around 13,000 to 14,000 feet. After the parachute opens, the canopy ride lasts roughly 5 to 7 minutes.
how long till i can kickflip

For most people it takes somewhere between a few weeks and a few months of regular practice, and it depends a lot on how solid your ollie is first. Get your ollie consistent and decently high, then practice the flick while stationary on grass or carpet to learn the foot motion. After that it's mostly repetition, so short daily sessions usually beat occasional marathon ones.
My partner has frostnip on her toes at 5000m. Rub them to warm?

Don't rub them, because rubbing damages the frozen tissue, and avoid direct heat like stoves or hot water bottles too. Rewarm gently with skin-to-skin contact, such as against your belly or armpits, or in a sleeping bag, and make sure her boots and socks are dry. If the skin stays white, waxy, hard or numb after rewarming, it may be frostbite and she should get down and see a doctor. Don't rewarm if there's a chance of refreezing, since that causes more damage.
Cheapest bungee place near me is like half the price of the others. Worth it?

A big price gap is worth checking out before you book. Look for how long they've been operating, whether they follow a recognized safety standard or industry body, and recent reviews that mention staff professionalism and equipment checks. Ask how often cords are replaced and how they verify your weight. If they can't answer clearly, paying more for a proven operator is the right call.
My 12 year old wants to swim across the bay with her dad (about 1.5km). She does swim club twice a week. Thoughts?

It's doable for a club swimmer that age, but build up to it rather than going straight for the full crossing. Have her do several shorter open-water swims first so she gets used to cold, waves and sighting.
