Student limits are often around 14 to 18 mph, and gusts matter even more than steady wind because they make canopies unpredictable near the ground. Holds are annoying, but they're exactly what a good dropzone should do.
What's the difference between a cruiser and a regular popsicle deck?

A popsicle deck is the standard symmetrical street board with kicked nose and tail, built for ollies, flip tricks and park skating. A cruiser is usually shorter or wider with a flatter shape and soft, bigger wheels, so it rolls smoothly over cracks and rough pavement but is pretty much useless for technical tricks. If you mostly want to get around town, go cruiser; if you want to learn tricks, get a popsicle.
honestly how risky is it to fly in light rain

Avoid it. A wet wing can become heavier and more prone to parachutal stall, where it loses forward speed and drops, and that's hard to recover from. Wet lines and fabric also age faster. If rain starts while you're up, land promptly, and avoid using big brake inputs on the approach.
What's the deal with silt? Everyone keeps warning me about it.

Many cave floors are covered in fine sediment that rises with a single careless fin kick and can drop visibility from fifty meters to zero in seconds, then hang there for hours. That's why cave divers obsess over buoyancy, trim and frog or modified flutter kicks that push water backward instead of down. It's also why you always need a continuous guideline, since a silt-out turns an easy swim out into a blind, touch-only exit.
I want to beat a free solo speed record on a classic route. What's the fastest way to train?

I'd steer you away from chasing free solo speed records. Adding a stopwatch to ropeless climbing strips out exactly the margin that keeps people alive. If speed is what excites you, competitive speed climbing on the standardized wall is an Olympic sport with real training paths, and roped speed records on big routes like the Nose have a strong culture behind them. Join a gym with a speed wall or find a partner to start running laps on rope.
Can I freedive after drinking last night?

Skip it if you're still hungover or haven't fully recovered. Alcohol dehydrates you, impairs your judgment and affects your breath-hold, which raises your blackout risk. Wait until you're well rested and hydrated. The ocean will still be there tomorrow.
what is the minimum gear for a luge race

Most sanctioned races require a certified full-face helmet, full leathers or an approved abrasion suit, gloves, and sturdy boots with braking soles, and many have rules about sled specs too. Check the specific event's rulebook, since requirements vary by organization and course. Some also need back protection. If you're unsure, contact the organizers early so you're not turned away at tech inspection.
rolled my ankle on a precision jump yesterday, its swollen and kinda purple. can i train tomorrow if i tape it?

No, that much swelling and bruising after a day means you've likely sprained it properly, and taping it to train tomorrow is how a one-week injury becomes a two-month one. Rest it, keep it elevated, use ice and compression, and get it checked by a doctor or physio, especially if you can't put weight on it or the pain is near the bone, because that can mean a fracture. Once it's cleared, rebuild with balance and strength work before going back to precision jumps. You can still train upper body and core in the meantime.
I broke my wrist last season doing a tail press. Nervous to do tricks again. Advice?

That nervousness is normal, and easing back in is the right approach. Make sure your wrist is fully cleared by your doctor or physio, wear wrist guards, and start with easy flatland tricks on a soft snow day to rebuild confidence. A refresher lesson can help a lot too, because a coach can tweak whatever technique caused the fall so you're not just hoping it doesn't happen again.
My boyfriend wants to solo a sea cliff route in Cornwall next month. He's experienced but I'm anxious. How can I support him without freaking out?

Tell him calmly how you feel, since honest communication is part of supporting him. Ask what his plan is: has he rehearsed it on a rope recently, how will tides and sea spray affect the rock, and what's his bail plan if he's not feeling it on the day. Ask him to agree to a firm rule that he'll walk away if conditions or his headspace aren't right. You can also ask him to consider toprope soloing it instead, which keeps most of the experience.
can i skip the forecast if i'm just doing a short tour near the road

No, you should still check the forecast. Plenty of avalanches happen near roads, and short tours can still cross or run under avalanche paths. Reading it takes two minutes and tells you which aspects and elevations are dangerous today. Even close to the car, a slide can bury you as fast as anywhere else.
my son just told me he's doing his first base jump next month. should i be terrified

It's normal to be worried, and the most useful thing you can do is ask him specific questions: how many skydives he has, who's running his First Jump Course, and what object he'll jump first. If he's doing a proper FJC with a reputable instructor and has a few hundred skydives with strong canopy skills, he's taking the responsible route into a genuinely risky sport. If his answers are vague, it's fair to encourage him to slow down and get proper training first.
Can I do this pregnant? 4 months, been jumping for years.

It's best to stop for the pregnancy. Hard water impacts and the risk of falls or abdominal trauma aren't worth it at any stage, however experienced you are. Talk to your doctor or midwife about which water activities are fine for you right now, as swimming is usually a great alternative.
Is it worth getting a neck brace for downhill or is that overkill for a hobby rider?

For a hobby rider hitting bike parks a few times a season, it's a reasonable choice rather than overkill, though plenty of riders skip it. The evidence on how much neck braces prevent serious injury is mixed, so the essentials come first: a certified full-face helmet that fits well, good knee pads, and a back protector. If you ride steep, fast tracks or start doing big jumps and drops, a brace becomes more worthwhile. If you get one, make sure it's compatible with your helmet and doesn't restrict your head movement.
Grabs. Indy vs Melon. What's the difference?

An Indy is your back hand grabbing the toe edge between your bindings, and a Melon is your front hand grabbing the heel edge between your bindings. Indy is usually easier first because you're reaching down in front of you. For either one, bring the board up to your hand by tucking your knees, rather than reaching down and folding over, which keeps you balanced for the landing.
River gauge says it's flooding but it's a run I know really well. Worth it?

Skip it. A river at flood stage is basically a different river: features you know get washed out, new hydraulics form, eddies vanish, and floating trees and debris show up everywhere. Rescue also gets much harder because swims are longer and banks are often underwater. Wait for it to drop into a range you've actually run, or check with local paddlers who know the high-water lines.
is a hardtail ok for bike park laps?

It can be on easier green and blue trails if you ride within its limits. A full-suspension downhill or enduro bike is much more forgiving on rough terrain, drops and big jumps. Renting a downhill bike for park days is common and lets you progress with less punishment. Check that the hardtail's brakes and tires are up to the job.
what is swim failure and how do i avoid it?

Swim failure happens in cold water when your arm and leg muscles cool down and stop working properly, often within 10 to 30 minutes, even if you still feel okay in yourself. You can avoid it by building cold tolerance gradually, wearing a wetsuit and cap in cold water, staying close to shore, and getting out while you still feel strong. If your stroke starts to feel clumsy or your hands won't close, get out right away.
My daughter (9) is obsessed with doing tricks after watching the Olympics. Where should she start?

A kids' freestyle lesson or park program is the best start, since coaches teach butters, small jumps and boxes in a fun, controlled way. At home she can work on balance with a skateboard or balance board, and a backyard trampoline with a good net helps with air awareness. Make sure she has a well-fitting helmet, and let her lead the pace so it stays fun rather than scary.
what's a good first BASE object

The usual first objects are high, clear bridges like the Perrine Bridge in Idaho, where you get lots of altitude, no wall to hit, and a big landing area. That's why most first jump courses run there. Avoid low objects, cliffs with close walls and anything with poor landing options until you have real experience. Big and forgiving beats impressive every time.
can i use my regular hiking crampons for ice climbing

Not really, at least not for vertical ice. Hiking crampons and microspikes are made for walking on flat or angled snow and ice, and they lack the stiff, aggressive front points you need to stand on steep ice without your feet popping. For ice climbing you want technical crampons, usually with vertical front points, paired with stiff mountaineering boots they're compatible with. Rent a proper boot and crampon setup for your first few days and you'll immediately feel the difference.
me and my mates want to rig our own bungee off a quarry using climbing rope. how hard can it be

Please don't, this is how people get killed. Climbing rope is designed to catch short falls, not stretch safely over a long drop, and getting the cord length and anchors right requires engineering calculations and tested gear you won't have at a quarry. Book a group jump with a licensed operator instead and you'll get the same story to tell with a much better chance of being around to tell it.
Do I need to warm up before cold water swimming or does it not matter?

Do a light warm-up on land, such as arm circles, gentle swinging and a bit of brisk walking, to get your blood flowing without breaking a sweat. Avoid a hard workout beforehand, because you'll lose heat faster once you're in the water. Getting in slowly and controlling your breathing matters far more than the warm-up itself.
I'm 45 and just started snowboarding last season. Is it too late to learn park tricks or will I break something?

It's definitely not too late. You just want to progress smarter than the teenagers. Stick to ground tricks, butters, small rollers, and wide low boxes, and wear a helmet, wrist guards, and impact shorts since falls hit harder at our age. A park lesson for adults is well worth it because a coach will keep you on features that match your skill. Plenty of people learn to ride the park in their 40s and 50s, it's just smart to skip the big jumps.
detailed q: I want to try longboard downhill on mountain roads near me, about 40mph. I have a helmet. what else

At those speeds a regular skate helmet isn't enough. Get a certified full-face helmet, slide gloves with pucks, leather or abrasion-resistant clothing, and knee pads. You'll also need solid sliding and braking skills before touching 40mph, so build up on small closed hills first. Go with an experienced group that uses spotters for blind corners. Many downhill communities run freeride sessions on closed roads, which is the safest way to learn.
just practicing static breath holds in my bathtub alone, thats fine right? its only like 40cm deep

No. People have drowned doing exactly this, because you can black out during a breath hold with no warning, and 40cm of water is plenty deep enough when you're unconscious. Do your static training dry, lying on your bed or couch, where a blackout just means you start breathing again. Save wet statics for a pool with a trained buddy watching you the whole time.
What oxygen saturation is normal at 5000 meters? My pulse ox says 78%.

At 5,000 m, readings of 75 to 85% are common in well-acclimatized people, so 78% alone isn't alarming. The number matters less than how you feel and which way it's trending, so a steady 78% with no symptoms is fine, while a sudden drop or a low reading plus breathlessness at rest is a red flag. Also check that your fingers are warm, because cold hands give falsely low readings.
I got frostbite on two fingertips on a climb last week. They're blistered and dark. Do I need a doctor?

Yes, see a doctor soon, ideally one with frostbite experience or a burn clinic. Dark, blistered fingertips suggest at least second- or third-degree injury, and early treatment, including drugs that restore blood flow, can affect how much tissue you keep. Don't pop the blisters, don't rub or re-warm the fingers with direct heat, and keep them protected until you're seen.
My buddy says we don't need to check the landing because people jump there every day. True?

Check it anyway, it takes five minutes. Storms, tides and currents move rocks and debris, and people dump stuff off popular ledges, so yesterday's safe spot isn't guaranteed today. Have someone swim the landing zone with a mask before the first jump.
My friend is getting a sat phone for touring. Is that overkill?

Not overkill at all, especially in remote areas with no cell coverage. A satellite communicator or phone lets you call for help, check updates and let people know you're safe. Just remember it doesn't replace beacon, shovel, probe or careful terrain choices, since help can take hours to arrive.
Is there any good app for checking avalanche forecasts?

Your regional avalanche center's website is the most reliable source, and many offer mobile versions or alerts. Apps like CalTopo or onX Backcountry can show slope angles and terrain, which helps with planning. Always check the latest forecast before heading out and pay attention to conditions on the ground.
friend says i should just send it off the big kicker and figure it out mid air. good idea?

No, ignore that one. Big kickers need the right approach speed, and if you go too slow you'll knuckle the lip and too fast you'll overshoot the landing onto flat ground, which is where the serious injuries happen. Work up through the small and medium jumps until your straight airs are consistent, and watch a few experienced riders hit the big one to see how much speed they carry before you try it.
Elbow pain from climbing, inside of elbow, getting worse. Should I just rest totally?

Pain on the inside of the elbow in climbers is usually medial epicondylopathy, or golfer's elbow, and total rest helps less than you'd think. Cut back on the hard pulling and steep climbing that flare it, and start eccentric wrist flexor work, like slow lowering with a light dumbbell or a flexbar. Antagonist training such as pushups and reverse wrist curls helps too. If it keeps getting worse after a few weeks of this, see a physio for a proper program.
I'm 47, been climbing 25 years, solid 5.11 trad. I've been thinking about soloing some easy multipitch I know cold. Thoughts?

With your experience you understand the trade-off better than most, so I'll be straight: deep knowledge of a route lowers some risks, but it doesn't touch rockfall, a snapped flake, a sudden cramp or a lapse in focus. Many deaths among highly experienced soloists happened on terrain far below their limit. If what you're after is moving freely and efficiently, think about simul-climbing with a trusted partner or carrying a light rack and rope to self-belay the cruxes. Either keeps the flow and adds a real margin.
can I go thermalling on my first solo flight? seems boring to just glide down

Not yet. Thermals bring turbulence, need active wing control, and involve other pilots circling near you, which is too much to handle on top of first-solo nerves. Those early glides are where you build the launch, landing and control skills that make thermalling safe later. Your instructor will tell you when you're ready, usually after a good number of solid flights.
My ears hurt on descent last dive and I just pushed through it. Was that bad?

Yes, pushing through ear pain risks a ruptured eardrum or barotrauma to your middle ear, so don't do that again. Equalize early and often, starting at the surface and every meter or so on the way down. If it still hurts, ascend a little until it eases, then try again. If you have ongoing pain, muffled hearing, ringing or dizziness now, see a doctor before your next dive.
brakes squealing and feel weak halfway down long runs, can i just keep riding

Fading brakes on long descents are a serious warning sign, so don't keep riding them as they are. You're probably overheating the pads and rotors, possibly with glazed pads or air in the system. Have a shop bleed the brakes and fit fresh metallic pads, and consider bigger 200 or 220mm rotors. Until that's done, stick to shorter runs and brake in firm bursts rather than dragging.
quickest way to get good at grabs?

Get comfortable with straight airs on small jumps first, then focus on bringing your knees up to the board instead of reaching down. Start with an indy or melon on a small jump where you have plenty of time, and hold it a beat longer each run. Repetition on small features beats big jumps every time for building clean grabs.
is it dumb to do a tandem with a cold? kinda stuffy

Not dumb, but probably uncomfortable. Congestion can make it hard to equalize your ears during the descent, which can mean real pain or even a damaged eardrum. If you're quite blocked, reschedule, since most dropzones are flexible about it. A mild cold with clear ears is usually fine.
I booked Everest for next spring. My highest is 5400m on a trek. Is that enough experience?

Honestly, that's a thin base for Everest, and reputable operators usually want to see at least one 7000 m or 8000 m peak plus solid crampon, fixed line and cold-weather experience. Do Ama Dablam, Aconcagua or Manaslu first so you learn how your body handles extreme altitude and long summit days. If your operator accepted you without that history, take a hard look at whether they're a safe company to climb with.
I'm 15 and want to try downhill skateboarding. My parents are nervous. What should I tell them?

Tell them you plan to learn the right way: a certified full-face or certified half-shell helmet, slide gloves, knee and elbow pads, and practice on gentle, empty hills before anything steep. Show them you'll learn to slide and footbrake to control speed before you chase it, and offer to take a lesson or join a local downhill clinic where experienced riders coach beginners. Parents usually relax a lot once they see a real plan and proper gear instead of just a kid bombing a hill.
best first wingsuit?

Get a small beginner suit, something like the Squirrel SPRITE or Phoenix-Fly Phantom, and ideally rent one through your First Flight Course before you buy. Small suits are forgiving, open with less drama, and let you build good habits. Resist the urge to buy a big suit early, because that's exactly the jump people regret.
Teaching my girlfriend to do a 50-50 on a box. Any tips? She's nervous.

Pick the lowest, widest box with an easy approach, and have her ride straight up to it with her board flat, looking at the end of the box the whole time. Tell her to ride off naturally rather than trying to jump off, and to keep her knees soft. Do it slowly the first few times so it's fun, not scary. If she gets frustrated, a single park lesson can make a big difference because a neutral coach often clicks better than a partner.
climbing coach says just climb through finger pain, everyone has it. true?

No, because sharp or localized finger pain, especially at the base of a finger or with a pop, can be a pulley injury, and climbing through that can lead to a full rupture. General achiness after a hard session is normal, but pain that's pinpoint, lingers or hurts when you crimp needs rest and assessment by a hand specialist or a physio who knows climbers. Drop the crimps and hangboarding until you know what it is.
I want to get into cliff diving properly, like the Red Bull guys. where do I start?

Start at a diving club with a platform diving program, since the pros nearly all come from springboard and platform diving backgrounds. Coaches will teach you entries, rotations and how to build up height safely, plus the dryland and trampoline training that goes with it. Natural cliff jumping is great fun, but the athletes you see on TV spent years learning their skills in pools.
do i need impact shorts

They're worth it if you're learning park tricks or riding lots of hard-packed snow. They cushion your tailbone and hips when you slam, and since you'll fall a lot while learning, they keep you riding longer and less sore. They're cheap compared to a bruised tailbone that sidelines you for weeks.
do loose trucks or tight trucks make it easier for a beginner

Medium is the sweet spot: tight enough that the board doesn't wobble at speed, loose enough that you can turn by leaning. Fully tight trucks make beginners fight the board to turn, while very loose ones cause speed wobbles that throw people off. Start with the kingpin nut snug, then loosen it a quarter turn at a time until carving feels natural. Leave at least a couple of threads showing above the nut so it stays secure.
Can my 15 year old son do a tandem with me? He's mature for his age.

That depends entirely on the country and dropzone, since most US dropzones require 18 and won't make exceptions for maturity. Some places in Europe and elsewhere accept younger jumpers with parental consent, so check directly. If he's too young, indoor skydiving is a great alternative you can do together now.
can i use earplugs open water? worried about swimmer's ear

Yes, earplugs are common in open water and help a lot with swimmer's ear and with the dizziness some people get from cold water entering the ear. Mouldable silicone types seal well. Dry your ears afterward by tilting your head, and if you swim cold water often, ask about surfer's ear, a bony growth that plugs help prevent. See a doctor if you get pain or discharge.
Is mixed climbing just ice climbing with rock? Can I jump right into it?

Pretty much: you're using tools and crampons on rock, ice and frozen turf, often torquing tools in cracks. It's harder to protect and pulls more on technique, so it's best to get comfortable on ice first. Many people try it at a dry-tooling crag or on top rope with a guide before leading any mixed routes. Building up that way keeps you from learning on poor protection.
Going to Croatia next month, any good cliff jumping advice?

Croatia has great rocky coastline for jumping, but tides are small and there are often boats, so watch for traffic and pick spots away from where boats pass. Check the depth yourself even at popular locations, wear water shoes for the sharp rocks and urchins, and plan your climb-out route first. If you want to try bigger heights, look for guided coasteering or cliff jumping tours, which know the safe spots.
Is there a difference between bungee and that giant swing thing?

Yes, a canyon or giant swing drops you briefly then swings you in a big arc instead of bouncing you up and down. Many people find it less jarring on the head, neck and back because you're upright and there's no sudden rebound. If you have health concerns about bungee's jolt, a swing can be a gentler option, though you should still check the operator's medical rules.
I'm terrified of rock gardens. I freeze and grab the brakes. help

Grabbing the brakes in a rock garden makes it worse, because the front wheel stops on rocks instead of rolling over them. Scrub speed before you enter, then let off a little and keep momentum while looking for the smoothest line ahead, not the rock you're scared of. Stay in an attack position with loose arms and let the bike move. Practice on short, easy rock sections until relaxing becomes your reflex instead of freezing.
Is it normal to feel sick after my first few wingsuit jumps?

Some people get mild nausea or a headache early on, usually from adrenaline, tension or line twists after deployment spinning you around. Hydrating, eating something light beforehand and relaxing your body in flight often helps. If you're dizzy, disoriented or feeling worse with each jump, stop for the day and talk to your instructor or a doctor before going up again.
I'm terrified of heights. Will bungee cure it?

It won't cure a fear of heights, but plenty of scared people do it and come away feeling braver. The worst part is the few seconds on the edge, and good staff are practiced at talking nervous jumpers through it. Go to a reputable site, tell the crew you're anxious, and don't let anyone rush you. If you have a real phobia that affects daily life, a therapist using gradual exposure will do far more than one jump.
is it bad to jump into the ocean when theres big waves

Yes, it's best to avoid it. Waves change the water depth by meters in seconds, so a landing zone that's deep one moment can expose rocks the next. They also make getting back out much harder. Choose a calm day, time your jump for the high part of the swell if there's any movement, and plan your exit route before you jump.
how fast can i go from sea level to 5000m if i feel great

Feeling great isn't a reliable signal, because AMS often shows up 6 to 12 hours after you arrive at a new altitude. The safe rule is to gain no more than 300 to 500 m of sleeping altitude per day above 3,000 m, with a rest day every three or four days. That puts you at roughly a week to sleep at 5,000 m, and anything faster is gambling.
Can I practice breath holds in my bathtub alone? Just want to get better fast.

Please don't. Practicing breath holds alone in any water is how people die from shallow water blackout. You pass out with no warning and drown in silence. Do your dry static tables lying on the floor or bed instead, and only do in-water holds with a trained buddy watching you the whole time. Dry training builds most of the CO2 tolerance you're after anyway.
can i just watch youtube videos and figure out wingsuiting myself? courses are expensive

Videos are great for visualizing body position and flight patterns, but they can't replace a first flight course. A coach checks your gear setup, briefs you on exit and deployment, and debriefs your actual flight, which is where the real learning happens. Deployment mistakes in a wingsuit can lead to malfunctions that videos won't prepare you for. The course is a one-time cost and well worth it.
Swim buoy, worth it or just a gimmick?

They're worth it, mainly because a bright tow float makes you far more visible to boats, paddleboarders and anyone watching from shore. It also gives you something to hold onto if you get cramp or need a rest. Most have a dry pouch for keys or a phone, and you'll barely notice the drag once you're swimming.
What's the safest way to spearfish while freediving?

Spearfishing has a high blackout rate because people focus on the fish and stay down too long. Always dive with a buddy using one-up, one-down, and set yourself a firm bottom-time rule you never break for a fish. Avoid hyperventilating, rest long enough between dives, and keep track of your session time. Know your local regulations and avoid areas with heavy boat traffic, or use a float flag.
Ok so how do you fall properly on a snowboard, my wrists keep getting hurt

Try to fall onto your forearms and roll instead of putting your hands straight out. If you're falling backward, sit down onto your butt and roll onto your back with your chin tucked; if falling forward, go down onto your knees and forearms. Wrist guards make a big difference while you practice. If your wrists are still painful after a few days, get them checked, since small fractures are common and easy to miss.
How do I know if a wall is safe to climb or jump on?

Test it before you trust it. Push and pull on the surface, look for cracks, loose bricks or capstones, and check for moisture, moss or sand that could make it slippery. Look at what's behind and below it, since a solid wall can still drop into a hidden gap. If you have any doubt about whether it will hold your weight, skip it.
How many skydives do I actually need before I can start wingsuit training?

The common standard is at least 200 skydives within the last 18 months. Many drop zones also want you to have a B license or equivalent. Treat 200 as the floor, not the finish line. You want canopy skills and freefall awareness to be automatic before you add a suit that changes everything about your exits and deployments.
Can I drink the night before my jump? Like a few beers

A couple of beers the night before is usually fine as long as you're fully sober and not hungover, but many dropzones set an 8 to 12 hour no-alcohol rule. A hangover hurts your reactions and makes nausea under canopy much worse. If you're doing a tandem or a student jump, keep it light and get proper sleep.
how much gas should i turn around at in a cave

The standard is the rule of thirds: use one third of your gas going in, one third coming out, and keep one third in reserve for problems or to share with a buddy. In siphons, or when diving with someone who has larger cylinders or a higher breathing rate, cave divers turn even earlier, often at a quarter. Turn the dive the moment the first diver reaches their turn pressure, whatever is ahead.
I keep getting speed wobbles around 30 mph and I'm kinda freaking out about it

Wobbles are super common and very fixable, so don't panic. Tighten your bushings or go harder, lower your truck angle on the front if your setup allows it, and stay relaxed with your weight centered or slightly forward over the front truck, because stiffening up and leaning back makes them worse. Most of all, stay below the speed where you wobble until you've fixed the setup and built your tuck. Speed comes with time.
My 16 year old daughter is a strong surfer and wants to start charging bigger waves. How do I support that safely?

Connect her with an experienced big-wave mentor or coach who can guide her progression rather than letting her figure it out alone with friends. Get her into a breath-hold and ocean safety course, and make sure she always surfs bigger days with a solid crew and ideally water safety. Gradual progression across seasons, not a big leap, is what keeps young chargers healthy and in the sport long-term.
Is it worth buying a dive computer for freediving?

A freediving watch or computer is worth having once you're diving regularly. It tracks depth, dive time and surface intervals, which helps you progress safely and stops you creeping deeper without noticing. Set alarms for your max depth and for minimum surface time. Treat it as a training tool, not a replacement for your buddy.
What's the difference between heat exhaustion and heat stroke, quickly?

Heat exhaustion causes heavy sweating, weakness, nausea, a headache and dizziness, but you can still think clearly. Stopping, cooling and getting fluids usually helps. Heat stroke involves a high core temperature and changes in brain function, like confusion, slurred speech, strange behavior or collapse, and it's a medical emergency that needs immediate cooling, ideally by immersing the person in ice water, plus emergency medical care. The key way to tell them apart is a change in mental state.
I want to solo an easy WI2 gully this weekend. I've climbed WI4 on lead. Talk me out of it or don't.

I'd pass on it, even with your experience. Being able to lead WI4 helps, but free soloing ice exposes you to factors your skill can't control, like a placement shearing through brittle ice, a crampon balling up, or a block falling from above. On easy terrain those are usually minor problems when roped, but deadly when unprotected. If you want speed and simplicity, climb it roped together with a light rack or a quick simul setup with a trusted partner, which gets you most of that freedom with a real margin for error.
is it ok to jump alone if I know the spot really well?

I'd avoid it. Even experienced jumpers get winded, hit the water wrong or get disoriented, and if you're knocked out or injured in the water with nobody around, a minor mistake can become fatal. Bring at least one friend who stays at the surface and watches each jump, and ideally someone who can swim out to help.
Wingsuit pilot. Lower back flared up, can barely sit for long. Gonna just do a quick flight to stay current.

With a back that bad, I'd sit this one out. Wingsuit flying needs strong core control and a clean deployment, and pain that limits movement can turn a small issue into a dangerous one on opening shock or landing. Get it assessed so you know whether it's muscular or something like a disc problem. Maintain currency with tunnel time or ground drills while you recover.
Just watched a BASE video, want to try it. Where do I start?

Start with skydiving, not BASE. Do a tandem or an accelerated freefall course, get licensed, and build a few hundred skydives with plenty of canopy training. Once you're experienced, book a reputable first jump course. The videos leave out the years of preparation behind those jumps.
we got a groupon for ice climbing at a local gym ice wall is that legit

Probably yes. Lots of climbing gyms and ice parks run indoor or artificial ice walls for intro sessions, and they're a great, controlled way to learn swing and kick technique. Check that staff run the belays or give you a proper belay check, and that rental boots, crampons, and helmets are included. The skills transfer well to outdoor toproping, though real ice adds conditions and hazards you'll want a guide to show you.
how do you deal with fear on a jump you know you can do

Break it down until it's manageable: practice the exact distance on flat ground, then at low height, and then with the real obstacle, so your body has evidence it can do it. Commit fully once you decide to go, because hesitating mid-jump is when people slip. If the fear is persistent, it's sometimes telling you something real, like a slippery take-off or tired legs, so it's okay to come back another day. Walking away from a jump is a skill, not a failure.
wall run up a 9 foot wall how

Run at the wall with good speed, plant your foot about waist-high with the ball of your foot, and drive upward instead of into the wall, reaching for the top edge with both hands. Start on lower walls and build up height gradually. Make sure the top edge is solid and not crumbling or sharp, and know how you'll get down before you go up.
My climbing friends are pressuring me to solo an easy route with them. I don't really want to.

Trust that instinct and say no. Soloing is only remotely defensible when someone genuinely wants to and is fully ready, and peer pressure is a classic factor in climbing accidents. Offer to climb it roped alongside them or belay, and anyone worth climbing with will respect that. If they don't, that tells you a lot about their judgment as partners.
best way to fall when lead climbing?

Keep your feet in front of you on the wall, hold your knees bent like springs, keep your hands near your chest and let go of the rope, and look down so you can see where you're landing. Keep the rope in front of your legs, never behind them, or it can flip you upside down. Practice falls in a gym with an experienced belayer who gives soft catches, starting small and close to a bolt.
i paddled into a big set and got destroyed, now scared to go back out. should I quit?

No need to quit. Getting rattled after a heavy beating is extremely common, even among pros. Ease back in with a few sessions in surf you're comfortable with to rebuild confidence, then step back up gradually. A breath-hold or water safety course can really help, because knowing your body can handle more than you thought takes the edge off the fear.
Lost my ice clipper mid-pitch last time and fumbled with a screw. Any tips?

Rack your screws on dedicated ice clippers on your harness, and practice clipping and unclipping them by feel on the ground, with gloves on. Before each pitch, double-check the clipper is clicked on securely. Placing a screw goes much smoother if you get a solid stance first, plant one tool, and start the screw at chest height. A spare screw or two gives you margin if you drop one.
is it fine to ride in sneakers if im just doing a few laps

No, sneakers are one of the worst things you can wear on a dirt bike, because ankle and foot injuries happen constantly even at low speed when a foot gets caught or the bike lands on it. Proper motocross boots have stiff soles, shin plates and ankle support that prevent breaks a sneaker can't. A few laps is exactly when people get hurt because they aren't taking it seriously. Even a used pair of MX boots is a huge upgrade.
is it illegal to BASE jump off buildings? like will i get arrested

In most places, jumping off a building without permission is trespassing at minimum, and you can face arrest, fines or worse depending on the jurisdiction. Urban jumps also carry extra hazards like wires, traffic and tiny landing areas, which is why they're not where newer jumpers belong. If you want legal jumping, look at places like the Perrine Bridge in Idaho, Bridge Day in West Virginia, or established sites in Norway and Switzerland. Learn there, keep a clean record, and stay alive.
My partner says we can skip helmets on easy ice since it's basically a walk-up. True?

No, keep the helmets on. On ice, the biggest helmet threat is usually falling ice, not falling yourself, and every swing from a climber above you or any party on the route can send chunks down. Even easy-angled ice gets hit by debris from above, and a dinner plate of ice to the head can do serious damage. Helmets are cheap insurance and should stay on from the base of the route until you're clear of it.
fastest way to learn a backflip on concrete? dont have access to a gym

There isn't a safe fast way to learn a backflip on concrete, and that's how people land on their necks. Learn it first on a trampoline, a sand pit, deep grass with a spotter, or at a gymnastics or parkour open session, which many places offer cheaply for drop-ins. Build the jump, tuck and set separately, then put them together on a soft surface with someone who knows how to spot. Only take it to hard ground once you're landing it consistently and could bail safely if you under-rotated.
Is night swimming in the ocean a terrible idea? Friends want to do it at a party.

At a party it usually is, because alcohol, darkness and the sea are a bad mix. You can't see currents, you can't see each other, and nobody on the beach can tell if someone's struggling. If you want to swim at night, do it sober, in a sheltered spot you already know, with a light or glow stick on each swimmer and someone staying dry on shore. Otherwise wading in the shallows is the fun version without the risk.
how much sag for downhill fork and shock

Most downhill setups run about 30 to 35 percent sag on the rear shock and 20 to 25 percent on the fork. Measure it with your full gear on and standing in the attack position. Treat those numbers as a starting point, then adjust based on how the bike bottoms out and holds up on your local trails. A good shop or suspension tuner can dial it in quickly if you're unsure.
Going to Croatia next month, heard there are good cliff jumping spots near Dubrovnik. Anything I should know before I just go for it?

The rocks around Dubrovnik, like the Buža bars area, are popular, but don't take crowd behaviour as proof a spot is safe. Watch locals jump the exact same line several times, swim the landing zone yourself to check depth and rocks, and figure out where you'll climb out before you leap, because the sea can push you into the rocks. Start low, skip it if the swell is up, and save the drinks until after you're done jumping.
i'm 52 and want to try cliff jumping on vacation in croatia. too old?

Not too old at all, but go in honestly. Back, neck, knee or heart issues matter more at this point, so check with your doctor if any apply. Start low, around 3 to 5 meters, at a popular spot where locals jump regularly and the depth is known. A guided coasteering trip is a great way to do it with someone who knows the water.
Rate my plan: solo, 40 degree couloir, high danger rating, I've got an airbag.

That plan stacks nearly every major risk factor: no partner, steep committing terrain that's likely a terrain trap, and a high danger rating. Under those conditions an airbag won't save you from trauma or a deep burial in a couloir. Pick a different day for the couloir, and when you go, bring a partner and wait for a low or moderate rating. Today, ski low-angle terrain or the resort.
Teach me a backflip. I've watched like 20 YouTube videos and I think I'm ready to try it on grass.

Videos teach you the shape of the move, but they can't spot you, and a short-rotated backflip on grass is one of the classic ways people land on their neck. Learn it at a gym or trampoline park with a coach. The usual progression is back rolls, backward jumps onto a raised mat stack, then spotted flips into a foam pit. Most people with decent jumping power get a clean flip within a few coached sessions, which is faster and far safer than trial and error in a park.
best way to stop on a skateboard

Foot braking is the one to learn first: keep your front foot planted and pointing forward, then gently drag the sole of your back shoe flat along the ground until you slow down. Put more pressure on gradually instead of stomping, and keep your weight centered over the front foot. Tail dragging works but chews through your tail fast, and powerslides are great to have once your basics are solid. Practice stopping on gentle ground until you can do it without thinking, before you take on anything with a slope.
found an old rope in my dad's garage from like the 90s, still looks fine. good to climb on?

Retire it, because nylon degrades with age even when it's sitting in a garage, and you have no idea how many falls it's taken or whether it was exposed to chemicals like battery acid or gasoline. Ropes can look fine outside while the core is damaged, and manufacturers generally recommend retiring them after about ten years even if unused. A new dynamic rope is a worthwhile investment since it's the thing holding your life.
Is a skate helmet fine for downhill? Full face ones are expensive.

No, a skate helmet isn't built for the speeds or the face-first impacts you get in downhill. Most parks require a full-face helmet on their gravity trails anyway. Look for a full face certified to ASTM F1952 or a similar downhill standard, or rent one from the park. Last season's models are often heavily discounted and protect you just as well.
How do I learn to drive a jetski for tow surfing?

Start with a PWC safety course and get comfortable handling the ski in calm and choppy water before you go anywhere near surf. Learn rescue sled pickups in small waves with an experienced driver coaching you. Then work up through medium surf over months, not weeks. Many big-wave safety programs offer specific water patrol and rescue training, and that's the best way to learn properly.
how do i ollie on a snowboard? total beginner at tricks

Start on flat ground or a mellow green run, shift your weight onto your back foot to load the tail, then spring up and pull your front knee toward your chest so the nose lifts first and the tail follows. Keep your shoulders level and your eyes forward, and land with your knees bent so they absorb the impact. Practice it at slow speed until it feels automatic before you try popping over anything.
Quick q: drop-through or top-mount for downhill?

Top-mount is generally preferred for serious downhill because it gives sharper control, better foot lock-in and more feedback at speed. Drop-throughs sit lower and are great for stability and easy pushing while you're learning or freeriding at moderate speeds. Many riders start on a drop-through and move to top-mount as they get faster.
I heard whumpfing on the skin track today, kinda cool sound. Does it mean anything?

Yes, it means a lot, because a whumpf is a weak layer collapsing under you and is one of the clearest danger signs you can get. The snowpack is telling you that it's unstable and could avalanche on any slope that's steep enough. When you hear one, get off and away from anything over about 30 degrees and stay on low-angle terrain for the rest of the day.
I want to go straight to a big performance suit, the beginner ones look boring.

Big suits are much harder to exit, fly and deploy, and pilots who jump into them too early tend to have unstable flights and bad deployments. Beginner suits teach the core skills that make bigger suits manageable later, and most people progress through a couple of sizes over their first 100 or so wingsuit jumps. Boring flights now mean fun, controlled flights in a big suit later.
What board should I get for my first 12-15 foot days?

You'll want a step-up or semi-gun, usually somewhere around 7'6" to 9' depending on your weight and the wave, with more length and foam than your daily board for earlier entry. The extra paddle power gets you in before the wave stands up and pitches, which is when most first-timers get caught. Talk to a local shaper who knows your spot, since they'll dial in the length and rails for that specific break better than any online chart.
Can you just tell me how to downclimb safely when soloing? Don't need the lecture.

Downclimbing is a core skill whatever your plans, and the basics are to face in on anything steep and keep three points of contact. Look down to find footholds before committing your weight, and move slower than feels necessary. Practice it a lot on top-rope and on easy terrain with a rope, including reversing whole pitches, because it's harder than going up. If a solo ever depends on downclimbing as your exit, rehearse that exact descent roped beforehand.
Does a lanyard really matter if I'm diving on a line?

Yes, the lanyard is what keeps you attached to the line. If you black out deep or get disoriented, it lets your buddy or safety system pull you back up instead of watching you sink out of reach. It's cheap insurance and standard for line diving. Use a quick-release one so you can detach easily if it ever snags.
Reservoir near me has no swimming signs but loads of people swim there anyway. Worth it?

Reservoirs are often banned for real reasons. The water stays dangerously cold even in summer, there can be hidden machinery and intakes with strong suction, and the edges are steep and hard to climb out of. People drown in them every year, often on hot days. Look for a lake or lido with lifeguards or an organised open-water session nearby instead. You'll get the same feeling without the hidden hazards.
My 16 year old son wants to go ski touring with his friends this weekend, none of them have avalanche training. Should I be worried?

Yes, it's reasonable to be concerned, because untrained groups are exactly who tends to wander into avalanche terrain without realizing it. A good compromise is to insist they either stick to low-angle terrain well away from steep slopes and runouts, or go with a guide or experienced adult this time. Longer term, offering to pay for a youth avalanche course or a Level 1 is a great way to support the hobby safely.
is a regular trail helmet fine for downhill or do I really need a full face

For lift-served downhill you really want a full face. The speeds and the way people crash on steep terrain mean faceplant and chin impacts are common, and a half-shell does nothing for your jaw or teeth. A certified downhill full face (look for ASTM F1952) is the standard, and many parks require one anyway. Save the trail lid for pedaling.
Is it ok to kayak alone if I'm careful? Nobody else is free on weekdays.

Solo whitewater is strongly discouraged, because many routine problems like a pin, a missed roll or an entrapment become fatal with no one there to help. If you want weekday time, stick to flatwater or very easy moving water you know well, and leave a float plan with someone. Local paddling clubs and online meetup groups are also a good way to find weekday partners.
How fast should I go in a hot ultra compared to normal?

Plan on going slower, often by 10 to 20 percent or more depending on how hot and humid it is and how acclimated you are. Pace by effort or heart rate instead of your usual splits, and keep the first half so easy it feels almost too easy. The heat makes you pay later, with interest, for anything fast early on.
Can I solo with a chalk bag and a phone just in case?

Carrying a phone won't change the outcome of a fall, which is the real problem with free soloing. If you want a safety net, it has to be a rope, either with a partner or through a properly learned self-belay setup. Keep the chalk bag and phone for an alpine scramble or roped day, and tell someone where you're going regardless.
honestly whats the worst that can happen if i solo something easy at my local crag

The worst that can happen is death, or a spinal injury that changes the rest of your life, and on easy terrain that usually comes from a broken hold, a slip on polish, or a moment of distraction rather than a hard move. Easy routes also tend to have ledges, which make falls more damaging. If you love the crag, set up a toprope or bring a partner and climb laps. You'll get the movement and the fun without betting everything on one hold.
What's the fastest way to cool someone down who collapses from heat on course?

Call for medical help right away, then start cooling immediately without waiting for them to arrive. Cold-water immersion up to the neck is the gold standard if a tub or creek is available. If not, rotate ice-soaked towels over the whole body and fan constantly, keep the head and airway safe, and don't try to force fluids into someone who's confused. With heat stroke, cooling in the first 30 minutes is what makes the biggest difference.
What's the deal with strainers? People keep warning me about them.

A strainer is anything that lets water through but stops solid objects, usually a fallen tree or a pile of branches, and it's one of the deadliest hazards on a river. The current pushes you into it and pins you underwater with enormous force, and even strong swimmers can't fight free. Scout any blind corners, keep a constant eye out for wood, especially after floods, and portage around anything sketchy rather than trying to sneak past. If you're ever swimming toward one, get aggressive and climb up and over it headfirst. Never let yourself get swept underneath.
Can I take a couple of ibuprofen before skiing so my knee doesn't hurt? It's been sore since a fall last week.

I'd hold off. Masking the pain takes away the signal that keeps you from loading a knee that might have a sprain or meniscus problem. Skiing puts big twisting forces through the knee, and those are exactly the forces that turn a minor injury into an ACL or meniscus tear. If it's still sore a week out, especially with swelling, clicking, locking or a feeling of giving way, get it examined before you ski again. A day off now could save your whole season.
My buddy wants to do a cave swim-through at a reef we're diving. We're both Open Water certified. Fine?

A short, wide swim-through where you can see daylight at both ends is generally okay if a guide who knows the site leads it. Anything that goes into an overhead with no direct path to the surface, or that silts out, is cave or cavern territory, and untrained divers die in those every year. If you can't see the exit the whole time, don't go in.
found a used reserve parachute online, 14 years old, never deployed. good deal?

I'd skip it. Most manufacturers put reserve service life at around 10 years, and the fabric and lines degrade with age even if it has never been thrown. Your reserve is the one piece of gear that absolutely has to work, so buy a newer one or have any used reserve inspected and repacked by a qualified rigger before trusting it. Also make sure it's sized for your all-up weight.
How many lessons until I can run class IV?

There's no fixed number. Most people need several seasons of regular paddling, including a reliable combat roll, strong river-reading and rescue skills, before class IV makes sense. A good benchmark is when class III feels relaxed and you're consistently making eddies and catching lines with margin to spare. A swiftwater rescue course is also a smart step before you push into IV.
Weight limit for tandem? I'm 240 lbs and kind of embarrassed to ask.

No need to be embarrassed, because the dropzone asks for safety reasons, not to judge you. Most tandem systems have a combined weight limit, so many dropzones cap passengers somewhere around 220 to 250 lbs depending on their gear and instructors. Call ahead and give them your honest weight, since lying about it can overload the equipment and some places weigh you on arrival anyway.
are bearings with higher ABEC rating faster?

Not really for skateboarding, since ABEC ratings measure precision tolerances that matter more for high speed machinery than for skating. What makes a bearing roll well on a board is that it's clean, lubricated and built tough enough to handle side impacts. Skate-specific bearings like Bones Reds are a solid choice no matter what ABEC number is printed on them.
is 20 meters too high for a first cliff jump lol

Yes, way too high. At 20 meters you hit the water at roughly 70 km/h, and that's high-diving territory where trained athletes land feet-first with tight form. Start around 3 to 5 meters, get your entry clean and consistent, and work up slowly over many sessions.
Got my first real wipeout at 15ft yesterday. Ears are ringing and I'm dizzy. Probably fine right?

Ringing ears and dizziness after a heavy wipeout could mean a ruptured eardrum, inner ear damage or a concussion, so see a doctor today. Keep water out of your ears until you've been checked, because a perforated eardrum can lead to infection. Stay out of the water until a doctor clears you, since dizziness and a second big hold-down are a bad combination.
Do I need to worry about jellyfish?

Mostly they're a nuisance rather than a danger, but some species, like the Portuguese man o' war or box jellyfish in tropical waters, can cause serious reactions. Check local warnings and ask lifeguards before you swim. If you get stung, get out, rinse with seawater rather than fresh water, and carefully remove any tentacles. Get medical help straight away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain or a spreading reaction.
can i hit the halfpipe on my first day in the park

I'd hold off. A halfpipe needs comfortable riding on steep walls, quick edge changes and speed control, and the walls are often icy and unforgiving. Spend your first park days on small jumps, boxes and the flat-bottom areas. If you want to try the pipe, ride the flat bottom and gently up the sides before going near the lip.
theres a huge hill near my house, like really steep with a stop sign at the bottom. best way to bomb it?

Don't bomb a hill that ends at a stop sign, because there's no runout and a car crossing at the wrong moment leaves you nowhere to go. Before you take on anything steep you need solid footbraking and slide stopping on mellow hills, and you need slide gloves, a helmet, and a hill with a safe bottom. Find a gentler hill with a long flat or uphill finish, learn to control your speed there, and work up gradually.
I have high blood pressure but it's controlled with meds. Can I still jump? Really don't want to miss out on this trip.

Talk to your doctor before you book. Bungee puts a sudden strain on your cardiovascular system, and the rebound briefly drives up the pressure in your head and eyes. Many operators list high blood pressure as a condition that needs medical clearance, so you may be asked about it anyway. If your doctor says no, a zipline or a giant swing can give you a similar rush with much less strain.
Ran out of air at 18m on my last dive and shared with my buddy. How do I make sure that never happens again?

Glad you're both okay, and well done handling it. Check your gauge every few minutes and agree on a turn pressure before you descend, something like the rule of thirds or turning at half your tank with enough reserve to reach the surface with 50 bar. Practice sharing air with your buddy in the shallows so it's automatic, and find out why you ran low, whether that was depth, current, stress or just not looking.
My partner freedives and I'm the worried one at home. What should I actually be checking she does?

The big ones are that she never dives alone, and that she dives with a trained buddy who watches every dive from the surface using one up, one down. She should also have proper training, from a recognized agency like AIDA, PADI or Molchanovs. It's reasonable to ask whether she's taken a course and practiced rescues. Those habits are what actually keep freedivers safe, so if she has them, you can worry a bit less.
do I need to break in a new engine or is that a myth

Breaking it in is worth doing. Most manufacturers recommend a short break-in period, like 30 to 60 minutes of varying throttle and gear use without long full-throttle runs, to help the piston rings and parts seat properly. Follow the procedure in your owner's manual, and change the oil afterward to clear out the fine metal particles. It's a little patience that pays off in engine life.
Thinking of running a 15 ft waterfall next month. I've done some 6 footers. Any tips?

Going from 6 to 15 feet is a significant step, because landing forces, the boof, and your lines for a bad landing all get much more serious, so I'd strongly recommend doing your first one with experienced creekers who know that specific drop. Scout it thoroughly, check what's at the bottom for depth, undercuts and recirculating holes, and set safety with throw ropes in place below. Many paddlers build up gradually with 8–10 footers first to dial in their tuck and angle. Taking it slowly isn't timid. It's how people keep doing this for decades.
is it ok to dive with a cold if i take decongestants

It's not a good idea. Decongestants can wear off at depth, which can trap air in your sinuses or middle ear and cause a reverse block on ascent, and that is painful and potentially damaging. Some also cause side effects like drowsiness or a racing heart that you don't want underwater. Wait until you can equalize easily without medication.
can you get frostbite while ice climbing even if you're moving a lot

Yes, especially in your fingers and toes. Gripping tools tightly reduces blood flow to your fingers, tight crampon straps or boots can restrict circulation in your feet, and wet gloves from melting ice pull heat away fast. Watch for numbness, white or waxy skin, or pain that suddenly fades, and warm up as soon as you notice it rather than pushing on. Dress for the conditions, keep spare dry gloves handy, and avoid lacing your boots too tight.
what goggles for open water

Go for goggles with a wider lens than pool racing goggles, since the bigger field of view makes sighting much easier. Tinted or mirrored lenses are best for bright sun, while clear or light lenses suit grey days and murky lakes. Comfort and seal matter most, so try a few pairs on and do a long swim in them well before any event.
My buddy says we can skip the guide because he watched a bunch of YouTube videos on building ice screw anchors. Thoughts?

I'd skip that plan. Anchor building on ice depends on reading ice quality, placement angle, and temperature effects, and you can't judge any of that from a video. A bad anchor fails catastrophically, with no second chance. Book a day or two with a certified guide or take an AMGA-style ice course; your buddy can practice anchors there with someone checking every one.
can i do tricks after a few beers? feel looser lol

Looser, maybe, but your reaction time and judgment both drop, and that's exactly what you need for timing a jump or rail. Alcohol also makes people overconfident about trying bigger features, which is how a fun day turns into an ER visit. Save the beers for après and ride sharp.
My 14 year old son has gotten obsessed with holding his breath in our pool and timing himself. Should I be worried?

Yes, take it seriously, because unsupervised breath-hold training in pools has killed a lot of strong, healthy teenagers, and it usually happens silently with no struggle. Set a firm rule that he never does breath-holds in the water without an adult right there watching him, and never does them after hyperventilating. If he's genuinely into it, a youth-friendly freediving course will teach him to do it properly and channel the interest somewhere safe.
What's the deal with wind loading? I see the term all the time.

Wind picks snow up from the windward side of ridges and drops it on the leeward side, which builds dense wind slabs that can be very reactive. Watch for cornices, rippled or pillowed snow, and slopes that sound hollow or crack underfoot. After strong wind, steer clear of steep lee slopes, especially just below ridgelines, until the slabs have had time to bond.
Can I skip the guideline if the cave passage is a straight shot? Seems pointless.

No, run the line every time. Caves that look straight have side passages, breakdown and silt that can wipe out visibility instantly, and a continuous guideline to open water is the single rule that has saved more cave divers than any other. Losing the line in a blackout is how 'simple' caves kill people.
How do they know how long the cord should be?

The crew calculates it from your exact weight, the jump height and the cord's stretch rating, which is why they weigh you on the day and often write it on your hand. Heavier jumpers stretch the cord further, so they'll adjust the cord or swap to a different one. That weigh-in isn't just paperwork, so give your real weight and don't round down.
Thinking of swimming the English Channel next year. I've done a 5k. Realistic?

It's a big jump from 5k to a 33km swim in cold water that can take 12 hours or more, so a year is ambitious but not impossible if you train seriously. You'll need to build to a six-hour qualifying swim in water under 16°C, and that cold acclimatisation is usually the hardest part. Get a coach with Channel experience, and book an official pilot through the Channel Swimming Association or Federation early, since slots fill years ahead. Many people do a relay or a shorter marathon swim first to see how their body handles it.
just tell me the highest jump in the world, i'm going big for my first one

The Macau Tower at 233 m and the Verzasca Dam in Switzerland at about 220 m are among the famous big ones, and both welcome first-timers under expert supervision. Going big on your first jump is actually common, since every height feels terrifying anyway. Just make sure you're healthy, pick a top-tier operator and budget for the price and possible weather delays.
Tandem paragliding in Nepal, any tips? Pokhara.

Pokhara is one of the world's great tandem spots. Book with an established, licensed operator through your hotel or a reputable agency rather than the cheapest street offer, and confirm the pilot is certified and the gear looks well maintained. Morning flights are usually smoother, and the views of the Annapurna range are clearest early on. Wear closed shoes and bring a layer, since it's cool up there.
Do I really need a continuous guideline to the surface? The cave is only like 30 meters long and the water is super clear.

Yes, every time, because clear water can turn to zero visibility in seconds from a silt-out or a percolating ceiling, and then 30 meters might as well be 3 kilometers. Many fatalities happened in short, clear, familiar caves where divers skipped the line. Run a continuous guideline from open water and keep a hand on it or within reach whenever visibility drops.
I'm on SSRIs for anxiety. Can I do a tandem?

Most people on SSRIs can do a tandem, but check with your prescribing doctor first, because they know your full picture. Mention the medication on the dropzone's medical form too. If your anxiety is managed, a tandem can actually be a great experience, so just make sure the right people know.
Is sidemount better than backmount for caves?

Neither is strictly better; sidemount is great for tight passages and lets you handle each tank separately, while backmount doubles are more stable and many divers find gas management simpler. A lot depends on the caves you'll dive and your own preferences. Try both with a qualified instructor before you spend money on gear.
how do you even steer a street luge

You steer a street luge mostly by leaning, shifting your shoulders and hips into the turn, with small adjustments from your feet and legs. You brake by dragging the soles of your feet on the pavement, which is why riders wear tough boots, often with rubber soles glued on. It takes a lot of low-speed practice before the lean steering feels intuitive, so start on gentle, closed slopes.
Just got my A license! When can I downsize my canopy? Want something zippy.

Congrats. Go slowly, because downsizing too fast is behind a huge share of serious injuries for experienced jumpers. A common rule is to stay at or below a wing loading of about 1.0 until 200 jumps, and to take a canopy course before each downsize. Ask your dropzone's S&TA or a canopy coach to help you pick the next step.
slam dunk question: wrist guards worth it?

Yes, they're probably the single best-value pad for beginners, since wrist fractures are among the most common skateboarding injuries. They work by spreading out the impact when you instinctively put your hands down to catch a fall. Get a pair with a rigid splint on the palm side and make sure they're snug. Lots of experienced skaters still wear them under gloves for exactly this reason.
ok so I passed out briefly at the end of a pool static, buddy got me up, I feel totally fine now. can I keep training today?

No. You're done for the day, even though you feel fine. After a blackout, you need rest, and you should get checked by a doctor if you inhaled any water or have a cough, chest tightness or shortness of breath later on, because a delayed lung problem is possible. Next time, ease off your targets and think through what pushed you over. Your buddy did exactly the right thing, so thank them.
We're going to a crag with my 14 year old. Do kids need helmets outside?

Yes, everyone at an outdoor crag should wear a helmet, including belayers and anyone hanging out at the base, since rockfall and dropped gear are real hazards. For climbers, a helmet also protects against head strikes during falls or flips. Make sure your teen's helmet fits snugly and is certified for climbing.
Just did my first class III run and I'm hooked!! What's the next step?

Congrats, that's a great milestone. Build consistency next by running that grade a lot, nailing a reliable combat roll, and catching eddies and ferrying well. A swiftwater rescue course is a smart next investment, and joining a local paddling club will get you good partners and mentorship for stepping up safely.
honestly whats the most common mistake people make on high peaks

Ascending too fast and ignoring the early signs of altitude sickness is the big one. Close behind is summit fever, where people keep pushing past a safe turnaround time because they're so close to the top. Respecting the acclimatization schedule and setting turnaround times before summit day are the two habits that prevent the most disasters.
Is it safe to dive headfirst off a cliff if I'm a good pool diver?

Pool diving skills help, but headfirst entries off cliffs are where most spinal injuries happen, because you can't see hidden rocks, sandbars or how deep the water really is. Unless you've personally checked the depth and you're jumping from a modest height into water that's clearly deep, go feet first. Headfirst cliff diving is something people train for specifically, often with coaches, and it's worth treating it that way.
what's the deal with swim buoys, are they actually useful or just for show

They're genuinely useful, mainly because they make you visible. A bright orange buoy is much easier for boats, lifeguards and friends to spot than a head in choppy water. You can also hold onto one for a short rest, although it isn't a certified lifesaving device, so don't rely on it if you're in real trouble. For the price, it's one of the best safety buys in open water swimming.
Lines on my wing look a bit fuzzy in spots. Do I need to worry?

Yes, get them checked. Fuzzy or frayed lines can mean wear, abrasion or UV damage, and a weak line can snap or change the wing's trim, which affects how it flies and how it recovers from collapses. Take it to a qualified service shop for a line check and trim measurement, ideally before your next flight. Most wings should get a full check every 100 hours or every one to two years anyway.
is it dumb to go in the park alone

It's not dumb, but it's riskier. If you slam hard, nobody might see you for a while, especially on a quiet day. Tell someone where you are, stick to features you're already comfortable on when you're solo, and save new or bigger tricks for when you're riding with a friend.
rate the danger 1 to 10, 20 meter jump, first time

For a first-timer, that's a 9 or 10. At 20 meters you're hitting the water at about 70 km/h, and without trained body control, even a slight tilt can mean broken bones, a concussion or spinal injury. Start at 3 to 5 meters and build up over many sessions, ideally with coaching if you want to work toward that height someday.
honestly whats the death rate for wingsuit flying

It depends heavily on which kind you mean. Wingsuit skydiving from planes is relatively safe for trained, current jumpers, with risk only a bit higher than regular skydiving. Wingsuit BASE and especially proximity flying are far more dangerous and have killed many very experienced people. The step from open-sky flying to flying near cliffs and terrain is where most of the risk lives.
wanna try a backflip on my crf250 after watching freestyle vids. tips?

Don't try backflips on your own on a dirt jump. Freestyle riders learn them into foam pits or resi ramps with coaching, a purpose-built takeoff and a lot of training, and a short rotation can cause catastrophic spinal injuries. If you're serious, look for a freestyle motocross training facility with foam pits or airbag landings. Until then, build your skills with whips, scrubs and bigger jumps on a proper track.
tired of wearing a wetsuit, it's 12 degrees, just going skins for my usual 3k

At 12°C, jumping straight from a wetsuit to a skins 3k is asking for trouble, because you can lose heat a lot faster than you think and hypothermia creeps up on you. Build up to it. Do short skins swims of 10 to 20 minutes and lengthen them gradually over a few weeks, keeping close to shore or near a support kayak. Watch for slurred speech, claw hands or shivering that won't stop, and get out at the first sign.
lol can i use my shortboard in 12 foot waves

You can try, but you'll struggle to paddle into anything and end up getting caught inside a lot. In 12 foot surf you want a step-up or small gun with more length and volume for paddle speed and early entry. That extra size makes the drop and your positioning much safer.
gonna try my first wingsuit jump solo this weekend, already watched a bunch of tutorials. tips?

My biggest tip is don't do it solo. Do your first flight with a certified coach on a proper first flight course. A coach will brief your exit, flight path and deployment, check your gear, and fly near you or at least debrief you after. If you're current and have your 200 jumps, a course can often be done in a weekend anyway, so you lose nothing by doing it right.
inflatable vest worth it or just extra drag

It's worth it, and the drag is minimal compared to what it gives you. Modern inflation vests like the Patagonia or Billabong V2 can pull you to the surface fast after a long hold-down, and that's why nearly every serious big-wave surfer wears one. Learn exactly how to deploy it, service the CO2 cartridges regularly, and remember it's a backup that doesn't replace fitness, breath-hold training, or a safety team.
Is it fine to run Badwater-type heat with no crew?

For extreme heat races like Badwater, a crew isn't optional, and the race itself requires one for good reason. In 120F conditions you need constant ice, fluids, cooling and someone watching for mental changes you won't notice yourself. Solo extreme-heat running is how people die in places like Death Valley. Build up through hot races with aid stations before attempting anything that remote.
I'm diabetic (type 1). Any special concerns for a hot 50K?

Yes, a few. Heat speeds up insulin absorption and can mask hypo symptoms, and dehydration skews your readings, so a CGM and frequent checks are really valuable. Work out a race plan with your endocrinologist, including basal adjustments, and run a few long hot training runs to see how your levels behave. Carry glucose and let the race medics know your condition.
Can I belay with a grigri without learning ATC first? Gym says I need a belay test either way

Yes, plenty of people learn on a GriGri first, and your gym's test is the right gatekeeper. Remember it's assisted-braking, not auto-locking, so your brake hand stays on the rope at all times. Many accidents happen when people hold the cam open to lower or pay out. Get taught the proper lowering technique and practice it until it's automatic.
im 58 and kinda overweight, is paragliding even an option for me

Absolutely. Plenty of people start in their 50s and 60s, and wings are rated for a wide range of pilot weights, so there's gear for you. The demanding part is ground handling and running on launch, so decent knees and some basic cardio will make training much more enjoyable. Get a quick check-up with your doctor first, especially if you have heart or joint issues, then book a tandem flight to see how it feels.
I'm 15 and my friends want to go climbing at a quarry without ropes. Is it ok if we stay low?

Quarries are risky even low down. The rock is often loose, landings are full of rubble, and sometimes there's deep cold water nearby. If you want to boulder outdoors, go to an established bouldering area with crash pads, or better still, start at a climbing gym. Many gyms have teen sessions where you'll actually learn the skills to do this safely.
Dive computer died on day two of a trip. Can I just follow my buddy's computer?

It's tempting, but your buddy's computer tracks their profile, not yours, and even small depth differences add up across repeat dives. The right move is to rent or borrow a computer and sit out a dive or wait about 24 hours so the new one starts with a clean slate. Many shops have spares, so ask before you skip a whole day.
I'm 52 and want to start whitewater kayaking. Is that crazy?

Not crazy at all; plenty of people start in their 50s and paddle for decades. Take a beginner course from a certified instructor, because learning the roll, wet exits and river reading properly from the start makes everything safer and more fun. If you have any heart, shoulder or back issues, it's worth a quick check with your doctor first, since the sport involves cold-water shock and some explosive effort.
Surfing waves bigger than you're ready for is the best way to get good fast, right?

That's the fastest way to get badly hurt or scared out of the sport, not the fastest way to improve. Big-wave surfers build skill by stepping up gradually, so their reading of the ocean, fitness and breath-hold keep pace with the size. Push your comfort zone a little at a time with good crew around, and you'll be charging bigger waves sooner and much more safely.
teen here, my mates jump off the harbour wall into the sea every summer. it's like 6m. safe?

Tombstoning like that injures people every summer, mostly because the depth changes with the tide and there can be rocks or debris you can't see. The cold can also make you gasp as you hit the water. If you're set on jumping, check the depth at that exact spot and time of day, never jump at low tide, never go headfirst, and make sure someone's watching with a phone. Better still, find a supervised coasteering session where instructors pick safe jump spots for you.
any supplements to boost heat tolerance? looking for a shortcut

Nothing in a bottle beats real acclimation. A couple of weeks of heat exposure does more than any pill. Some runners use sodium loading before the race, which can help a little, but there's no shortcut, and stimulant-heavy products actually raise heat risk. Spend your energy on saunas and smart pacing instead.
Can I do wingsuit BASE without skydiving first? I've got a BASE course booked.

No reputable path to wingsuit BASE skips skydiving. The standard progression is a solid skydiving background, then plenty of wingsuit skydives, then regular BASE experience, and only then wingsuit BASE. Jumping a suit off an object with no wingsuit background would be extremely dangerous, so talk to your BASE course provider about where you actually stand.
Is it OK to ride after a couple beers? Just chill trail riding

Skip the beers until after you're done riding. Even small amounts of alcohol slow reaction time and affect balance and judgment, which matter a lot on a dirt bike even on easy trails. Many crashes happen on routes people consider simple, and alcohol can make injuries worse. Enjoy the drinks back at camp when the bikes are parked.
I froze on my last BASE exit and almost went anyway. Should I keep jumping?

Freezing is your brain telling you something, and not going was the right call. Jumping while you're hesitant leads to poor exits and unstable delays, which cause most off-heading problems. Talk it through with your mentor, figure out what was bothering you (conditions, the object, your gear, or just your head that day), and go back to easy objects until you feel confident again. Taking time off is always better than forcing an exit.
Pregnant, 12 weeks, still bouldering. Should I stop?

Many people switch to top-rope climbing during pregnancy, because bouldering falls and impacts become riskier as the pregnancy progresses. A full-body or maternity harness helps later on as your belly grows. Check with your OB or midwife about your specific situation and listen closely to how your body feels.
Got a headache and nausea about an hour after my dive. probably just dehydration right?

It might be, but don't assume. Headache and nausea after a dive can be early decompression sickness or carbon monoxide from a bad air fill. Breathe 100% oxygen if the dive center has it, lie down, drink water, and call DAN's emergency hotline or a local hyperbaric center for advice now. If you have numbness, weakness, confusion or trouble breathing, treat it as an emergency and get to medical help immediately.
carving vs pushing to go faster, what's better

Pushing is the main way to gain speed on flat ground. Push with long smooth strokes from your back foot while keeping your front foot facing forward over the bolts. Pumping is what generates speed in bowls and on pump tracks, and the turns in it come from shifting your weight. On flat ground carving mostly controls speed rather than adding it.
